45: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits X and Y in a cage (reading left to right) form a pair of coordinates that point to Row X, Column Y (rXcY). The digit at rXcY is determined as follows: 1. If X or Y is in the entropic set: {1,2,3}, it represents the base-3 digit 0; {4,5,6}, it represents the base-3 digit 1; {7,8,9}, it represents the base-3 digit 2. 2. The entropic base-3 representations of X and Y now form a 2-digit base-3 number (reading left to right still). 3. Convert this number back to base-10, and place this digit at rXcY. No two cage coordinates point to the same cell. Digits do not repeat along the negative diagonal (blue line). Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Adjacent digits on an orange line differ by at least 4. If a cage has a small number in the top left, the digits in that cage sum to that number. Digits either side of a white dot are consecutive. On a black dot, one digit is double the other. Digits either side of an X sum to 10. Digits either side of a V sum to 5. A digit on a grey square is even.

Chose two colours with which to colour each cell in the grid such that all cells of either colour are orthogonally connected to each other, and no 2x2 area may be entirely one colour. 63: Note that to solve this puzzle from scratch you first have to determine which of the characters in the maze is telling the truth and which is lying. Matt's team found this part of the puzzle straightforward so he tasked us with the sudoku part ie revealing who the truth-tellers were at around 12minutes into the video). If you want to solve the WHOLE puzzle then you will need to deduce the liars/honest characters from the text below: Normal sudoku rules may apply. You find yourself in a maze of regions connected by doors. Each region is made of rooms connected by passageways. You encounter some helpful people along your travels through the rooms. Here's what they have to say: Stephanie: Some rules apply to the whole maze. Others apply to regions. Some people tell only lies. Some only tell the truth. All true statements about region specific rules apply to different regions. Daniel: Everyone lies all the time. In particular Stephanie lies all the time. Only listen to me. I'm pretty sure Stephanie didn't even tell you the truth about what you're supposed to do here. Some rooms contain a digit from 1-8 while others are empty. Rooms in the same column or row containing the same digit must be further apart than the value of that digit. Rooms containing the same digit can not touch diagonally. Maurice is a liar. Maurice: All rooms contain a digit from 1-9 such that no digit is repeated in a row, column, or region. Only one digit is still visible, a five. In fact, once you know the rules of the regions you will be able to immediately place 2 more fives in the grid. Please help us find all the missing digits. Patrick: Maurice and Helen are both telling the truth. There is a region with a single door to the West in which orthogonally connected rooms not separated by a wall must contain digits at least 4 apart. There is a region in which orthogonally connected rooms not separated by a wall must contain digits that differ by a power of 2. There is a region in which orthogonally connected rooms not separated by a wall must contain digits that are non-consecutive. Caroline: In one region with only 2 doors the largest and smallest digits on the shortest path between the doors are next to the doors. In another region with only 2 doors the digits on the shortest path between the doors strictly increase from one door to the other. In yet another region with only 2 doors along the shortest path between the doors the digit next to one of the doors is equal to the sum of the remaining digits. By the way, Annabelle is a liar. Vladimir: Patrick is a liar. There is a region with a single door to the South in which all numbers formed by reading the digits from North to South or West to East from wall to wall (or door) are perfect squares. Another region read this way contains prime numbers. A third region read this way contains multiples of 7. Helen: Exactly one of Jessica and Annabelle is a liar. One region of the maze is an exact clone of another, but may be rotated. Annabelle: In one region with only 2 doors the digits on the shortest path between the doors alternate between odd and even. In another region with only 2 doors the digits on the shortest path between the doors form a prime number when read in one direction. In yet another region with only 2 doors the product of the digits on the shortest path between doors is a perfect square. By the way, Caroline is a liar. Jessica: There are either 3 or 4 liars here. There is a region with a single door to the North in which orthogonally connected rooms not separated by a wall must not both contain prime numbers. There is another region with a single door to the East in which orthogonally connected rooms not separated by a wall contain digits that either have a difference of 1 or one is double the other (or both!)
67: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each unique clue type listed below cannot contain more than one instance of each of the digits 1-9. Clue types: a) Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive; b) digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio, ie. one digit is double the other; c) digits in cages sum to the total in the upper left corner, if given; d) digits on a pink line form a set of consecutive digits IN ORDER. Eg 123 and 321 are valid length-3 lines but 132 is not; e) digits outside the grid give the sum of the digits on the diagonal pointed to by the arrow; f) each segment on a blue line sums to the same total. Box borders separate a line into segments. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digit in a cell may reveal some of the fog, possibly revealing more clues.
68: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. Region borders divide a blue line into segments. Each segment sums to the same total.
70: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. Digits on a grey thermometer must increase from the bulb to the tip.
74: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 3. If two digits are either side of a V, the V ‘points’ to the smaller digit.
75: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. Digits in a cage do not repeat, and sum to the small number in the top left corner of the cage.
76: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. A digit in a grey cell with arrows pointing outwards is greater than all cells orthogonally adjacent. If two digits are separated by a V, the V ‘points’ to the smaller digit.
77: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the circle attached to that arrow.
94: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.
95: Fill in the grid with digits, which cannot repeat in any row, column or marked 3x3 box. The digits inside the large circles must appear in the cells that they touch. IN ADDITION, the circles function diagonally as ‘black kropki dots’, i.e. when two digits are separated diagonally by a large circle, one of them is two times the other. Small white dots separate consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are shown.
338: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 5 in the grid must have a 1 directly above it or a 9 directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both. A camel’s move in fairy chess is a jump of three squares horizontally and one square vertically or three squares vertically and one square horizontally. Any cell a camel’s move away from a camel cell has to contain a digit that is either consecutive or in a 2:1 ratio with the digit in the camel cell. There are exactly seven camel cells in the grid. Two of them are shown; the others are hidden. All the hidden camels are in odd-numbered boxes and contain the digit of the box that they live in. The 3x3 boxes are numbered in normal reading order.
437: I’m sorry, the rules seem to have been invaded by pickles. I hope you can still make pickle of them. Normal pickle rules apply. Two adjacent pickles on a pickle line have a difference of at least 5. Pickles separated by a light pickle dot are consecutive. Pickles separated by a dark pickle dot are in a 2:1 pickle. Not all pickles are necessarily shown. Have pickle!
1508: Oh, no! The Wicked Witch Lorena has cursed you with forgetting all numbers! Fortunately for you, the International Accord on Curses, Hexes and Jinxes of 1692 forbids unbreakable curses so, like it or not, she must ensure that there is a way to get out of it. It’s the law! But that doesn’t mean she has to make it easy. Cruel as she is, she has determined that the only way for you to fully break the curse will be to solve this sudoku. Luckily, as the fog lifts in your mind, the numbers will gradually start to come back to you. Once a given digit appears in the grid for the first time, you may use it to fill in cells. If a digit hasn’t yet made an appearance, you are not allowed to use it (pencilmarks are okay). Placing a correct digit may or may not remove fog anywhere in the grid. Digits cannot repeat in any row, column or marked 3x3 box. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a 2:1 ratio (i.e. one of the digits must be double the other). Grey palindrome lines must read the same in both directions. Adjacent digits in a green German whispers line must differ by at least 5. Breaking these rules or trying to guess digits at random to clear the fog might end up with you being turned into a frog, so consider yourself warned. Note: Yes, you remember the concept of numbers, so you can understand the rules. You’re still not allowed to use them until you see them in the grid. Nice try, though.
2102: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a purple line may not repeat and form a consecutive set, but may be in any order. Digits connected by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.
2108: Fill each cell with a single digit and draw a “train” that covers every cell in the grid. The train consists of 4 carriages of equal length and each carriage is formed of an orthogonal path of cells. A carriage doesn't touch itself, not even diagonally. Adjacent digits along a carriage are consecutive. An X connects the end cells of two carriages, which sum to 10. The black fly connects two digits with a 1:2 ratio. Identical digits may not touch each other orthogonally. A digit on the train indicates how many times that digit appears on the train.
2109: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the circle. Digits separated by a white dot have a difference of one while digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots are given.
2110: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a grey thermometer must increase from the bulb end. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5.
2111: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide blue lines into segments with equal sums. Cells separated by a black dot are in the ratio 1 to 2. All possible black dots are given.
2112: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells. Digits along a line sum to the product of the digits in the squares at either end of the line (if it is the same square, multiply that digit by itself). Digits may repeat on a line if permitted by the other rules. Lines do not branch or cross, but they may share squares with other lines.
2113: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid contains a set of non-overlapping cages with the same sum. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. The cages are partially invisible.
2114: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum.
2115: Normal sudoku rules apply. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. TELEPORTS: Entering a yellow teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the other teleport. From there she can continue her journey. The teleports contain the same digit. BLACKCURRANTS: Cells connected by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Not all possible blackcurrants have been given. CAGES: Digits don't repeat in a cage. Every cage has the same total, which is to be deduced. The digit on a cage's electricity symbol is its 'shock value'. Any cage with a shock value of 5 or more is switched on, and Finkz should not enter these for safety reasons. Cages with a shock value lower than 5 are switched off and therefore safe to enter. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, the correct path will be a valid Chinese Whisper line, ie; adjacent digits along the path must differ by at most 2.
2116: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a pink “renban” line form a consecutive sequence in any order. Cages mark “Vaults” in which digits MAY repeat, but must sum to the total, if given. Digits orthogonally adjacent to a vault may NOT be included within that vault.
2117: Normal sudoku rules apply. The dashed lines are part of non-overlapping rectangular cages hidden in the grid. Digits in a cage do not repeat, and sum to the number represented by one or more cells in its upper left corner (read from left to right). Eg If a cage summed to 27, its upper leftmost cell would have a 2, with a 7 to its right.
2118: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of digits along a line between two circles is equal to the sum of the digits in those two circles. An X in the center of a 2x2 region of cells, a “product square,” indicates that the two digits in the square’s positive diagonal have the same product as the two digits in its negative diagonal. The product is not necessarily the same for different product squares. Not all product squares are necessarily indicated.
2119: Normal sudoku rules apply. Correctly placed digits clear the fog around them. The grid contains exactly fifteen cages that do not overlap and each cage occupies two or more cells. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Not all cage sums are given but sums that are given are located in the left-most cell in the highest row reached by the cage. Two cages of the same size cannot have the same sum (regardless of whether either cage's sum is given). Digits in cells with a shaded circle must be odd. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.
2120: Divide the four lines in the grid into two pairs. The lines in a pair are copycats of each other, i.e. they have the same composition of digits. E.g. if one line has two 3s, five 4s and a 9, then the other one also has two 3s, five 4s and a 9. The order of the digits is not necessarily the same on the two lines. The two lines in the grid with a circle on one end are an average arrow and a thermometer. The two lines without a circle are a region sum line and a german whispers line. The solver has to deduce which line obeys which rule. Average Arrow: The digit in the circle is the average (exact, not rounded) of the digits on the line. Thermometer: The digits have to increase along the thermometer, starting from its bulb. Region Sum Line: The line is cut into multiple segments by the box borders, each summing to the same number. German Whisper: Two neighboring digits have a difference of 5 or more.
2121: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
2122: Shade some cells such that all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and there may not exist a run of four or more consecutive shaded or unshaded cells horizontally or vertically anywhere in the grid. Furthermore, each cell containing a number must not be shaded, and the number in the cell represents the total count of shaded cells in orthogonally connected groups sharing an edge with that number. A '?' indicates a single digit number. A '??' indicates a double digit number. (The solution check function will work if you enter an ‘S’ into every shaded cell and a ‘U’ into every unshaded cell in the finished grid.)
2123: Normal sudoku rules apply; but, every clue is wrogn. Any clue that fully obeys one of the following rules is not wrogn. Ambiguous Thermos: Digits along a gray line must strictly increase from one end to the other. Ascending Starters: A clue outside the grid applies to the sum of the first run of ascending digits from the position of the clue (i.e. the sum from the first digit encountered until digits are no longer ascending). This may be only a single digit. Entropic Lines: Along a peach line, every group of three consecutive cells must contain one low {1,2,3}, one medium {4,5,6}, and one high {7,8,9} digit. Killer: Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the given total. Modular Lines: Along a teal line, every run of three digits must all have different remainders under division by 3. Nabner: No two cells on a yellow line may contain either the same digit or consecutive digits. Parity Lines: Along a red line, adjacent digits may not have the same parity. Renban: Digits along a purple line form a non-repeating consecutive set. Quadruples: Every digit in a circle must appear at least once in the surrounding four cells.
2124: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. The maze has been filled with fog. When correct digits are entered, the nearby fog will clear. No guessing is required. Digits connected by a blackcurrant are in a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Not all possible blackcurrants have been given. The digit on a pink motion sensor indicates how many of the (up to 9) cells immediately surrounding the sensor are visited by Finkz - ie; any cells neighbouring the sensor cell (diagonally or orthogonally), as well as the sensor cell itself, are counted, if they lie on the path. Digits don't repeat in a cage. Every cage has an electricity symbol, which indicates its 'shock value'. Any cage with a shock value of 5 or higher should not be entered by Finkz. Cages with a shock value lower than 5 are safe to enter. In this experiment, the first cage that Finkz enters could have any total. After that, each subsequent cage she enters must have a total exactly one greater than the previous cage she entered. Cages not entered by Finkz can have any total.
2125: Normal sudoku rules apply. The circles contain a complete set of the digits from 1 to 9. In other words, no two circles may contain identical digits. Pea Lines: The sum of the digits on a line strictly between two circles is equal to a concatenation of the two values in the circles, in some order. For instance, 3_346_1 could be a valid split pea line, as 3+4+6=13, which is 1 concatenated with 3.
2126: Place the digits 1 to 9 once each into the 3x3 boxes. Digits may not repeat in the same row, column, or box of the 6x6 grid. Each of the two marked diagonals contains only 3 distinct digits. Digits along an arrow must sum to the value in that arrow's circle. Digits in cages must not repeat, and sum to the small number in the top left corner of the cage.
2127: Shade some cells in the grid such that all unshaded cells (the inside of the ‘cave’) are orthogonally connected to each other and all shaded cells (the walls) are orthogonally connected to the edge of the grid. Clue cells are unshaded and indicate the number of unshaded cells seen in the four orthogonal directions from that cell, including itself. Shaded cells obstruct vision. The cave and each wall section is a separate region for the purposes of a ‘LITS puzzle’. In a LITS puzzle, solvers must place one tetromino into each region. No two tetrominoes of the same shape may share an edge - reflections/rotations count as the same shape. All tetrominoes must form a single orthogonally connected area. No 2x2 area of the grid can be completely covered in tetrominoes. For the solution check function to work, having completed the puzzle, solvers should enter a 3 into every cell filled with a tetromino; a 2 into every non-tetromino shaded cell; and a 1 into every non-tetromino unshaded cell.
2128: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages do not repeat, and sum to the total, if given. Digits orthogonally adjacent to a cage may NOT be included in that cage. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.
2129: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments. Along a line, each segment’s digits sum to the same total. Different lines may have different sums for their segments.
2135: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1 to 6, once each, into each row, column and rectangular box). One cell in each row, column, and box is a ‘doubler’, and each digit is doubled once. Digits do not repeat in cages. Each cage sums to a different total (with doubled digits counting as twice their value) and the totals are ranked in order from lowest (1) to highest (6). The number in the top left of the cage, if given, indicates this rank.
2136: Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells. Each cell should contain a number equal to the size of its region (i.e. the number of cells in its region). Each number from 1 to 9 must be present in the grid. Cells adjacent to each other can't be consecutive (not even diagonally). Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits with a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other).
2137: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. White dots join consecutive digits, the black dot digits in a 1:2 ratio. A red cell shows the position of their cell's column number in that row, e. g. a 3 in R2C1 would put a 1 in R2C3.
2138: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (ie place the digits 1-6, once each, into every row, column and box.) Draw 6 lines, each with a different turquoise spot at both ends. Each line must occupy at least 3 cells, and may move orthogonally and diagonally. Lines may not branch, cross each other, or share cells. Each line is a 'same difference' line ie Every pair of adjacent cells along a line has the same difference - this is its 'difference value.' Every line has a different 'difference value'. Digits in a cage sum to the total given in the cage’s top left corner.
2139: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end.
2145: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digit in the circle is the exact average of the digits on the golden line. (eg r5c4 is the exact average of the digits in r5c4, r5c5 & r5c6). The digits along each grey line must sum to 10. The four cells surrounding the small white circle in box 6 must contain consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order.
2146: Normal sudoku rules apply. The Hare and the Tortoise must race in orthogonal or diagonal steps, and must not enter ponds, or cross or overlap each other or themselves, apart from at the finish line, where both their paths end. The Hare must enter every 3x3 box exactly once each (including box 9 - starting in box 9 does NOT count as entering it). The Hare's racing line will be a valid “Fast Thermo” - ie. digits along it increase by at least 3 at a time, but the Hare has a nap at every box border and the Thermo may begin again on any digit in the next cell. The Tortoise's racing line will be a valid Slow Thermo - ie. digits along it may not decrease. The Fox declares the winner by displaying a digit that does NOT appear on the winner's racing line. Digits separated by the Duck sum to 5.
2147: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column and region. The grid is mostly covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. No guessing is required. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Arrows may only move orthogonally and don't share cells with other arrows.
2148: Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally-connected cells. Every row, column, and region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Digits along a pink line form a non-repeating consecutive set, but may be written in any order. A cell with a number in its top-left corner is a “Chess Sums” cell. The number in the top-left corner indicates the amount of Chess Sums satisfied by the digit in that cell. A digit in a Chess Sums cell gives one or more of the following: • The sum of all digits that share its region and are a king’s move away • The sum of all digits that share its region and are a knight’s move away • The sum of all digits that share its region and are a bishop’s move away
2149: Draw a snake (a 1 cell-wide path) in the grid whose head and tail are given by circled cells. The snake can touch itself diagonally, but cannot touch itself orthogonally or revisit any square. Besides the snake, the remaining cells must form exactly nine white areas, one of each size from 1 to 9. Numbers in the grid must be part of white areas of the indicated size. (For the solution check function to work, place a digit into each white cell equal to the size of its region.)
2150: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-6, once each, into every row, column and 2x3 rectangle). Shade every cell one of two colours such that each colour forms a single orthogonally connected area and no 2x2 area is entirely one colour. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the digits in the first continuous run of same-coloured cells along marked diagonals. The grid is toroidal; i.e. each edge of the grid is considered to be adjacent/orthogonal to its opposite edge. For example, the 2nd cell pointed at by the 22 diagonal clue is r2c1 (and, for the avoidance of doubt, this cell is orthogonally adjacent to r2c6).
2151: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into 3 zones. Each zone consists of a single group of orthogonally connected cells. No 2x2 area may be entirely within one zone. The first zone is 'too hot'. Any cell in the hot zone has a value one greater than its digit. The second zone is 'too cold'. Any cell in the cold zone has a value one less than its digit. The third zone is 'just right'; this is the Goldilocks Zone. In this zone, a cell's value equals its digit, like normal. The 9 objects (bowls, chairs and beds) all contain different digits, but each object of the same type has the same value. Zone borders (NOT box borders) divide blue lines into segments, each of which has the same total (ie; the total being the sum of that segment’s VALUES.) The two ends of a blue line always lie in different zones.
2152: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The grey line in the grid is a palindrome (ie the string of digits along the line must read the same forwards and backwards.)
2153: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits connected by a black dot have a 2:1 ratio. Digits connected by a white dot are consecutive. Cells separated by a chess king’s move cannot contain the same digit. Cells separated by a chess queen’s move cannot contain the same digit, but this rule applies only to digits 3, 6 and 9. Any three consecutive digits along a peach line must include a digit from the set (1, 2, 3), a digit from the set (4, 5, 6) and a digit from the set (7, 8, 9). All peach lines of length three MUST contain the digits 3, 6 and 9 in some order.
2159: The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog, possibly revealing more clues. No guessing is required. Each row, column, and region contains the digits 1–9 exactly once each. A region is an orthogonally connected collection of cells, and regions are to be determined. The digit in a cell containing an arrow indicates the number of region borders in that direction. (If there is more than one arrow, the number of borders is the same in each direction eg a 4 in the cell with two arrows pointing East and North would indicate that there were 4 borders to the East AND 4 borders to the North). The outer edges of the grid do not count as borders. A digit in a circle equals the total number of cells seen horizontally and vertically that are in the same region as the digit, including itself. Borders obstruct vision.
2160: In each N-by-N grid, normal N-by-N sudoku rules apply. The indicated diagonals have the same sum.
2161: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each purple line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, which can appear in any order. Using red, green, and blue, colour in all circles such that: -Orthogonally adjacent circles are different colours. -Circles on the same purple line are the same colour. -The digit inside a circle appears that many times in circles of that colour.
2162: Divide the grid into 12 regions, one of each size 1 to 12. Black cells are not in regions. A region may not contain repeated numbers, and it may only contain factors of its size (e.g. a region of size 6 may contain any combination of 1,2,3, and 6, including none of them). In this puzzle, enter a number into each cell with an arrow (other cells remain empty). That number must equal the number of cells belonging to its own region seen in a straight line in the corresponding direction (not counting itself) before the first cell outside the region (or the edge of the grid). (For the solution check function to work, in addition to entering the numbers on arrows, enter a 0 in the region of size 1.)
2163: Normal sudoku rules apply in both grids. In each grid, the circles contain a complete set of the digits 1-9. For each pair of circles in the same position in both grids, the digit is the same. In one of the grids, the value of the cell is double the value of the digit. In the other grid, the value is unchanged. The doublers are not necessarily all in the same grid. It is up to the solver to determine in which grid each digit is doubled. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. The values of the cells in a cage must sum to the small clue, if given. Even if the cage total is not given, two cages in the same position in the two grids must contain values summing to the same total.
2164: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. (No guessing is required.) Any combination of one or more digits within a cage CANNOT sum to the small value given in the cage’s top left corner. Digits may not repeat in a cage. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots are given.
2165: Fill every cell with a digit from 1-8 such that digits do not repeat in a row, column or 4x2 box. There are eight boxes, which overlap at dashed lines, and some boxes wrap around the grid, which is a torus. For example, r1c6 and r4c2 share a box. Adjacent digits on the orange line must differ by at least 4. Digits separated by a V must sum to 5.
2166: 1-8 must be placed in each row, column, and 4x2 box. Every digit is "married" to exactly one other, and married couples share their values, eg. if 3 and 7 are married, then every instance of the digits 3 and 7 in the grid has a value of (3+7), which is 10. The VALUES in a cage must sum to either 37, 26 or 9. Digits and/or values may repeat in a cage. DIGITS separated by a heart are consecutive. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) may not contain the same DIGIT.
2167: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into two galaxies. Every cell in the grid belongs to one of the two galaxies. Each galaxy must consist of a region of orthogonally connected cells, and must have 180 degree rotational symmetry. (The central point around which a galaxy is symmetrical doesn't need to actually belong to that galaxy.) No 2x2 area may belong entirely to one galaxy. One of the two galaxies behaves like a German whisper; orthogonally adjacent cells in this galaxy must have a difference of at least 5. An arrow cell counts how many cells in its own galaxy are being pointed at altogether by its arrow(s), and this combined total is displayed on the arrow cell (the arrow cell itself is not included in the count.) Vision is not obscured by the other galaxy's cells.
2168: Part 1: Normal Fillomino rules apply (see below). Part 2: Normal LITS rules apply (with the created regions from the Fillomino). Part 3: Normal Star Battle rules apply (with the created unshaded regions from the LITS (NOT the Fillomino regions)). Each Part may (if solved independently) have more than one solution but only one grid fill will satisfy all three Parts together. Fillomino rules: Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells. Each cell should contain a number equal to the size of its region (ie the number of cells in its region). The size of any region must not be the same of an orthogonally adjacent region. LITS rules: Place one tetromino into each region. No two tetrominoes of the same shape may share an edge - reflections/rotations count as the same shape. All tetrominoes must form a single orthogonally connected area. No 2x2 area of the grid can be completely covered in tetrominoes. Star Battle rules: Place 1 star in each row/column/region such that no two stars touch each other, even diagonally. For the solution check function to operate, place a 1 in every cell of the final grid that contains a star (and leave other cells empty).
2169: Normal sudoku rules apply. Within a 3x3 box, orthogonally connected cells must have a difference of at least 3. Place an arrow in the grid with its (single cell) circle in box 1 (the top left 3x3 box of the grid), with a straight shaft and the tip of its shaft in box 9 (the bottom right 3x3 box). The circle plus the shaft is eight cells long. Digits on the shaft sum to the digit in the circle of that arrow.
2170: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is mostly covered in fog; placing a correct digit removes fog in surrounding cells. No guessing is required. A red "X" indicates a product square: a 2x2 region of cells where the product of the digits on the negative diagonal equals the product of the digits on the positive diagonal. A blue "X" indicates a sum square: a 2x2 region of cells where the sum of the digits on the negative diagonal equals the sum of the digits on the positive diagonal. Digits in cells separated by a white dot must be consecutive. No rule is subject to a negative constraint.
2171: Normal sudoku rules apply. Pea lines: The sum of the digits on a line strictly between two circles is equal to a concatenation of the two values in the circles, in some order. For instance, 3_346_1 could be a valid split pea line, as 3+4+6=13, which is 1 concatenated with 3. Zipper lines: Cells on a lavender line at an equal distance to the centre, which is marked with a dot, sum to the digit at the centre. (Note: The circles of pea lines are NOT part of the zipper lines. Ie the pea lines are green and lavender but the zipper lines are only the lavender parts.)
2172: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may touch itself diagonally, but not orthogonally. Adjacent digits on the loop differ by 5 or more. The 3x3 box borders divide the loop into segments. Circles are on the loop and their digits count the number of cells in their segments.
2173: Normal sudoku rules apply. There is exactly one Doubler cell in every row, column, and 3x3 box. These cells contain a full set of the digits 1-9 and do not overlap with the Body Snatcher cells. A Doubler cell's value is twice the value of the digit in that cell. There is exactly one Body Snatcher cell in every row, column, and 3x3 box. These cells contain a full set of the digits 1-9 and do not overlap with the Doubler cells. Body snatcher cells count as exactly one higher, or one lower than the value of one of the cells they are orthogonally adjacent to and that cell must be in the same box as the Body Snatcher it's parasited by. Each purple line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating values, which can appear in any order. Digits can repeat on a purple line as long as no value ends up repeated on the line.
2174: Place 1-6 in each row, column and 3x2 box. Each clue is an X-sum, a sandwich clue, and a little killer clue. Thus: it is the sum of the first X numbers it sees in its column where X is the first such digit. It is also the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 6 in its column, and the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.
2175: Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells, and place the region size in each cell of those regions. Regions of the same size can't share an edge. Clues outside the grid contain the sum of the first X numbers from the direction of the clue, where X is the first number seen by the clue.
2176: Normal sudoku rules apply. Starting in a corner, along the grey stairs the difference between the first pair of digits is at least 2, the next pair at least 3, then at least 4 etc. Moreover the first and last digits are equal.
2177: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identify 9 Balance Cells in the grid such that there is one Balance Cell in every row, column, and 3x3 box. Each Balance Cell must contain a different digit. The value of a Balance Cell is the arithmetic mean of the up to 4 digits orthogonally adjacent to itself, regardless of the digit in the Balance Cell. The sum of the values of every cell in the grid is 405. The values of cells in a cage must sum to the total in the top left corner. Digits may not repeat within a cage, but values may.
2178: 𝗦𝘂𝗱𝗼𝗸𝘂: Normal sudoku rules apply. 𝗙𝗼𝗴 𝗢𝗳 𝗪𝗮𝗿: The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. 𝗦𝗽𝗶𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗚𝗮𝗹𝗮𝘅𝗶𝗲𝘀: Divide the grid into galaxies: orthogonally connected groups of cells that have 180 degree rotational symmetry about their centers (marked with a large circle). All cells must be part of a galaxy; no galaxies overlap; a galaxy may be a single cell. Digits may not repeat in a galaxy. If given, a number orbiting a galaxy center shows the sum of all digits in that galaxy. 𝗭𝗶𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝗚𝗮𝗹𝗮𝘅𝗶𝗲𝘀: A "Z" orbiting a galaxy center marks a zipper galaxy where each digit and the cell rotationally opposite to it sum to the circled digit.
2179: You will start in Puzzle A. You will need to complete both puzzles simultaneously to succeed. Important note: the conflict checker will NOT work completely correctly. You may wish to turn it off to not be confused. The grid is covered by fog of war. Placing correct digits will remove the fog in the surrounding cells. In the grids, you will find labeled cages. The digits in these cages are to be transferred to the matching cage in the other puzzle to reveal more fog. The outside clues are red squares covered by fog of war. They indicate the order of the runs of contiguous cells that must be shaded red. The number in the square indicates the sum of the cells in the run. There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs of the same color, but that is not required for runs of different colors. All shaded runs are given. For best results, remove all unshaded marking done once complete. Cells connected by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.
2180: The color of the squares in this puzzle are yellow (Y), pink (P), green (g), gray (G), dark blue (B) and light blue (b). The squares outside the grid indicate the order of the runs of contiguous cells that must be shaded the color of the clue. The number in the square indicates the sum of the cells in the run. There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs of the same color, but that is not required for runs of different colors. All shaded runs are given. For best results, remove all unshaded marking done once complete.
2181: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits may not repeat along a main diagonal (marked in blue). Cells separated by a (single) king's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
2182: Normal sudoku rules apply, except: for each type of clue, three clues are correct (generous), one clue is wrong (haters). Solvers have to find the wrong clues (haters:)), e.g: 347 is a wrong Renban or 238691 is a wrong thermo. A correct purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. In a correct killer cage, there are no repeat digits and the sum of the cage is shown. For a correct thermo, digits must strictly increase from the bulb to the tip. X connects digits summing to 10 and V connects digits summing to 5 if they are correct clues. A correct orange circle indicates an odd digit.
2183: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into grey and orange regions. A region is a group of orthogonally connected cells of the same colour. No 2x2 area may be all one colour. Two regions of the same colour may not touch diagonally. A digit on an arrow cell indicates how many cells you have to travel in the indicated direction until you reach a cell of the opposite colour. Eg: if an orange arrow cell contains a 1 then the neighbouring cell in the direction of the arrow would be grey. Two orthogonally adjacent orange cells must have a difference of at least 4. A small clue indicates the number of cells in the region. In a cage, the sum of orange digits must equal the sum of grey digits. Digits MAY repeat in a cage if allowed by sudoku.
2184: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in its attached circle. (Digits may repeat on an arrow if allowed by other rules.) Digits in a cage cannot repeat. If a number is given in the upper left corner of a cage, the digits in that cage sum to that number, or less.
2185: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells. Digits on a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Split-Pea Lines: The sum of the digits on a line strictly between two circles is equal to a concatenation of the two values in the circles, in some order. For instance, 4-347-1 could be a valid split pea line, as 3 + 4 + 7 = 14, which is 1 concatenated with 4. Digits may repeat on a line if allowed by the other rules. Lines do not cross, branch or share cells with other lines, but they may share circles.
2186: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the blue 'negative' diagonal may not repeat; this diagonal begins in row 1 column 1 and crosses the grid to row 9 column 9. Some of the grid is covered in fog; placing a correct digit will remove the fog surrounding that digit. No guessing is required. A cell with a blue square contains an even digit. Digits in cells joined by an X sum to 10; NOT all X clues are given. Digits in cells joined by a V sum to 5; ALL V clues are given and visible from the outset of the puzzle. If two digits are joined by a black dot then one of those digits is double the other. Not all black dots are given.
2187: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some additional cells grey ("walls") and leave some unshaded ("cave"). The cave is one orthogonally-connected group, and walls form orthogonally-connected groups that touch an edge of the grid. Draw a 1-cell wide loop that moves orthogonally, entering every cave cell (and no wall cells). Each digit on the loop in row N differs from its neighbours on the loop by at least N. Gold is found in wall cells with digits larger than their row number. All possible gold has been given. Digits separated by a white dot have consecutive values.
2191: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell wide loop that moves orthogonally through the center of cells and does not branch, intersect with itself or touch itself (neither orthogonally nor diagonally). The loop has to visit each box at least once. For each box, the maximum number of cells belonging to the loop is k, where k is the box number. Within each box, the box number has to be part of the loop. Boxes are numbered in normal reading order. Two orthogonally adjacent cells are only allowed to contain digits that sum to 7 or 10 if both cells are not part of the loop. The 24 cells that are enclosed by the loop have to contain two magic squares. A magic square is a 3x3 region containing the digits from 1 to 9 once each, where each row, column and diagonal must sum to the same value.
2192: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green German whisper line must differ by at least 5. Both digits (which can be equal) on the endpoints of a green line form a look-and-say clue. If for example the digits on both endpoints of a line are 4 and 3, then the digit 3 has to appear exactly four times on this line AND the digit 4 has to appear exactly three times on the line. The line that starts in R2C6 ends at R2C8.
2193: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orthogonally adjacent cells do not contain consecutive digits. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to a perfect number. A perfect number is a number that equals the sum of its proper divisors (i.e. each divisor excluding the number itself). For example, 20 is not a perfect number since the sum of the proper divisors is 1+2+4+5+10=22, which is not 20. [Hint: There are only two perfect numbers that are less than 45]
2194: Normal sudoku rules apply. In each line of four cells the sum of the first two digits equals the sum of the last two digits.
2195: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide each line into non-overlapping segments, each of which sums to 6. A clue outside the grid is the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in the corresponding row/column. Cages show their sums.
2196: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat on either marked diagonal. Digits on a line form a set of nonrepeating consecutive digits, which may be in any order. Digits connected by an X sum to 10, and digits connected by a V sum to 5.
2197: Draw a closed loop through the centre of some cells that passes through the numbers 1 to 9 in order (so after the 9 the loop returns back to the 1). Each number is passed through exactly once and all other numbers are unvisited. The loop may not turn on numbers it passes through, and the loop crosses itself exactly at the given intersections. Some cells are to be shaded such that all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all orthogonally-connected groups of shaded cells touch the perimeter of the grid. A digit not visited by the loop is unshaded and indicates the number of unshaded cells “seen” in all four directions from the cell containing the digit, including itself (where shaded cells block vision). All digits visited by the loop as well as intersections are shaded. Along the loop, there may never be three shaded or three unshaded cells visited sequentially. For the solution check function to work, enter a ‘1’ in every cell where the loop turns and a ‘2’ in every other unfilled loop cell.
2198: Normal sudoku rules apply. The value of cells along an arrow must sum to the value in its originating circle. White dots separate two cells of consecutive value. Black dots separate two cells where one is double the value of the other. Cells along a pink line form a set of consecutive, non-repeating values in any order. Cells along a green line must differ in value by at least five. No two lines will occupy the same cell. Place 𝐂𝐎𝐏𝐘𝐂𝐀𝐓 cells into the grid so that there is exactly one Copycat cell in each row, column and box; each Copycat cell must contain a different digit and the value of a Copycat cell is the digit in the cell rotationally opposite itself in the grid - 180° rotation about the centre of the grid (for example, if R2C3 is a Copycat cell containing the digit 5 and R8C7 contains the digit 9, the value of R2C3 is the digit in R8C7, which is 9). The value of cells within a cage must sum to the number in the top-left corner (if given). The grid is partially covered in 𝐅𝐎𝐆; placing correct digits will clear the fog from the surrounding area. (Digits at the bottom of the grid have been provided for tracking purposes.)
2199: Select six different digits from the set 1-9. Use these six digits only to fill every cell such that a digit does not repeat in a row, column or box. Grey lines are entropic AND modular; i.e every 3-cell sequence on a line must contain a digit from {123}, one from {456} and {789}; also these digits must include one from {147}, one from {258} and one from {369}. Both indicated diagonals have the same sum. The inequality sign ‘points’ to the lower digit. Any 5 in the grid must have a 1 directly above it or a 9 directly below it (or both).
2200: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Entering a teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. From there she can continue her journey. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits. A redcurrant always sits between an even digit and an odd digit. In this experiment, any cell on the path equals the digit at the top of its column plus the digit at the left-hand end of its row.
2201: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end.
2202: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle.
2203: Draw a non-intersecting loop through the centers of some cells that passes through every circle and moves orthogonally between cells (ie never diagonally). The loop must turn on black circles and travel straight through the cells on either side. The loop must go straight through white circles, and turn in at least one of the cells on either side. All orthogonally connected groups of non-loop cells must be connected to the edge of the grid. For the solution check function to work, enter a 1 into every non-loop cell and 2 into every cell in which the loop turns.
2204: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Digits along a diagonal marked by an arrow sum to the digit on the arrow, if one is given. Any digit along an 'arrow diagonal' indicates exactly how many arrow diagonals contain that digit. Eg: if there is a digit 3 somewhere along an arrow diagonal, then exactly 3 arrow diagonals contain at least one 3.
2207: Divide the Fillominosaurus into regions of orthogonally connected cells with a maximum size of 9 cells such that regions of the same size do not share a border, and fill every cell with a digit equal to the size of its region (ie the number of cells that region contains). A thick black line is a region border. Adjacent digits on a dark green line differ by EXACTLY 5. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. The digit in the circle shows how many times it appears in that circle. The eight cells with teeth attached all contain different digits. (Please note that the teeth themselves are not part of the grid for the purpose of the Fillomino! It is the eight "gum" cells that must contain different digits!)
2210: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into an ocean and islands of one or more orthogonally connected cells such that each island contains a set of digits summing to 9. Digits may repeat on an island but each island must contain a unique set of digits. Islands must not touch each other (even diagonally) except at cells joined by a line, each line marks a bridge between two islands. All cells not part of an island are in the ocean which must be a contiguous region of orthogonally connected cells that never completely fills a 2x2 area. A digit in a circle counts the number of cells in its own region (island or ocean) seen in its row and column combined, including itself, where cells in other regions block vision and are not seen.
2212: Normal sudoku rules apply. In graves (cages), digits must sum to the day, month or year of the date of the day before or after the date on the grave. Digits cannot repeat within graves. Escape the graveyard by carefully plotting an orthogonally connected path between the green and red cells. The path may not cross the highest or lowest digits in a grave. All dates use the international standard Gregorian calendar in the DD/MM/YY format.
2213: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Digits separated by a green grape have a difference of at least 5. In this experiment, dotted box borders divide the correct path into 'index lines'; In any box, the Nth cell visited by Finkz is called 'position N'. (So, for example, in box 7, r9c2 is position 1.) The digit in position N always indicates which position along that segment contains the digit N. Eg: In a box, Finkz might visit the digits 35142 in that order. The first digit being a 3 indicates that the third digit is a 1, the second digit being a 5 indicates that the fifth digit is a 2, and so on.
2214: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. The digits in a cage sum to the number shown, if given. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Shade some cells such that the shaded cells and the unshaded cells each form a single orthogonally-connected region. No 2x2 area can be completely shaded or unshaded (Yin-Yang rules). In a cage, even digits are always shaded, odd digits are always unshaded. On a thermometer, odd digits are always shaded, even digits are always unshaded.
2215: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Diagonal cell pairs (sharing a corner) must have a difference of at least 2.
2216: Normal sudoku rules apply. A black dot joins digits with a ratio of 1:2. Not all dots are given. A digit in a circle must have a value between the digits on both ends of the row. A digit in a green cell must have a value between the digits on both ends of the column. All possible circles and green cells are given.
2217: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each thick grey line can be divided into one or more non-overlapping segments. Each segment contains digits that sum to 10. Eg 513173 is a valid fill for a length 6 line, because it can be broken into 5131 and 73, each of which sum to 10. Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits. These digits can appear in any order. Digits along a thin grey line connecting two circles must have values between the digits in the circles. Eg if the two circles at a line’s ends contain 3 and 8 then digits on the line itself must be selected from [4567]. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio, meaning one digit is exactly double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given.
2218: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the clue in the top left. Moreover, if cages are adjacent to each other (i.e. share an edge), they must contain at least one common digit.
2219: Normal sudoku rules apply. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. NULLIFIERS: In each row, column and 3x3 box there is one 'nullifier' cell to be located. The value of a nullifier cell is zero. Each nullifier cell contains a different digit. MOTION SENSORS: The value on a pink motion sensor indicates how many of the (up to 9) cells immediately surrounding the sensor are visited by Finkz. The sensor itself is counted, if visited. BLACKCURRANTS: Values connected by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio. GRAPES: Values connected by a green grape have a difference of at least 5. FORBIDDEN DOORS: Values connected by a red X sum to 10. Finkz may not pass directly through a red X. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, if a row / column / box is visited by Finkz, then the values of ALL the visited cells in that row / column / box must sum to exactly 13 (even if the cells aren't all adjacent on the path.)
2220: Normal sudoku rules apply. The first digit on a diagonal seen by a camera indicates how many times that digit appears on that diagonal. Any leftover digits on the diagonal (the ones not equal to the first digit) are sorted from lowest to highest, i.e. they appear in non-decreasing order moving away from the camera. Speech bubbles all say the same odd digit.
2221: Fillomino: Divide the grid into orthogonally connected regions such that no two regions of the same size share an edge, and enter a number into each cell equal to the size of its region. Cave: Shade some cells in the grid such that all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all shaded cells are orthogonally connected by other shaded cells to an edge of the grid. Each region must either be entirely shaded or entirely unshaded. If a clued cell is unshaded, the clue indicates the sum of numbers seen orthogonally from that cell; region borders block vision. If a clued cell is shaded, the clue indicates the total sum of numbers in its group of orthogonally connected shaded cells (which could include more than one region).
2222: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each pair of digits connected by a line segment must either differ by at least 5, or sum to at most 5.
2224: Draw four 3x3 boxes in the grid that don't overlap, and fill them with the digits 1-9. Digits can't repeat in a row, column or 3x3 box. Cells that are not in any box are empty, and their value is 0. Digits can't repeat in a cage, and sum to the clue given in the top-leftmost cell of that cage. Draw four snakes, each existing completely inside one of the 3x3 boxes. Each snake is a one cell wide path that only moves orthogonally, and must pass through every cell of its box. Adjacent digits along a snake sum to 10 or 11.
2225: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orthogonally adjacent digits cannot be consecutive. Digits along a line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. The sum of the digits along a diagonal, indicated by an arrow, sum to X, where X must be determined and is the same sum for all arrows.
2226: Fill each row, column and region with the digits 1-6. Each letter corresponds to a unique digit. A cell with one letter in contains the appropriate digit. Digits in a cage sum up to the double digit number represented by two letters inside that cage. Digits may repeat in cages. The digit in the grey square is even.
2227: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Digits connected by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio. All cages have the same total, to be deduced. An electricity symbol indicates the cage's ‘shock value’. Finkz may not enter any cage with a shock value of 5 or higher. Cages with a shock value lower than 5 are safe to enter. In this experiment, dotted 3x3 box borders divide the correct path into segments. The total of each segment must be higher than the total of the previous segment on Finkz' path.
2228: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along each separate grey line (lengths: 3, 5 or 7) the product of the digits is 80. Each cage contains a 2-digit prime number (read left-to-right). A+B = C+D = A+C = B+D = 80
2229: Normal sudoku rules apply. The value of a digit on a line between two circles must be between the two values of the digits in those circles, eg if the two circles joined by a line contain 3 and 6, the digits on the line could be 4 or 5.
2230: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by an X add up to 10. Digits separated by a V add up to 5. If digits are separated by a black dot, one is double the other. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all possible dots or X/V clues are necessarily given.
2231: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every cage has the same sum.
2232: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digit on one end of each line is the sum of the other digits on that line. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the first X grid digits starting from the clue where X is the nearest, eg if R5C1 is 4 then the sum of R5C1-4 is 15.
2233: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. No guessing is required. Shade some cell such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected and each 2x2 area contains shaded and unshaded cells. The value of an unshaded cell is its digit. The value of a shaded cell is double its digit. Values along an arrow sum to the value of the attached circle. Arrows don't overlap.
2234: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent cells cannot contain consecutive digits. A clue outside the grid indicates the sum of the digits along that diagonal path. Cells separated by a black dot are in the ratio 1:2.
2235: Normal sudoku rules apply. In any cell that contains a digit that is smaller than the digit in the diagonally adjacent upper right cell, the sum of those two digits is given, where a question mark can be replaced by any sum ranging from 3 to 17
2236: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some correctly-entered digits clear fog from certain cells, but those cells may be in other parts of the grid. Other digits, even when entered correctly, do not clear fog at all. When the puzzle is fully solved, all the fog will be cleared. Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the cage's top left corner, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle (and these digits can repeat if allowed by other rules). Arrows do not cross or overlap, and all arrow sums are single-digit. Digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10. Digits in cells with a shaded square must be even. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. If digits are separated by a black dot, one is double the other.
2237: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall. If digits are connected by a blackcurrant one digit will be double the other. Not all possible blackcurrants have been given. Entering a teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. From there she can continue her journey. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits. Finkz' path is formed of one or more segments. Any uses of teleports will divide Finkz' path up into physically separate segments, ie; if a teleport is used, the current path segment ends at the entry teleport, and a new separate path segment begins at the matching exit teleport. Any path segment must function as a “renban” ie it must consist entirely of a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits, which can be arranged in any order along the path segment.
2238: Fillomino: Divide the grid into polyominoes so that polyominoes of the same size don't share an edge. Each cell contains a number equal to its polyomino's size. Draw a loop that moves orthogonally from one cell to another through the grid. The loop must not touch itself orthogonally; however, it can touch diagonally. Along the loop, any three consecutive cells must contain numbers congruent to 0 mod 3, 1 mod 3, and 2 mod 3. (In other words, one of the numbers is from the set {3, 6, 9, 12, …}, one is from {1, 4, 7, 10, …}, and one from {2, 5, 8, 11, …}. Numbers on cells with arrows refer to the total amount of loop cells seen in the indicated direction or, if more than one arrow, in the directions combined.
2239: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line in this puzzle is either a Renban Line or a Nabner Line. The solver must determine which is which. Digits along a Renban line must form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. No two digits along a Nabner line can be consecutive, regardless of their position on the line. Digits in cells separated by a black dot are in a 2:1 ratio. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Cells marked with a grey square contain even digits. Cells marked with a grey circle contain odd digits.
2240: Use exactly six digits from 1-9 to fill the grid, with each digit appearing once in every row, column and box. A digit in a diamond is the square root of the sum of the digits along the arrow.
2241: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid gives the sum (or the parity (Odd or Even)) of the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a ratio 1:2.
2242: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade the entire grid using two colours, so that each colour forms a single orthogonally connected area, and no 2x2 area is entirely one colour. An arrow in a cell indicates that the digit in that cell equals the sum of the contents of all cells of the opposite colour in the direction of the arrow. If a cell contains multiple arrows, each arrow is summed separately.
2243: Normal sudoku rules apply. Similarly colored blocks are clones and must contain the same digits in the same positions. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the number shown. A clue outside the grid indicates the digit which has to be placed in the Nth cell in the corresponding direction, where N is the digit placed in the first cell in that direction.
2249: Digits cannot repeat in a cage. Cages show their sums, and are colored purely for decoration.
2251: Place 0-9 in each row, column and outlined region. A cell with a slash features two digits, the digit with the smaller value appearing above the larger one. The orientations of the slashes are purely decorative.
2252: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orange bars in the grid sit between ALL adjacent pairs of consecutive digits.
2253: Divide the grid into nine non-overlapping regions each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1-9 once in each row, column, and region. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog in that cell and possibly other cells; revealing new clues. Some cells contain a grey square inside them. The digit in such a cell is equal to the sum of the (up to 8) surrounding digits that are in different regions. Digits separated by a white dot differ by 1 and belong to the same region. A digit N on an arrow counts how many cells it sees of its region in the indicated direction, including itself. Region borders block vision. Additionally, the digit N+1 must appear immediately behind the first seen region border. Each arrow MUST therefore see a region border within the grid.
2254: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits X, Y and Z in pill shapes (reading left to right) signify that rXcY = Z. Eg, if a pill read [825], then the cell in row 8 column 2 would have to be the digit 5. Digits along the negative diagonal (thin blue line) must not repeat. Any set of three sequential cells along the thick teal line must contain one digit from [1,4,7], one digit from [2,5,8] and one digit from [3,6,9]. Cells separated by an X sum to 10. Not all Xs are given.
2255: SCHRODINGER CELLS: Fill each row, column and box with the digits 0-9 once each. To make this possible, each row, column and box contains one Schrödinger cell, which contains two digits. The value of a Schrödinger cell is equal to the sum of its two digits. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. BLACKCURRANTS: Two values separated by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio. ONE-WAY DOORS: Finkz may only pass directly through a purple arrow in the direction it is pointing. A purple arrow always points to the smaller of the two values it sits between. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, dotted box borders divide the correct path into segments that each contain at least 2 cells. The values of two adjacent cells within the same segment always have the same difference, and this difference is unique for every segment. Eg: if a segment has a sequence of values 1, 3, 5, 7, then its 'same difference' is 2, and so no other segment may have a 'same difference' of 2.
2256: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits MAY repeat in cages if allowed by other rules. The sum of digits in each cage must be a two-digit number that acts as a valid “look-and-say clue” for that cage. Eg if the sum is 21, there must be exactly two 1s in the cage along with any combination of other digits (such that, overall, the digits in the cage sum to 21). Eg2 if the sum is 17, there must be exactly one 7 in the cage along with any combination of other digits (such that, overall, the digits in the cage sum to 17).
2257: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must strictly increase from the bulb. The sum of the digits in each cage is given. The digits on a line must strictly be in between the digits connected on the attached empty circles. Full grey circles (but not necessarily thermometer bulbs) contain odd digits.
2258: Place exactly one queen in every row, column and coloured region. Two queens cannot touch each other. Not even diagonally.
2259: Normal sudoku rules apply. Nine cells (one in each row/column/3x3 box) are "doublers", and have a value of double their digit. Each digit appears in exactly one doubler. Values along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Values in a cage sum to the given total. Digits may not repeat in a cage, but values may.
2260: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1 to 6, once each, in every row, column and 2x3 rectangle). Every indicated diagonal has the same product.
2261: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer digits must not decrease from the bulb to the tip(s).
2262: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Each rectangular trapdoor has a different total (the sum of its two digits.) Finkz should not step on a trapdoor without first locking it shut, making it safe to cross. To make it safe to step on a trapdoor, Finkz must first press all the circular buttons that match the colour of the trapdoor. A digit on a coloured button indicates how many buttons of that colour contain that digit. In this experiment, the correct path will be entropic, ie; every group of 3 adjacent cells along the path must contain one low digit (1, 2 or 3), one medium digit (4, 5 or 6) and one high digit (7, 8 or 9).
2263: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a line sum to the same value for each row the line passes through.
2264: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog in that cell and possibly other cells. The vertical dashed lines are folded onto each other so that columns 1, 2, 8 and 9 form a secondary grid (as if the other columns disappear). In this grid all clues are still valid. Digits in a cage don't repeat and sum to the total given in the top-left corner. Cages don't overlap. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are given. Clues outside the grid give the sum of all cells that contain a digit equal to the distance of that cell from that clue in the row or column. For example, a 4 in Row 2, Column 4 would count towards the 10 clue in row 2, and any other number would not. Horizontal distances in the folded 4x9 grid are limited to 1-4.
2265: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells that are a knight's move away are not allowed to contain identical digits. Both digits (which can be equal) on the endpoints of a line form a look-and-say clue. For example, if the digits on the endpoints are 5 and 3, then there have to be exactly five 3s AND three 5s on this line. The different line colors are only used to avoid confusion regarding line crossings.
2266: Normal sudoku rules apply. A border square is a 2x2 square that crosses at least one 3x3 box border. For all border squares exactly 2 digits are the same. The middle 3x3 box in the grid is a magic square i.e. the sum of digits in each row, column and main 3-cell diagonal in that box is N (where N must be determined by the solver). There are exactly N ‘friendly’ cells in the grid. A cell is friendly if its digit is equal to at least one of its row number, column number or box number. (Rows are numbered top to bottom; columns are numbered left-to-right; boxes are numbered in normal reading order.) Digits separated by a black dot must be in ratio 1:2 (ie one digit is double the other). Not all dots are necessarily given.
2267: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a 1-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells, which does not branch or touch itself, not even diagonally. Circled cells are not on the loop, and the digit in a circle indicates how many of the up to 8 surrounding cells are on the loop. For each pair of adjacent digits along the loop, the larger digit is an integer multiple of the smaller digit. The cell with the rectangle is on the loop.
2268: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage.
2269: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells along lines between two circles must have values between those in the circles. Digits in white circles must be present at least once in the cells the clue touches.
2275: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along the green line, adjacent digits must differ by at least 5. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits between the 1 and 9 on the indicated diagonal. The base paths are double arrows: the digits on each path have the same sum as the bases at the ends of the path. The bases contain four different digits.
2276: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. Adjacent digits along an orange line have a difference of at least 4. Each orange line is in the shape of a square. Cells separated by a black dot are in the ratio 1 to 2. Not all black dots are necessarily shown.
2277: Normal sudoku rules apply. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. TELEPORTS: Entering a teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. From there she can continue her journey. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits. MIRROR CELLS: Each row, column and box contains exactly one mirror cell. Mirror cells may not contain teleports. The value of a mirror cell equals the digit in that cell subtracted from 10. Eg: a 2 in a mirror cell is 'mirrored' on the 1-9 scale, and has a value of 8. Every mirror cell contains a different digit. ONE-WAY DOORS: Finkz may only pass directly through a purple arrow if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two values it sits between. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, the values of any two physically adjacent cells along the path (ie; not separated by teleportation) must have a difference of at least 5.
2278: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells separated by a (single) king's move in chess cannot contain the same digit.
2279: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits must not repeat in cells that are a single knight's move apart (in chess). The digits in a cage must sum to the small clue printed in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Adjacent digits along each green ‘German Whisper’ line must have a difference of at least 5. Lines and cages do not overlap. The grid is partially covered with fog. Correctly placed digits will clear the fog around that cell. No guessing is required.
2280: Normal sudoku rules apply. Color every cell in the grid one of two colors such that all cells of each color are orthogonally connected and no 2x2 region is a single color. A digit in a square indicates how many cells of the same color are seen orthogonally from that position, including itself, where cells of the other color block vision. Diagonally adjacent cells may not contain the same digit.
2281: Normal 4x4 sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. The difference between two adjacent digits on a coloured line indicates exactly how many pairs of adjacent digits along that line have that exact difference.
2282: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. The difference between two adjacent digits on a coloured line indicates exactly how many pairs of adjacent digits along that line have that exact difference.
2283: Normal 9x9 sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. The difference between two adjacent digits on a coloured line indicates exactly how many pairs of adjacent digits along that line have that exact difference.
2284: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a circle indicates how many circles contain that digit. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits do not repeat along the marked diagonal.
