2285: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. Along a line, any changes in shading divide that line into segments of fully shaded or fully unshaded cells. On each line, each such segment (shaded or unshaded) must have the same sum as all other segments. Within the shaded areas, adjacent digits along the lines must differ by at least 5. Within unshaded areas, any string of 3 or fewer digits along the lines must be from a different set of (147), (258) and (369).
2286: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits on a line strictly between two circles is equal to a concatenation of the two values in the circles, in some order. For instance, 3_346_1 could be a valid split pea line, as 3+4+6=13, which is 1 concatenated with 3. A circled digit indicates exactly how many circles contain that digit. Note: This also includes all circles which are bounding the split pea lines. If, for example, a 3 appears in a circle, then there must be exactly 3 circles that contain a 3.
2287: In this experiment, nine letters of the alphabet (to be determined) must be used to fill the grid so that no letter repeats in any row, column or 3x3 box. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. DYNAMIC FOG: Entering correct letters may clear fog somewhere in the maze. No guessing is necessary. CUE CARDS: Each pink cue card sits between two letters that both appear on that cue card. BRAINWAVE MONITORS: The faint light of 11 blue monitors are visible through the fog; Finkz must visit all of these before reaching the cupcake. With any luck, they will provide an insight into her thoughts. TEST CONSTRAINT: 3x3 box borders divide Finkz' path into segments. If a segment contains more than one cell, then the cells must be visited in alphabetical order.
2288: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along orange lines must have a difference of at least 4. A digit in a white circle must appear once in the four surrounding cells. Any two cells which are in the same relative position within their respective 3x3 boxes must contain different digits. For example, if 7 was placed in the top-left corner of box 1, then no other boxes could have a 7 in their top-left corner.
2292: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 region can be completely shaded or unshaded. Each cell in one region has a value of its digit plus 1. Each cell in the other region has a value of its digit minus 1. The sum of the values of cells on lines connecting two circles is equal to a concatenation of the two values in the circles, in some order. For example, 3_346_1 is valid, as 3+4+6=13. Leading zeros are allowed. Every line between two circles is summed separately.
2293: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear some of the fog in the grid. No guessing is required (or recommended). Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 region can be completely shaded or unshaded. R5C5 is neither shaded nor unshaded in the final grid. The sum of the digits on a line strictly between two circles must be equal to a concatenation of the digits in that line's circles. For instance, 3-346-1 could be a valid split pea line, as 3+4+6=13, which is a concatenation of 3 and 1. (ie One circle contains the ‘tens’ digit of that line’s sum; and one circle contains the ‘units’ digit of that line’s sum.) Each circle in the puzzle indicates the number of cells along each line directly connected to the circle, including the bounding circles, which are of the same shading as the circle. All lines travel orthogonally. Lines may not branch or cross, except at circles. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Not all X or V are given.
2294: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column and 3x3 box). Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
2295: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least five. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with an equal sum.
2296: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along the holly outline (green) differ by at least 5. The 3x3 box borders divide the bell outline (yellow) into segments that sum to the same value. Digits on baubles (pink) form a consecutive sequence in any order. Digits in white circles must appear at least once in the surrounding 2x2 cells.
2297: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Entering correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells. The number in the top left corner of a red cage (if given) indicates the sum of the digits sandwiched between 1 and 9 in that row. The number in the top left corner of a blue cage (if given) indicates the sum of the digits sandwiched between 1 and 9 in that column. The digit in a cage indicates how many digits (including the crust of 1 and 9) the corresponding sandwich sum contains. “?” can represent any number at all.
2298: Normal sudoku rules apply. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick walls. (The walls have been decorated with red tinsel.) As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so. DYNAMIC FOG: Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the maze. CHRISTMAS LIGHTS: An orange Christmas light indicates that any digits visited by Finkz in its row or column are odd. A blue Christmas light indicates that any digits visited in its row or column are even. TELEPORTS: Every teleport is part of a matching pair. Entering a teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. From there she can continue her journey. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits. BLACKCURRANTS: Blackcurrants sit between two digits with a 1:2 ratio. BAUBLES: The number on a gold bauble gives the total of any cells it touches. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, any two cells that are adjacent along the path contain consecutive digits (except when separated by teleportation, where the digits are identical.)
2299: Normal sudoku rules apply. Within a cage, digits may not repeat, and the sum of their values is equal to the expression in the top left corner. There are nine vampire cells and nine prey cells in the grid, one of each in every row, column and box. Every digit from 1-9 appears exactly once in a vampire cell, and exactly once in a prey cell. A vampire cell steals the value of the digit in the prey cell in the same box and adds it to its own digit to create its value. The value of the digit in a prey cell is 0.
2300: Divide the grid into square-shaped regions. Fill each region of size NxN with the numbers 1-N, such that no number repeats in any row or column of the region. Same numbers cannot touch orthogonally, even across region borders. Additionally, the following constraints apply: Numbers along an arrow must sum to the number in the attached circle; numbers along a grey thermometer must increase from the bulb end; and numbers along a pink line must form a non-repeating consecutive sequence - these numbers can appear in any order.
2301: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5. A pink line contains a sequence of consecutive digits in any order. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the attached circle.
2302: Normal sudoku rules apply (place 1-9 in each row, column and marked 3x3 box).
2303: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into galaxies: orthogonally connected groups of cells that have 180 degree rotational symmetry about their centers (marked with a small dot). All cells must be part of a galaxy; no galaxies overlap. Grey dots mark "renban" galaxies: those with two or more cells, whose digits form an unbroken consecutive sequence in any order. White dots mark galaxies whose digits do NOT form a consecutive sequence. Digits may not repeat within a galaxy. There is one "dark star" (a single cell galaxy) that is not marked. As per Galactic Map Standards: All galaxies with at least TWO cells indicate their SMALLEST digit with a diamond icon. All galaxies with at least SIX cells indicate their LARGEST digit with a circle icon. The Galactic Census requires that all galaxies with at least THREE cells must report their star system count (sum of digits in the galaxy).
2304: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each blue line is both a "region sum line" and a "10 line". Region sum line: box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum. 10 line: the line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10 – these groups cannot overlap.
2305: For each 4x4 quadrant of the grid, choose 4 of the digits from 0-9, and use them to fill that quadrant so that no digit repeats in any marked 2x2 box. In the overall 8x8 grid, no digit may repeat in any row or column. Digits on the pink line form a non-repeating consecutive sequence which can appear in any order along the line. Box borders divide a blue line into segments whose digits each have the same sum. Digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. No two digits anywhere on a yellow line may be consecutive or the same.
2306: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits in a cage sum to the value indicated. No adjacent run of three cells may be all odd or all even, horizontally or vertically.
2307: Normal fillomino rules apply (ie divide the grid along grid lines into non-overlapping regions of orthogonally-connected cells such that no two regions of the same size touch each other orthogonally; and fill each cell in each region with that region's size ie the number of cells in its region). Use only the digits 1 to 9 and the digit N cannot appear in row N or column N. Digits on the marked diagonals cannot repeat and must sum to the total (if given). The grid is covered by fog. Correctly placing digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid.
2308: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in cages. If a cage contains a clue in the top left corner, that cage must be comprised of 1-, 2-, 3-, and/or 4-digit numbers that sum to that value. Numbers are made from either horizontally adjacent digits read left-to-right; or vertically adjacent digits read top-to-bottom (ie numbers cannot bend!). Every digit within a cage must be part of exactly one number, and numbers may not cross cage borders.
2309: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers outside the grid are both Sandwich Clues and X-Sum Clues. A sandwich clue shows the sum of digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row or column. An X-Sums Clue shows the sum of the first X digits, where X is the first digit, from that direction. Shaded circles are odd numbers. The grid is partially covered with fog. Placing correct digits will remove the surrounding fog.
2310: Divide the grid into nine regions each containing 9 orthogonally-connected cells, such that each cell is part of exactly one region. Some region borders have already been given. Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 such that no digit repeats in any row, column or region. From each circle, draw some arrows that travel in a straight line either horizontally only or vertically only. The number in the bottom right corner of a circle cell indicates the number of arrows that must be drawn from that circle. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the attached circle. Additionally, all cells along arrows must be part of the same region as the circle they originate from. If an arrow doesn't reach the edge of the grid, the cell directly after the tip must be in a different region than the arrow.
2311: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide a blue line into sequences with the same sum. Adjacent digits along a red line have a difference of at least six. If digits are separated by a red cherry, one is double the other.
2312: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The 3x3 boxes in the grid are numbered in normal reading order. In odd numbered boxes, odd digits appear in ascending order (with respect to position within that box). In even numbered boxes, even digits appear in ascending order (with respect to position within that box). (Cells within 3x3 boxes are also numbered in normal reading order.) In cells separated by a black dot, one digit is double the other.
2313: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in that arrow’s circle. A purple line contains a non-repeating set of consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order. Digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10. Digits in cells with a shaded square must be even.
2314: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1 to 6, once each, into every row, column and 2x3 bold-outlined rectangle). Each finger has lost its gold ring! Can you find them? Every row, column and box contains one gold ring, and none of them are located on a finger. Each gold ring contains a different digit. The digits ABC along a finger, reading towards the fingertip (the C goes on the fingernail), indicates that row A column B contains that finger's missing gold ring, which contains the digit C.
2315: Normal sudoku rules apply. In the positive diagonals (ie the blue marked diagonal and the diagonals parallel to it), the difference between two neighboring digits is only 4 or 5. Along the blue marked diagonal all digits are different.
2316: 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: Place 9 non-overlapping 3x3 boxes in the grid. Fill each cell in a box with a digit from 1-9 such that digits don't repeat in rows, columns or boxes. A cell that is not in any 3x3 box should be left blank but its value for the purposes of the loop/palindrome is zero. 𝗗𝘆𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗰 𝗙𝗼𝗴: The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog from that cell and possibly other cells; revealing new clues. 𝗪𝗵𝗶𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝗟𝗼𝗼𝗽: Draw a loop through the centers of some cells that moves orthogonally from cell to cell (never diagonally). The loop may touch itself diagonally, but not orthogonally. Gray lines are palindromes in which the digits along the line must read the same both forward and backward. Digits in a cage sum to the number given. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive.
2440: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages indicate the sum of numbers within them in the top-left corner (but see below). Digits may not repeat within a cage. Arrows indicate the sum of numbers along their diagonal (but again see below). Digits may repeat along a diagonal. The numbers involved in clues can be single-digit or straight multi-digit numbers (but each digit can only contribute to one such number). Vertical numbers are read top-to-bottom, and horizontal and diagonal numbers are read left-to-right.
2455: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages sum to the total given in the cage corner. The highest digit in each cage is inverted (i.e. 9 counts as -9, 8 as -8 etc). Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
2456: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. In some cases, only the parity of that total is given. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb. Adjacent digits on a green line must differ by at least five.
2492: In each across and down segment of length N, place the digits 1 to N once each. Bars divide segments. (Use 0 in this puzzle as a digit to represent 10).
2493: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must NOT sum to a total that satisfies the inequality in the top left corner of the cage. For example, the cage in box 1 must not sum to a total that is greater than 7. Digits MAY repeat in cages if allowed by other rules. Digits on an arrow must NOT sum to the number in the attached circle.
2494: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent numbers along a green line must differ by at least 5. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 2:1 ratio. A number outside the grid indicates the sum of the first X digits, where X is the digit in the closest cell to the clue. Numbers may not repeat in a cage. For the answer check to work, no large digits should be entered outside the grid.
2495: Normal sudoku rules apply. Place 9 halvers (one per row/column/box) into the grid. Each digit must appear in a halver cell. The value of a halver is half its digit. Box borders divide lines into segments with equal sums. Cages with identical labels must contain identical digits in the same relative positions to the label.
2496: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers outside the grid must be deduced and are the sum of the digits between the 1 and 9 in that row or column. Numbers separated by a white dot have a difference equal to the value of the white dot - which is the sum of the numbers on the arrow attached to that dot. Numbers separated by a black dot have a ratio equal to the value of the black dot, which is the sum of the numbers on the arrow attached to that dot.
2498: Yin-Yang: shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 region is entirely shaded or unshaded. In addition, place a digit (from 1 to 9) in every cell with an arrow. This digit is the total number of shaded cells in the indicated direction (including the cell itself, if it is shaded). No two shaded cells can contain the same digit, and no two unshaded cells can contain the same digit. (However, the same digit may occur once shaded and once unshaded.) Cells without arrows do not contain digits.
2499: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells to form a 1-cell-wide orthogonally connected loop. The loop may not touch itself orthogonally, but can touch itself diagonally. Non-loop cells form several orthogonally connected groups. Such a group of size N contains exactly the digits from 1 to N. Each cell with an arrow (called an 'arrow cell') lies on the loop. The digit in an arrow cell is the number of visible loop cells in the indicated direction, where non-loop cells obstruct vision. (The arrow cell is not included in this count). Additionally, digits increase along loop cells seen by an arrow, starting with the digit in the arrow cell.
2500: Subdivide the grid into orthogonally connected regions such that regions of the same size do not share a border. The value of each cell in the grid is equal to its region size. Each "?" represents a digit from 1 to 9 which must be deduced. Dutch flat mates: every cell with value 5 either has a value-1 cell above it, or a value-9 cell below it (or both). Mod-3 groups: all cells with values which are equal modulo 3 form a single orthogonally connected group. This means every cell in the grid belongs to one of three orthogonally connected groups. (I recommend shading cells to keep track of groups.) For answer-check, replace 2-digit numbers with "0", and check that no digits have been rendered above clues.
2501: The grid consists of three types of cells: 'clue cells' (brown), 'shaded cells' (dark grey), and 'loop cells'. You will use the clue cells to determine shaded cells (which can touch each other), and draw a loop through all remaining cells. The loop travels orthogonally through the centres of cells and may not branch or cross itself. Two shaded cells are given. Place the digits 0 to 8 in the nine brown clue cells with no repeats ie the brown cells must contain one of each of the digits 0,1,2…7,8. Each digit counts two things: first, it is the number of shaded cells in the eight neighbouring cells. Second, it is the total number of shaded cells in all indicated directions. (This count is not obstructed by any other cell-types.) For clarity, clue cells are not considered shaded, and cannot be shaded.
2513: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colors used in this puzzle are green (g), brown (b), and black (k). A clue outside the grid with an arrow (little killer) shows the sum of the cells on the indicated diagonal. Digits separated by a black (kropki) dot have a 1:2 ratio. Clues in colored squares outside the grid (none of which lie) indicate the sum of all cells in that row or column that are shaded the color of the clue. Shading does not need to be contiguous. If a cell is shaded, and if a cell has a clue in the lower right corner, the clue gives the digit in the cell. If a clue is unshaded, then the number in the lower right corner is a lie, so the digit in the cell is not the clue. Some clues are lying, while others tell the truth. All truthful clues are fully-shaded, lying clues must not be fully-shaded. Note that there are an equal number of truth-tellers and liars for both the little killers and the Kropki dots.
2530: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits do not repeat and sum to the number shown. There are 5 types of balls in the grid: A: 1 set of digits around it must sum to 10 B: 2 sets of digits around it must sum to 10 C: 1 set of digits around it must sum to 5 D: 2 sets of digits around it must sum to 5 E: 1 set of digits must sum to 5, 1 set of 2 digits must sum to 10 A ‘set of digits’ always contains 2 orthogonally connected digits. No digit is part of 2 sets on the same circle, but it may be part of sets on different circles. There are no negative constraints, so other pairs may add to 5 or 10 around circles or elsewhere.
2531: Normal sudoku rules apply. The pumpkin (orange line) is an entropic line on which each neighbouring group of three cells include one low (1,2,3), one middle (4,5,6) and one high (7,8,9) digit. The stem (green line) is a German whisper, where neighbouring digits have a difference of at least 5. The face is made up of of thermometers, on which the digits increase from the bulb end. Digits separated by an X sum to 10 and digits separated by a V sum to 5.
2532: For each of the four marked 9x9 grids, normal sudoku rules apply. A gray line is a palindrome, reading the same backwards and forwards. Box borders divide a blue region sum line into segments with the same total. Different lines may have different values. Digits in a cage can repeat in different sudoku grids, but cannot repeat within a single sudoku – they sum to the total given. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1-X ratio where X is the number on the dot.
2533: Normal sudoku rules apply. Fog appears in the grid. Placing correct digits clears fog from surrounding cells. Digits on an arrow sum to the number in the attached circle. On a red line, each set of three digits includes one low (1,2,3), one middle (4,5,6) and one high (7,8,9). The entropic lines move horizontally and vertically, and do not overlap with each other.
2538: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits an equal distance from the centre of a purple line must sum to the digit in the centre of that purple line. A clue outside the grid indicates the total of any digits in its row/column that neighbour at least one consecutive digit within that row/column. Eg, if a column, reading downwards, contains the digits 128396547, the clue at the top of the column would be 18; the sum of 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6, which are the only digits which neighbour a consecutive digit within that sequence. Cells separated by the black dot contain digits with a 1:2 ratio ie one digit is double the other.
2539: Normal sudoku rules apply. Place 9 ‘halvers’ (one in each row, column and 3x3box) into the grid. Each digit must appear in a halver cell. The value of a halver is half its digit. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments and the sum of the values on each segment must be the same. (Different lines may have different segment sums). The shaded dominoes are clones: ie they contain the same digits in the same positions. Eg if r2c3 is a 1 then r5c7 is a 1 and r9c4 is a 1.
2545: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a cell with arrows facing outward must be greater than all of its orthogonal neighbors. Digits along arrows sum to the digit in the attached circle. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits in cells separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.
2546: CHAOS CONSTRUCTION: Divide the grid into 8 regions each containing 8 orthogonally connected cells, and fill the grid with the digits 1-8 so that digits don't repeat in a row, column or region. DOUBLERS: Each row, column and region contains exactly one doubler cell. The value of a doubler cell is double its digit. Each doubler cell contains a different digit. QUADSWALLOP: Each digit 1-8 is represented by a different letter of the alphabet, to be determined. In each grey quad circle, 4 of the letters correspond to the digits (not values) in the surrounding 4 cells, but there is also one lying letter which does not correspond to any of the surrounding digits. The purple and green circles on the right can be used to keep track of letters in the grid, and their corresponding digits. PURPLE X: Values separated by a small purple X sum to 10, and are in the same region. The two ends of a grey, red or blue line always lie in different regions. Red and blue lines have an additional rule: PARITY LINES (RED): Two adjacent cells along a red line contain one even value and one odd value. REGION SUM LINES (BLUE): Region borders divide blue lines into segments which each have the same total value.
2547: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some of the grid is covered in fog; entering a correct digit will clear all fog in that digits immediate neighbourhood. Guessing is not required. The 3x3 box borders divide lines into segments, whose sums must strictly increase from one end to the other. No line has more than one segment in any single 3x3 box; different lines are different colours; lines may not branch or share cells with other lines; and lines may cross diagonally but only at cell vertices.
2548: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits with a 1:2 ratio ie one digit will be double the other. Not all dots are given.
2549: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
2550: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a line, each set of 3 adjacent digits sums to a multiple of 5.
2551: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into a number of islands -- orthogonally connected groups of cells. Every island contains a single circled cell; the digit in the circle indicates the number of cells making up the island. The islands are surrounded by a waterway -- a single orthogonally connected group of cells. All caged cells are waterway cells; The digit in a caged cell indicates how many waterway cells are seen orthogonally from that position, including itself (island cells block vision). The waterway cannot form any 2x2 areas.
2552: Normal fillomino rules apply ie Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally-connected cells. Fill each cell with a number equal to its region’s size (ie the number of cells in its region). No two regions of the same size can share an edge (although they may touch diagonally). Use only region sizes of 1 to 9 and the digit N cannot appear in row N or column N. Two digits separated by a black dot must be in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit should be double the other). Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
2553: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. Digits along a purple line are a set of consecutive digits in any order with no repeats. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the circle of that arrow. Additionally, adjacent digits on the purple lines and the arrows (including the circles) are different and not consecutive.
2554: Normal sudoku rules apply. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid - no guessing is necessary. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other). Todd and Steven are playing a game of Tic-Tac-Toe in a sudoku grid, where they attempt to 'claim' each 3x3 box. It's a very close game, with one player claiming four boxes and the other claiming five. However, the winner isn't necessarily the player to claim most boxes. To win the overall game, a player must claim at least one straight line of three 3x3 boxes (horizontally, vertically or diagonally), without their opponent managing to get a line of three boxes themselves. To determine who claims each 3x3 box, Todd and Steven play a mini game in each box. Todd places odd digits and Steven places even digits. A player claims a 3x3 box by getting at least one straight line of three digits of their parity (horizontally, vertically or diagonally) in that box, and without their opponent managing to get a line of three digits themselves. Every 3x3 box has a definitive winner, and there is also a definitive winner of the overall multi-box game. But who is it?!
2555: The shaded regions (outlined in red) create a 6x6 grid scattered throughout the big grid. In this 6x6 grid, place the digits 1-6 exactly once in each row, column and region. The unshaded regions create a 10x10 grid scattered throughout the big grid. In this 10x10 grid, place the digits 0-9 exactly once in each row, column, and region. Normal Japanese Sums rules apply. Colors used in this puzzle are orange (r), green (g), black (b), light blue (L), dark blue (k), yellow (y), and purple (p). For best results, remove all unshaded marking you have done once completed. The squares outside the grid indicate the order of the runs of contiguous cells that must be shaded the color of the clue. The number in the square indicates the sum of the cells in the run. There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs of the same color, but that is not required for runs of different colors. All shaded runs are given.
2556: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a closed loop that moves orthogonally or diagonally between the centres of no more than 23 cells. The loop passes through all boxes except box 5 (the shaded box). The digit 1 appears on the loop once, the digit in the circle appears on the loop twice, and every other digit N that appears anywhere on the loop appears on the loop N times. Adjacent digits on the loop are different and box borders divide the loop into regions of equal sums.
2557: Normal sudoku rules apply. Green cells are illuminati cells. A digit on an illuminati cell cannot repeat anywhere along the 4 orthogonal and 4 diagonal directions from the given cell. Green cells also form a magic square (extended), so considering green cells only, each 3-cell row, column or diagonal sums to the same number and no two green cells are the same. White dots connect consecutive digits. Black dots connect dots with a 1:2 ratio. Purple lines contain consecutive digits in any order. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the total given.
2558: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. Digits in cells with a shaded square must be even. The digit in the cell with a shaded circle must be odd.
2559: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Correctly placed digits will remove fog from surrounding cells. Guessing is not required or recommended. Draw a one-cell wide snake of orthogonally connected cells that does not branch or touch itself. The non-snake cells must form a single, orthogonally connected area. No 2x2 region can be entirely snake or entirely non-snake. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Cells separated by dots will contain one snake cell and one non-snake cell. The 3x3 box borders divide the snake into segments, each of which have the same sum.
2560: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle.
2561: Normal sudoku rules apply. There are clues outside the grid. Each side either contains all Sandwich clues, or all X-Sum clues. Which side contains which type of clue is to be determined by the solver. A sandwich clue gives the total of the digits placed between 1 and 9 in the row or column. An X-Sum clue gives the sum of the first X cells that are seen in the row or column from the clue, where X is the first seen cell (i.e. a clue of 8 could be satisfied by 26 or 314 or 341).
2562: Normal sudoku rules apply. Dots divide lines into segments with equal sums. Digits may not repeat within a segment. E.g: 8-35-125.
2563: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Each pink line (or branching line) contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, which can appear in any order. Digits on a gray line must sum to 10. Lines may share endpoints, but otherwise don't overlap.
2564: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat along either main diagonal. Some of the grid is covered with fog. Placing correct digits into cells clears the fog from all adjacent cells. Guessing is not required or recommended. Digits in cages must sum to the number in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within cages.
2565: Normal sudoku rules apply. One digit from 1-9 (to be determined) is 'inactive' and always gets ignored by any line it appears on. REGION SUM: The 3x3 box borders divide blue lines into segments which each have the same sum (not counting any inactive digits.) The region sum may be different for different blue lines. RENBAN: All active digits on a pink line must form a non-repeating consecutive set. NABNER: Any two active digits anywhere on a yellow line may not be consecutive or the same.
2566: Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Each row, column and region contains the digits 1-9 once each. Digits along an arrow must sum to the number in the attached circle. Additionally, each arrow must be contained within one region, and the circle cannot belong to the same region as its arrow. The number in the circle shows how many region cells it sees in its row and column (including the cell with the circle itself) until it reaches the borders of the region.
2567: Normal sudoku rules apply. Place doubler-cells into the grid so that there is exactly one doubler-cell in each row, column and box. Each doubler-cell must contain a different digit and the value of a doubler-cell is twice the value of the contained digit. On both marked diagonals there are no repeated VALUES. VALUES along a purple line form a non-repeating consecutive set, in any order. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments which each have the same sum (ie the sum of their VALUES is the same).
2568: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits do not repeat in the marked cage. Neighbouring digits along a green line differ by at least 5 or more. Along a thermometer, digits increase from the bulb end. The grey (non-thermometer) lines are palindromes ie digits read the same forwards and backwards.
2569: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide blue lines into segments with the same sum. Along a pink line, digits form a non-repeating consecutive sequence in any order. Each cage's sum is a perfect cube.
2570: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in cages. If the sum of a cage is a 1-digit number, that number must be in the cell pointed at by the cage's northwest corner. If the sum is a 2-digit number, it must be in the domino formed by that cell and the one to its left. (Example: if the sum of the cage in Box 3 was 9, then r1c6 would be 9. If it's sum was 12, then r1c5 would be 1 and r1c6 would be 2.) Every set of 4 adjacent digits on a peach line must contain a digit from each of the X-pair (ten-pair) subsets of {1,9}, {2,8}, {3,7}, and {4,6}. A 5 may not appear on a peach line. Digits on a line may repeat if allowed by other rules.
2571: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the given total.
2572: Normal sudoku rules apply. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is necessary. Digits along a beige 'hitline' do not repeat. The number on a blue circle (or two-digit pill reading downwards or from left to right) points to the first cell ('position 1') along a hitline, and indicates the total of any digits that equal their position number along that hitline. Eg: on a 4-cell hitline, if the sequence of digits reads 1694 starting from the cell being pointed at, then the blue total would be 5 (the sum of 1 and 4) because 1 is in the 1st position and 4 is in the 4th position, and these are the only digits which match their position numbers.
2573: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a line sum to the same total for each box the line enters. Different lines may have different totals. Any set of three sequential cells along an entropic line must contain a low digit (1,2,3), a middle digit (4,5,6), and a high digit (7,8,9). Digits may repeat on a line, if allowed by other rules. All lines in this puzzle conform to both rulesets.
2574: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along the teal line, any set of three adjacent digits must contain one digit from (147), one digit from (258) and one digit from (369). Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the top left corner. In two cells separated by a black dot one digit must be double the other. Digits separated by a white dot differ by 1.
2575: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. A purple line has no repeats and contains a set of consecutive digits, which may be in any order. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with equal sums. A black dot indicates digits which have a 1:2 ratio.
2576: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide a blue line into segments; each segment along a line must have the same sum. (Different lines may have different segment sums.)
2577: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single chess knight's move cannot contain the same digit. The grey line is a Palindrome ie its digits read the same in both forward and backward directions. Digits in a cage must not repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.
2578: Normal sudoku rules apply ie fill the grid with the digits 1-9 so that digits don't repeat in any row, column, and marked 3x3 box. Two cells adjacent along a red line must contain one even digit and one odd digit. Two cells connected by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Two cells connected by a black dot contain digits where one is double the other.
2579: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the small number in the top left corner of the cage.
2580: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each wooden stake (line) sums to either 16 or 17. Each grave (cage) sums to the value shown. There are 9 vampires (digits 1-9 once each) in the grid; one in each row, column and box. There are also 9 victims (digits 1-9 once each) in the grid; one in each row, column and box. For purposes of cage and line totals: (a) vampire cells have a value equal to the sum of their digit plus the digit of the victim cell in their box, and (b) victim cells have a value of 0.
2581: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line is divided into segments at 'split points', to be discovered on certain cell edges crossed by the line. Each segment along a line has the same sum, but this sum can be different for different lines. Digits MAY repeat along a segment, if allowed by sudoku. The digit in a green circle indicates the number of split points on that line.
2582: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum.
2583: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments; the segments along an individual line must each have the same sum.
2584: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments; along an individual line, each segment must have the same sum. Additionally, digits may not repeat on a line.
2585: Normal sudoku rules apply. There is a small cloud in the top left corner of the grid. It will probably disappear when you reach the end of your space journey. The sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in the connected circle. Along pink lines, digits form a consecutive sequence in any order.
2588: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a V sum to five. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. The grid is covered in fog; placing correct digits will clear the fog.
2589: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum up to zero. Digits on the indicated diagonals also sum up to zero, but may repeat if allowed by other rules. Divide the grid into two orthogonally connected regions, such that no 2x2 area is entirely one region or the other. In one region, every digit counts as twice its value for the purposes of cages and diagonals. In the other region, every digit counts as the negative of its value for the purposes of cages and diagonals. [For example, a two-cell cage that adds up to zero could be fulfilled by a doubled 1 (which counts as 2) and a negated 2 (which counts as -2).]
2590: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (i.e. one digit is twice the other). Digits may not repeat on either of the marked diagonals.
2591: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single chess knight's move cannot contain the same digit. Cells that are part of the grey tower must be greater than all orthogonally adjacent non-tower cells. Note: any cell that the tower even partially covers is considered a tower cell. Every group of 3 cells along Rapunzel's hair must contain one low digit (1, 2, 3), one medium digit (4, 5, 6), and one high digit (7, 8, 9). Note, for the avoidance of doubt, that Rapunzel's hair begins in row 4 column 2.
2595: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog in that cell and possibly other cells. Guessing is not required. A cell with an arrow contains the sum of all cells where the digit in a cell (in the direction of the arrow) equals the distance from that arrow clue. If multiple arrows are in one cell, the sum total of all such digits in those directions is used. E.g. if the digit in Row1, Column7 is a 2, it would contribute to the sum in Row3, Column7 while every other digit in that cell would not.
2596: Welcome to the dungeon! Can you find your way through the different rooms of the dungeon and reach all checkpoints with an evolving class? Normal Sudoku Rules apply. Digits in cages (rooms) do not repeat and sum to the total if given. Adventure Path: Draw a path starting at the first check point (the green square with a 1) to every visible checkpoint in ascending order. The path only travels orthogonally and must visit each cage (room). The path can never travel outside of rooms nor checkpoints and can only enter and exit any cage (room) exactly once. Dynamic Fog: Each time you determine the exact path and the digit in the highest visible checkpoint cell, put it in to reveal a new checkpoint and new cages. Dynamic Classes: Each time you reveal new cells, delete the path and all entered digits that are not on checkpoints. Then change your class, which determines the line type all cells on the path have to obey. List of classes (you start with Palindrome): 1-2 : Palindrome: Digits on a palindrome path read the same forwards and backwards. 1-2-3: German Whisper: Two cells connected by a German Whisper path must have a difference of at least 5. 1-2-3-4: Region Sum: Box borders divided the path into segments of equal sums. 1-2-3-4-5: Dutch Whisper: Two cells connected by a Dutch Whisper path must have a difference of at least 4. You have completed the dungeon when all 5 checkpoints are revealed and the complete grid is filled.
2597: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each turquoise line is an Index Line, i.e. the digit in the Nth cell along such a line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. For example, if a diamond cell contains a 3, the third cell along that line must have a 1. The yellow lines are Nabner Lines, i.e. on such a line there may not be consecutive or repeated digits. For example, if a 5 lies on a Nabner line, this line may not contain another 5 and neither a 4 nor a 6.
2598: Normal sudoku rules apply. Outside clues are the absolute difference between the sum of digits between 7 and 8, and the sum of digits between 8 and 9, in their corresponding row or column. '?' represents a digit (0~9) to be determined by the solver. All sandwiches have at least one filling, i.e. there are no runs of three adjacent cells in any row or column containing only the digits 7, 8, and 9.
2599: Draw seven 6-cell regions in the grid (some region boundaries are given), and place the digits 1-6 in every row, column, and region. (Regions consist of 6 orthogonally connected cells). Cells not in regions should be left empty. Each clue outside the grid gives the sum of the cells in the row or column from the direction of the clue until reaching an empty cell.
2600: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade the whole grid using two colours such that each colour forms an orthogonally connected region, and no 2x2 area is a single colour. The digit in a caged cell indicates how many cells of the same colour are seen orthogonally from that position, including itself. The other colour blocks vision. Digits along an arrow sum to the value in the attached circle.
2601: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a line, each set of 3 adjacent digits sums to multiple of 5. In cells joined by a black dot, one digit must be double the value of the other.
2602: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into rectangular regions of orthogonally connected cells, so that every cell is in a region and regions do not overlap. Each region contains exactly one circle, and a digit in a circle indicates the number of cells in its region. Digits cannot repeat within a region. Digits cannot repeat on the indicated diagonal. The sum of the digits inside each cage is equal to the number shown.
2603: Normal sudoku rules apply. A circled digit indicates exactly how many circles contain that digit. Digits along a purple line do not repeat and form a consecutive sequence, but can be arranged in any order. Adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits along a red line must alternate between odd and even.
2604: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along an orange line have a difference of at least 4. Box borders divide the blue lines into segments whose values have the same sum. Different lines may have different sums. Digits along the purple line are a set of consecutive digits in any order. Cells separated by an X sum to 10.
2605: Place a digit from 1-9 in each cell so that every digit appears once in every row, column, and box. (For clarity, there are 6 rows, 6 columns, and 54 cells in the puzzle). Digits increase along thermometer lines, starting from the bulb. Digits may not repeat in the cage. Each cell with an arrow contains the sum of the digits on the diagonal pointed to by the arrow.
2606: Place the digits 1 to 9 once each in every row, column, and region. Each region consists of 9 orthogonally-connected cells; regions do not overlap and must be located by the solver. The digit in the top-left cell of a region (the leftmost cell in its highest row) is its region number. All region numbers are different. If a cell with the digit X in a region with the number N contains an arrow, then the cell X steps away in the indicated direction belongs to the region numbered N+1. Not all possible arrows are given.
2607: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring digits on a line must have a difference of at least 4.
2608: Normal sudoku rules apply. Fog covers the grid. Placing a logically deduced digit in a cell lifts fog from that cell and possibly other cells. Spiral Galaxies: Divide the 9x9 grid into “galaxies” of orthogonally connected cells; each galaxy is180° rotationally symmetric about its centre – ALL galaxy centres are marked with a square. Each cell is part of exactly one galaxy. Digits don't repeat in a galaxy and sum to the value on its central square clue. Circled digits count the number of cells in their galaxy.
2609: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a marked diagonal cannot repeat. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Cells with the same relative position within a 3x3 box must contain different digits. (Eg the middle-left position of r2c1, r2c4, r2c7, r5c1, r5c4, r5c7, r8c1,r8c4 & r8c7 must all be different). Let a digit's entropy describe if it is low (123), medium (456), or high (789). Let its modularity be its remainder when divided by 3. Let a SET be a set of three digits such that their entropy and modularity are either all the same or all different. Some examples of SETs are: 789 (same entropy, different modularity), 258 (different entropy, same modularity), 168 and 348 (different entropy and different modularity). In this puzzle, the three rows and three columns of each box all form SETs.
2610: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered with fog. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is necessary. Five tetrominoes (shapes made of 4 orthogonally connected cells) have just moved into a large house with 12 pentominoes (shapes made of 5 orthogonally connected cells). No two characters are exactly the same shape (rotations and reflections count as the same, e.g. there is only one L tetromino). There is also a pet cat called Ocho, who occupies just one cell. Fit all 18 occupants into the grid so that none of them overlap. Outlines of characters are shown with a thick black line. A small clue appearing anywhere within a character indicates the total sum of all the digits in that character. No two characters have the same total. Digits never repeat on a character. Around the grid are photos of some (not all) of the characters. Each photo shows a character as it appears in the grid, unreflected (i.e. photos are not mirrored). It also shows one of its digits, with its correct orientation and position within the character. (Each character must be placed in the grid so that its given digit is up the right way.)
2611: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in cages and sum to the total in the top left corner of the cage.
2612: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the indicated value; some of the values have been replaced by question marks. White dots connect consecutive digits. Along purple lines, any consecutive group of three values (digits or cage totals) must sum to a multiple of three.
2613: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb towards the tip. Along the green lines neighbouring digits must differ at least by 5. (Digits may repeat along these lines.) Each purple lines contain a set of consecutive digits in any order. (Eg 354 is a valid arrangement.) The blue line is just for decoration!
2614: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 3x3 box contains an invisible 'index line' whose route must be determined. The index lines are all 9 cells long, only move orthogonally (not diagonally), and don't cross any 3x3 box borders. They don't cross themselves, or pass through any black or green spots. Each row, column and box contains exactly one hidden diamond, which lies at one end of its index line, and contains its box number. (Boxes are numbered 1-9 in normal reading order from top left to bottom right.) The digit in position N along an index line (starting at the end with the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N should be placed. Eg: if the 1st digit is a 3, then the 3rd digit will be a 1. Digits separated by a black spot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other). Digits separated by a green spot have a difference of at least 5.
2615: Normal sudoku rules apply. Fog hides some clues. Placing a logically deduced digit lifts fog from its cell and sometimes other cells. Cages with the same letter have the same sum.
2616: Normal sudoku rules apply. The gray lines in the grid are either Renban lines or Region Sum Lines. Renban lines contain a set of non-repeating consecutive digits (not necessarily in order). Box borders divide the Region Sum Lines into segments whose values have the same sum. Different Region Sum Lines may have different sums. The clues outside the grid show the sum of the first X digits from that direction, where X is the first of those digits.
2617: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a (slow) thermometer digits must increase or stay the same from the bulb to the tip.
2618: Normal sudoku rules apply. Purple lines are zipper lines: digits an equal distance from the line’s central cell must sum to the digit in that central cell. The grid contains nine "doublers," one in each row, column, and 3x3 box; each digit from 1-9 is "doubled" exactly once. Doubled digits count as twice their value for the purposes of the zipper lines.
2619: Normal sudoku rules apply. Pink lines must contain a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order. Cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are necessarily given.
2620: In each of the four stacked grids, normal 4x4 Sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1 to 4, once each, into every row, column and 2x2 box.) The value of a cell with a window is the sum of its digit and the digit in the cell from a different grid that can be seen through the window. Each value in a circle is the sum of the values on the attached arrow. Adjacent values along a green line differ by at least five.
2621: Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally connected cells. Place a digit from 1-9 in every cell such that each digit appears exactly once in every row, column, and region. Region boundaries divide the line into segments. The digit in the Nth cell of a segment indicates the position of the digit N on that segment. Positions are counted starting from 1 at an end of the segment which much be determined. Different segments may count in different directions relative to the line.
2622: Normal sudoku rules apply. The colored cells all contain ODD digits. Greater than and less than signs indicate one digit is higher or lower than the one next to it. Each letter corresponds to a different number and these must be resolved.
2625: The King's Law states that for a digit X, exactly X instances of the digit X are a king's move away from another instance of the digit X. However, two of the digits 1-9 (to be deduced) are rebellious and do not abide by this law. In fact, a rebellious digit is never a king's move away from another instance of itself. The grid is partially covered with fog. Correctly placed digits will clear the fog around that cell.
2626: Shade some cells so that all shaded cells form one orthogonally connected area and no 2x2 region is entirely shaded. Clues cannot be shaded, and every orthogonally connected area of unshaded cells contains exactly one clue, the value of which represents the size of the area.
2627: This puzzle is a 4 × 4 grid of cells, which are arranged in four rows and four columns of four cells each. Cells are divided into "cell pieces" by grey lines. Write a digit from 1–4 in each cell piece. Digits may not repeat in a cell. In each row, column, and box, the total area of the cell pieces containing the digit 1 must equal the area of a single cell. The same is true for the digits 2, 3, and 4. When cell pieces in the same cell have equal size, you may enter their digits in either order.
2628: Place 1-6 in each row, column and marked region. Place Doubler cells into the grid so that there is exactly one Doubler cell in each row, column and box; each Doubler cell must contain a different digit and the value of a Doubler cell is twice the value of the contained digit. Cells along a red line form a set of consecutive, non-repeating values in any order.
2629: Each of the 16 puzzles has a unique ruleset. Here are the rules for puzzle 1. You'll need to discover the rest of the puzzles' rules as you go! Normal 4x4 sudoku rules apply. The difference between a pair of adjacent digits along a coloured line equals the number of adjacent pairs along that line that have that difference. The black dot sits between two digits with a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other).
2630: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box 1 is a magic square in which all the rows, columns and both diagonals sum to the same total. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least five. Digits along a purple line are a set of consecutive digits in any order with no repeats. Digits on the blue line are even. Digits on the orange line are odd. Cells separated by black dots are in the ratio of 1 to 2.
2631: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. The digit in a bulb counts the number of pairs of consecutive digits appearing on its thermometer.
2636: Place the digits 1-9 without repeats in each row, column, and 9 deduced regions each of 9 orthogonally connected cells. A clue outside the grid indicates that the first N cells pointing in that direction are in the same region - followed by a region border - where N is the first digit seen by the clue. Neighbouring digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5.
2637: Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie Place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column and 3x3 box.) Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. In a 3x3 box every horizontal threesome contains one digit from {1,2,3}, one from {4,5,6} and one from {7,8,9}. A positive diagonal is any diagonal going from South-West to North-East. When normal sudoku rules allow neighbouring digits on a positive diagonal to be equal they MUST be equal. eg r2c4, r3c3 and r4c2 must contain the same digit; r6c2 and r7c1 must contain the same digit; etc.
2638: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the circle. Digits in a cage sum to the total given. A clue outside the grid shows the total of the indicated diagonal. Digits do not repeat along the marked diagonal. Digits separated by a king's move in chess do not repeat.
2639: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some of the grid is covered in fog. Entering correct digits uncovers more clues. No pair of adjacent digits on a beige line may have the same difference. For example, if a line has a 3 and 5 next to each other, it may not also contain a 7 and a 9 next to each other. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.
2640: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie Each row, column, and 3x3 must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each). Digits in a cage cannot repeat and sum to the small clue in the cage’s upper left corner. Renban: Digits along purple lines are a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in some order.
2641: These groups can consist of a single cell or multiple cells. Both of a region's groups must have the same size and shape, but may be rotated or reflected. Shaded groups may not be orthogonally adjacent. Cells with arrows are not shaded, and indicate the size of a group of shaded cells which occupies the adjacent cell in the indicated direction(s). (Note: a 2 in a cell with two arrows would indicate that there was a region of size 2 in BOTH directions.) For each region whose shaded groups consist of multiple cells, one shaded group must contain a set of consecutive digits in any order, and adjacent digits within the other shaded group must differ by at least 5. The solver must determine which is which.
2642: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along each coloured route can be read as a 6-digit 'route number', starting at the square and finishing at the spot. These nine route numbers can be ranked from lowest to highest. A circled yellow taxi on a route indicates that route's rank. (A '1' taxi would be on the route with the smallest 6-digit route number. None of the route numbers are the same, so there are no tied ranks.) Box borders divide a BLUE ROUTE into segments whose digits have the same sum. Adjacent digits on a GREEN ROUTE have a difference of at least 5. Digits on a PINK ROUTE form a non-repeating, consecutive set in some order.
2643: Place a digit from 1 to 9 in every row, column, and cage. If and only if adjacent digits do not sum to a prime number, shade the boundary between them. Shaded boundaries must divide the grid into exactly 2 regions. There may be shaded boundaries that lie within a region without fully dividing it. A digit in a cell with one or more arrows indicates the total number of shaded boundaries in the directions of all arrows combined.
2644: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in cages and must sum to the given total in the top left corner. Pink lines must contain a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order.
2645: The digits 1 to 9 occur exactly once each in every row, column, and region. Regions cannot overlap and each consists of nine orthogonally-connected cells. The region borders must be deduced. A digit in a cell with arrow(s) gives the total number of cells in the same region as the arrow cell in all indicated directions combined (NB this count includes the arrow cell itself.) Cells in different regions to the arrow cell immediately block vision (and therefore prevent any cells further along the arrow’s path in that direction from contributing to the arrow cell’s count).
2646: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage is either full of "oil" (even digits), full of "water" (odd digits), or a mix of both. In all cases, each "row" within a cage is of just one type (oil or water). Oil floats on water, so even digits will always be in rows above odd digits in mixed cages. Digits in cages do not repeat and must sum to the small clue, if given. Black dots separate two digits where one is double the other.
2647: Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie Place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row, column and 3x3 box). Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
2648: Normal sudoku rules apply. There is a bishop's constraint on the white squares of the checkerboard: the digits on each white diagonal are different. (Please note that playing in Dark Mode switches the white and black squares!). Digits connected by a V or X sum to 5 or 10 respectively. Digits connected by a white dot are consecutive.
2649: Squishdoku: Place the digits 1 through 9 once each in every 3x3 box, with no repeats in any row or column. Cells on region borders (dashed lines) are simultaneously part of the 3x3 boxes on both sides of the line. Index Lines: The digit in the Nth cell along a teal line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. For example, if a diamond cell contains a 3, the third cell along that line must have a 1.
2650: Normal sudoku rules apply. The diagonal from r1c1 to r9c9 acts as a parity mirror. Each cell has the same parity as the cell reflected in the mirror, i.e. if r2c6 is even, r6c2 is also even. The digit in the Nth cell along a teal line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. For example, if a diamond cell contains a 3, the third cell along that line must have a 1.
2651: Normal sudoku rules apply. On purple lines, digits an equal distance from the centre of the line must sum to the digit at the centre. The centre of the line is marked with a dot. On blue lines, each set of 3 digits sums to a multiple of 5.
2652: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle.
2653: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade the boundary between adjacent digits if and only if they sum to an even number. Shaded boundaries must divide the grid into exactly 2 regions. There may be shaded boundaries that lie within a region without fully dividing it, as allowed by other rules. A digit in a cell with one or more arrows indicates the total number of shaded boundaries in the directions of all arrows combined.
2654: Normal sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1-9 exactly once in each row, column and box). Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end.
2655: Normal sudoku rules apply. The four hungry hungry hippos on the edges of the grid are fighting to eat all of the large circles in the grid. If a circle is entirely within the colored territory of a single hippo, that circle will be eaten by that hippo. If a circle is on the border between multiple hippos' territories, which hippo eats that circle must be determined. A number on a hippo shows the sum of all circles that it eats. A digit on a circle indicates how many circles contain that digit. Digits separated by a small white dot are consecutive. These dots are too small for the hippos to care about, so they are not eaten. Not all possible dots are shown.
2656: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every group of 3 cells along a teal line must contain one digit from each modulo 3 group (1, 4, 7), (2, 5, 8), and (3, 6, 9). A digit in a circle counts the number of odd digits on its line. A digit in a square counts the number of even digits on its line. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.
2657: 𝗙𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗼𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗼. Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells. Regions can be upto 9 cells large. Fill each region with the number of cells it contains (eg: fill any 7-cell regions with seven 7s, etc). 𝗔𝗻𝘁𝗶 𝗥𝗼𝘄/𝗖𝗼𝗹𝘂𝗺𝗻. Except for the given 1 in R3C1, the digit N cannot appear in row N or column N. 𝗚𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻 𝗪𝗵𝗶𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀. Orthogonally adjacent digits in different regions must differ by at least 5.
2658: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as a German Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 5). Each cell on the loop represents a skyscraper with a height equal to its value (non-loop cells are not skyscrapers). A digit in a clued cell gives the number of skyscrapers visible in the indicated direction (not including the cell itself), where skyscrapers block the view of skyscrapers with the same or lower height behind them. The clued cell may or may not be on the loop.
2659: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Entering a correct digit will clear the fog in that cell, and maybe some others too. No guessing is required. Spots divide lines into segments. A 'segment total' is the sum of the digits in that segment. Digits may not repeat within a segment. Along a BLUE LINE, each segment has the same total. Along a PINK LINE, all the individual segment totals form a non-repeating consecutive sequence, but the segments can appear in any order (eg: 11, 13, 10, 9, 12.) Along a yellow line, any two segment totals anywhere on the line may not be consecutive or the same (eg: if there is a segment whose cells sum to 12, then no other segment may have a total of 11, 12 or 13.) One of the digits 1-9 (to be determined) is the 'mischief digit.' Every line follows one of the three line rules above, but any line containing the mischief digit has been painted the wrong colour. (Any line NOT containing the mischief digit is the correct colour.)
2660: Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin Yang: Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is fully shaded or fully unshaded. Small numbers in the corners of cells are ‘internal X-Sum’ clues: The digit in a cell with a clue gives the total number of cells (including itself) of the same shading as itself seen in all horizontal/vertical directions combined (cells of the opposite shading block the vision). Those cells sum to the number given by the clue. Digits may repeat within a sum if allowed by other rules.
2661: Normal sudoku rules apply. Renban lines: purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Nabner lines: gold lines contain a non-repeating set of digits, and no two digits on the same line can be consecutive (regardless of their position on the line). Digits in cells with a shaded circle must be odd. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio. (ie One digit will be double the other.)
2662: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the main diagonals may only contain 3 distinct digits. Digits in a Quadruple circle must be placed at least once in the four cells touching that circle. The cell with the gray circle must contain an odd digit.
2663: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into islands of one or more orthogonally connected cells such that no two islands touch each other orthogonally. All non-island cells are in the ocean which must be a contiguous region of orthogonally connected cells that never completely fills a 2x2 area. Each black dot connects 2 island cells. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio. Each white dot connects an ocean and island cell. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Each island contains exactly 3 different digits (with potential repeats), with the highest digit being equal to the island’s size.
2664: Digits do not repeat in cages, and sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Each row, column and region contains the digits 1-9 once each. The smallest digit in each cage counts the number of different regions that enter that cage.
2665: Normal sudoku rules apply. Purple lines (“Renban”) contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Digits do not repeat in cages, and sum to the small clue in the top left corner if given. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb to the tip. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio ie one digit will be double the other. Along green lines, adjacent digits must differ by at least 5. Each constraint type may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g. ALL renban cells must contain no repeated digits, ALL cells connected by a black dot must contain no repeated digits etc.
2666: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in dynamic fog. Correctly placed digits may remove fog from other cells. Guessing is not required. German Whispers: Along green lines, digits must differ from their neighbours by at least 5. Killer: Digits do not repeat in cages, and sum to the small clue in the top left corner if given. Renban: Purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Parity: Along a peach line, adjacent digits must alternate between odd and even. Kropki: Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio. Each constraint type may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g. ALL renban cells must contain no repeated digits, ALL cells connected by a kropki dot must contain no repeated digits etc.
2667: Normal sudoku rules apply. Kropki: Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other). Killer: Digits do not repeat in cages, and sum to the small clue in the top left corner if given. Thermo: Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb to the tip. Dutch Whispers: Along orange lines, digits must differ from their neighbors by at least 4. German Whispers: Along green lines, digits must differ from their neighbors by at least 5. Parity: Along a red line, adjacent digits must alternate between odd and even. Each constraint type above may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g. If one Thermo contains a 5, then no other Thermo may contain a 5 etc. The grid is partially covered in fog. Correctly placing digits will clear the fog around that cell. No guessing is required.
2668: The rules for each puzzle are different so read them carefully for each sudoku you attempt :)
2669: Normal sudoku rules apply, but strange things are afoot.. Creatures of the night have invaded the land! Each row, column and box contains one creature, marked by a coloured dot. All creatures are marked. Cells containing a creature ‘index’ either the row, column or 3x3 box number (read in normal reading order) they're placed in. Each number assigned to a creature is unique and can't be repeated. Marked by a green dot, zombies have an infectious bite ie orthogonally adjacent cells are even when the zombie's number is even, or odd when the zombie's number is odd. Marked by a grey dot, poltergeists throw everything into disarray ie orthogonally adjacent cells are either all higher than the poltergeist's number, or all lower. Marked by an orange dot, horsemen have a knight's reach ie Cells a chess-knight's move away from the horseman can't contain the same digit as the horseman's number. Marked by a red dot, vampires suck the power from their victims ie Orthogonally adjacent cells sum up to the vampire's number. The land is covered in fog. Placing correct digits will lift the fog. No guessing is required. The monster under your bed will know if you cheat!
2670: Normal sudoku rules apply. Magic Squares: red cages are magic squares where the row, column and main diagonals all add up to the same number. Digits in a magic square cannot repeat. Dutch Whisper Lines: two cells connected by an orange line must have a difference of at least 4. Fog: the grit is partly covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog. No guessing is required.
2671: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a grey palindrome line read the same forwards and backwards. The lines do not bend, diverge or cross each other. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog. No guessing is required.
2672: Pick five digits from 1-9. Place those five digits in each row, column and box. Cells a chess-king's move away from a cell marked by a star cannot contain the same digit. A digit on a grey square is even. Digits connected by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.
2673: Pick five digits from 1-9. Place those five digits in each row, column and box. Starting from the bulb, digits on a grey (slow) thermometer must either increase or stay the same. Digits can never decrease.Digits connected by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Digits connected by a red dot are in a 1:3 ratio.
2674: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie Place the digits 1-9 exactly once each in every row, column and 3x3 box). The 3x3 box borders divide blue lines into segments. The digits on each segment of the same line must sum to the same total. The sum of the digits along an arrow must equal the digit in that arrow’s circle.
2675: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits a King's move (in chess) apart must be different. Black dots indicate digits in a 1:2 ratio, white dots consecutive digits. Not all dots are necessarily given.
2676: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid starts mostly covered in fog. Placing some correct digits will cause the fog to be removed from some cells of the grid, revealing clues in those cells. Not all correct digits will reveal fog, and the fog may be anywhere in the grid. Digits on a line must be strictly between the digits placed in the circles at the ends of that line. Each line may only pass straight through a cell or have 90 degree turns. Lines may not cross or overlap, though may share circles at their ends. Each Between Line has a unique colour, though the circles are all the same colour as they may be shared. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 2:1 ratio.
2677: LATIN SQUARE - Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row and column. LATIN SQUARES - Subdivide the grid into smaller latin squares, which can be any size except 1×1. An N×N latin square contains exactly N unique digits selected from 1 to 9 (such that those N unique digits do not repeat in any row/column of their latin square). Latin squares with the same size may not have the same digit in the same relative position. (Eg if a 4×4 latin square has a 7 in its upper left corner, no other 4×4 latin square may have a 7 in its upper left corner). Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle.
2678: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row, column and 3x3 box.) Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. Any horizontal or vertical threesome within a 3x3 box must not consist of three consecutive digits in some order.
2679: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a Quadruple circle must be placed at least once in the four cells touching that circle. The sum of the digits on a line between two circles is equal to the sum of the digits in the circles at either end of the line.
2680: Chiki the Monkey has taken the forbidden bargain! He has obtained immortality and vast wealth but will forever be hunted by a snail assassin who will draw ever closer. Help keep Chiki alive while he collects his earnings and settles in for the night. Fill the 9×9 grid so that every row, column and marked 3×3 box contains the digits 1-9 without repeats. Mangoes separate two consecutive digits, while Coconuts separate two digits where one is double the other. Not all fruit has been given. Draw a path for Chiki through the centre of grid cells, towards the feast of fruit awaiting him. Chiki may move orthogonally or diagonally — if there is room to do so —but may not revisit or cross his own path, nor can he pass through any bright blue maze walls. The snail that hunts him has spoiled one of the digits in the grid. This forbidden digit — the "poison digit" — must be avoided at all costs. Chiki's path is separated by box borders into segments; each segment acts as a "thermometer" and must strictly increase numerically from where he enters (the "bulb") to where he leaves (the "tip"). Chiki must collect ALL Golden Coins, which represent an almost complete set of the digits 1-9 (excepting, of course, the poison digit). These must also be collected in numerical order, starting low and ending high. You may think this task trivial but do not become overconfident, for there's yet one problem...decoy snail. Decoy snails are safe to cross, of course, but what if it isn't a decoy...?
2681: Normal sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column, and 3x3 box). Any cell that is orthogonally adjacent to a cell containing a digit 2 also has a value of 2. Values in a cage sum to the value in the top left corner. Digits may not repeat in a cage, but values may. Nabner Lines: Values on a yellow line may not be the same or consecutive with any other value on the line.
