2682: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on an orange line must have a difference of at least 4. All outside cells on a clue must contain a digit. That digit must also appear in the Nth position looking into the grid in the row/column, where N is the digit in the first position.
2683: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells of the grid in two different colors, such that there is exactly one cell of each color in every row, column and box. Digits don't repeat within the same color. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the digits between the two colored cells in that row or column.
2684: Normal sudoku rules apply. One of the digits from 1-9 (to be determined) is always given its negative value in the grid. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with digits that sum to the same value. Adjacent digits on a green line have values that differ by at least 5. Cells separated by a V have values that sum to 5.
2685: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a circle indicates the number of times that digit appears in either a circle or a square. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle.
2686: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
2691: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a purple (REN) line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. Along a peach (ENT) line, no digit can be within 2 cells of a digit of the same entropic class [High (789), Middle (456), or Low (123)].
2692: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits on each arrow equals the digit in the circled cell. Each digit in the grid represents the height of the skyscraper in each cell. A digit outside the grid indicates the number of skyscrapers seen from the corresponding direction. Taller skyscrapers conceal smaller ones.
2693: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the gray lines must have values in between the values of the digits in the attached circles. (There is a line connecting the circles in r1c1 and r1c4, and a separate line connecting the circles in r1c4 and r4c4. Also there is a line connecting the circles in r1c6 and r1c9, and a separate line connecting the circles in r1c9 and r4c9). The sum of the digits along each red line is equal to the sum of the digits in the attached circles. Cells separated by a V sum to five.
2694: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw 4 snakes, moving orthogonally through the grid. Snakes may not move diagonally, branch, enter cages, cross themselves, or share cells with each other. But they may touch themselves and each other in any way they like. Each circled digit lies at one end of a snake, and indicates how many marked 3x3 boxes that snake visits. Digits in a cage sum to the clue in the corner (if one is given.) Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Each snake follows ONE AND ONLY ONE of the four rules below (breaking all the other rules at least once.) Each snake follows a different rule. • ALTERNATING PARITY: Digits along the snake alternate between odd and even. • GERMAN WHISPER: Adjacent digits have a difference of at least 5. • PALINDROME: The snake reads the same in either direction. • NON-VENOMOUS: No pair of adjacent digits anywhere along the snake sum to exactly the 'venom value'. The venom value (which is the same for any snake) is to be deduced.
2695: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Adjacent digits on an orange line differ by at least 4. A purple line contains a set of distinct and consecutive digits in any order. Digits increase on a thermo from the bulb. Adjacent digits on a red line differ in parity. A black dot joins digits in a 1:2 ratio; a white dot joins consecutive digits.
2696: Place a digit from 1-8 in every cell such that a digit does not appear twice in a row, column, 2x4 box. Cells separated by a single king’s move cannot contain the same digit. The diagram shows a Chess game after 5.0 moves (5 white moves and 5 black moves); draw lines representing each move that has been made up to this point; all lines are straight except any representing a knight's move (which is represented as a single line that moves two orthogonal steps in one direction followed by one step in a perpendicular direction); all lines are considered distinct from each other, even if they share cells with other lines. The lines representing the odd-numbered moves (i.e. each player's 1st, 3rd and 5th moves) are Region Sums Lines ie 2x4 box borders divide a Region Sums Line into segments, whose digits have the same sum. The lines representing even-numbered moves are Renban Lines (ie dgits on a Renban Line form a non-repeating consecutive set). Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
2697: Normal sudoku rules apply. All cages have a small “clue” in the leftmost cell of the top row that the cage occupies. Digits in a cage must not repeat and must sum to that cage’s clue. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other). The grid is partially covered in fog. The fog will clear from surrounding cells when a digit is placed correctly. No guessing is required.
2698: The grid is partially covered in fog. The fog will clear from surrounding cells when a digit is placed correctly. There are nine 3x3 regions in the grid which have to be located – each contains the digits 1-9. No row or column can repeat a digit. A clue outside the grid indicates how many cells belong to regions in the direction pointed to, and those cells must sum to a multiple of the clue. A digit in a cell with arrows indicate the sum of the digits in the cells N steps away in the directions pointed to, where N is the digit in the cell with the arrows. Empty cells do not contribute to the “steps”-count. A black dot separates digits with a 1:2 ratio.
2699: Normal sudoku rules apply. 1) Digits on a purple Renban (RB) line form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits. 2) The 3x3 box borders divide blue Region Sum (RS) lines into segments with the same sum. 3) Neighbouring digits on a green German Whisper (GW) line must have a difference if at least 5. 4) Neighbouring digits on a red line (P) must alternate parity. 5) Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other). 6) Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. 7) Cells with a grey square contain an even digit. Each constraint type may contain no repeated digits anywhere in this puzzle. Eg. If one renban line contains a 5, then no other renban line may contain a 5. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid.
2700: Normal sudoku rules apply. A) Neighbouring digits on a green German Whisper (GW) line must have a difference of at least 5. B) Neighbouring digits on an orange Dutch Whisper (DW) line must have a difference of at least 4. C) Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. D) Along purple zipper (Z) lines, pairs of digits equidistant from the centre of the line have the same sum. On odd-length zipper lines, this sum is the value of the digit in the central position. E) Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the clue in the top left of that cage (if given). Each constraint type may contain no repeated digits anywhere in this puzzle. Eg. If 2 appears on a GW line then no other 2 may appear on any GW line in the puzzle. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid.
2701: Normal sudoku rules apply. Constraints: A) Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle; B) Neighbouring digits on a green German Whisper line (GW) must have a difference of at least 5; C) Digits on a purple Renban line (RB) form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits; D) Grey Ten-lines (T) must be divided into non-overlapping segments each of which sums to 10; E) Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other). Each constraint type may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. Eg. If one renban line contains a 5, then no other renban line may contain a 5. Digits cannot repeat on the positive (SW-NE) diagonal. Digits cannot repeat on the negative (NW-SE) diagonal. Digits cannot repeat in cells with blue squares. Cells with an opaque grey circle contain odd digits. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid.
2702: Normal sudoku rules apply. Between Lines: digits along a line must have values strictly between the digits in the attached circles.
2706: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie Place the digits 1-9 so that they do not repeat in any row, column, or 3x3 box). Zombie Cages: Digits in cages must sum to the number in the initial top-left corner, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. ALL cages must grow by at least one orthogonally connected cell (and could grow by more than one!). Different cages cannot share cells.
2707: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat along the indicated diagonals. 5s live in Dutch Flats: All 5s in the grid must have a '1' directly above it or a '9' directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both. If a digit is in a Circle, exactly that many instances of that digit must appear in Circles. 5s live in Dutch Flats, they don't live in Circles.
2708: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column, and 3x3 box). The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments. The digits on each segment of the same line must sum to the same total. (Eg r2c7=r2c6+r3c5=r4c5).
2709: Normal sudoku rules apply. Escape from the diamond vault by finding a path from the ventilation shaft (r9c9) to the door (r2c1). Your path may only move orthogonally, and may not visit any cell more than once. You may not pass through any coloured display plinths. Also, stepping on any floor tiles with an even digit will trigger the alarms, so don't do that. The digit on a diamond equals the sum of the digits on all the keys that match its plinth colour (and letter). No two diamonds have the same digit. Discover these diamond digits to steal them, and find the path to escape the room. You have 45 minutes!
2710: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey line is a bulb-less thermometer. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb to the tip. The solver must deduce where each thermometer's bulb is - it will always be at one end of the line.
2711: Normal sudoku rules apply. Help Croakz to chase the fly by drawing his path from water lily to water lily! The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself or pass through any sharp rocks (the thick grey walls). As well as moving orthogonally, Croakz may move diagonally — if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so — but may never pass diagonally through rounded rock on the corner of a cell. The grid contains nine (9) water lilies that must ALL be part of the path (of which you must determine the order). No water lily may contain the same digit. Digits separated by a brown twig sum to 5. Digits separated by a leaf have a difference of at least 5. Digits separated by a round frog egg have a 1:2 ratio. Water lilies divide Croakz' path into "split pea" segments. A segment between two water lilies must sum to a two-digit number formed by both digits. For example, if the water lilies containing the digits 1 and 2 are joined by a segment, that segment must sum to either 12 or 21. The segment from Croakz' starting position to the first water lily must sum to the digit on that water lily — this includes the digit on Croakz' starting position itself.
2712: Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row and column. Cells outside the grid are for note-taking if desired. INDIVIDUALITY: No two bricks have the same digits (regardless of order). COMMONALITY: A brick's commonality is the number of bricks that have the same sum (including itself). A circled digit on a brick shows its commonality. An inequality symbol points to the less common brick.
2713: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with the same sum.
2714: Normal sudoku rules apply. The lavender lines are zipper lines. Each pair of digits equidistant from the centre digit has a sum equal to that centre digit. For instance, 16827 would be a valid fill for a zipper line because 8 = 1 + 7 = 6 + 2. The darker off-green kind-of-unpleasant-looking lines are modular lines. Each set of three adjacent digits along a modular line must contain one of 147, one of 258, and one of 369.
2715: Normal sudoku rules apply. Lines are special region sum lines. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with the same sum. Additionally, digits on such a line may not repeat.
2716: Each unique clue type listed below cannot contain more than one instance of each of the digits 1-9. Clue types: a) Neighbouring digits on a green German Whisper (GW) line must have a difference of at least 5; b) Every set of three sequential cells on a mint modular (MO) line must contain one digit from (1,4,7), one digit from (2,5,8), and one digits from (3,6,9); c) Neighbouring digits on an orange Dutch Whisper (DW) line must have a difference of at least 4. (DW); d) Neighbouring digits on a red parity (P) line must alternate parity (odd/even); e) Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the clue in the top left of that cage (if given); f) Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other); g) Cells with a grey square contain an even digit; h) Cells with a grey circle contain an odd digit. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid.
2717: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 5 in the grid must have a 1 directly above it or a 9 directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both. The grid is covered in fog. Entering correct digits might clear fog somewhere in the grid. A stick always has a lower total (the sum of its digits) than any stick which lies on top of it. Sticks that aren't grey have an additional rule: A yellow ENTROPIC stick must contain one low digit (1, 2 or 3), one medium digit (4, 5 or 6), and one high digit (7, 8 or 9.); a teal MODULAR stick must contain one digit from each of the sets (1,4,7), (2,5,8), and (3,6,9); a pink RENBAN stick must contain a set of consecutive digits – these can be arranged in any order; along an orange DUTCH WHISPER stick, adjacent digits must have a difference of at least 4; along a red PARITY STICK, digits must alternate between odd and even.
2718: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the total shown. A clue outside the grid is the sum of the digits between two ‘crusts’ in that row/column. The crusts are determined by the row or column the clue is. For example, if the clue is in row 2 then the sandwich crusts are 2 and 8; if the clue is in column 7 then the sandwich crusts are 7 and 3 (the crusts will sum to 10). All sandwich fillings are in their own Killer Cages.
2719: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits inside each cage is equal to the small number in the top left corner. Each purple line contains a pair of consecutive digits. Digits in cells separated by a V sum to 5. Digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10. All possible Vs and Xs are given (i.e. there are no Vs)!
2720: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages with the same letter sum to the same value. These values are to be determined by the solver. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order.
2721: Normal sudoku rules apply. Dynamic Fog: The letter has been partially smudged this time and digits may or may not reveal more clues. Digits on the tail of an arrow sum to the digit in the bulb. All bulbs are visible from the start. If a line heads towards a cell, it enters that cell. They are snipped so they can't been seen through smudge. Adjacent digits on a green line must differ by at least 5. Adjacent digits on a red line must have an even and odd digit. For every 3 adjacent digits on a peach line, one must be from the set {1, 2, 3}, one from {4, 5, 6} and one from {7, 8, 9}. For every 3 adjacent digits on a teal line, one must be from the set {1, 4, 7}, one from {2, 5, 8} and one from {3, 6, 9}. Digits on a blue line must sum to the same value for each box it enters.
2722: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits a chess knight’s move apart cannot contain the same digit. Box borders divide the blue line into segments which each have the same sum. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.
2723: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages do not repeat and sum to value in the upper left corner. All cages sum to 19. Digits cannot repeat along the positive diagonal; digits cannot repeat along the negative diagonal. (Both are marked with a blue line). Adjacent digits on a green line must differ by at least 5.
2724: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the top left corner. On an index line, the digit in the Nth cell along the line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. Eg: 3214 would be a valid line; the 1st digit, 3, indicates that the 3rd digit is a 1, and so on.
2725: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. The first correctly placed digit on each constraint will remove fog from other cells. Each constraint type may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g. If one cell on a parity line contains a 5, then no other cell on a parity line may contain a 5. Constraints: a) Along a red line, adjacent digits must alternate between odd and even; b) Digits do not repeat in cages, and sum to the small clue in the top left corner if given; c) digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); d) pairs of digits equidistant from the centre of a lavender zipper line must sum to the digit in the middle of that line (noted by a dot); e) digits along a thermometer increase from bulb to tip; f) a cell with arrows pointing inward must be smaller than all other cells that share its edge; and g) a digit in a grey square is even. Each listed constraint type appears at least once in the puzzle.
2726: Normal sudoku rules apply. 3x3 box borders divide a blue stick into segments. Each segment along a stick has the same sum. This segment sum can be different for different sticks. A stick always has a lower total (the sum of ALL its digits) than any stick which lies on top of it.
2727: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as a parity line: digits along the loop must alternate between even and odd digits. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's bulb, and all bulbs are on the loop. Additionally, arrow tips point towards a cell containing the digit within the arrow's bulb, and this cell with the pointed-to digit is also on the loop. The digit in the arrow tip indicates the distance from the arrow tip to the pointed-to cell. There may be other instances of the same digit between this cell and the arrow tip.
2728: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in its circle.
2729: Normal sudoku rules apply. CHESS SUMS - A digit on a chess piece is the sum of the digits in cells the chess piece could move to in a single move. Bishops and kings can only move to cells in the same 3x3 box, but knights can jump into other boxes. Fog covers part of the grid. Placing a correct digit will clear fog.
2730: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits increase from the bulb to the end of each thermometer.
2731: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the grey lines must have values in between the values of the digits in the attached circles. Adjacent digits in each row of the puzzle have a difference of at least four.
2732: Normal sudoku rules apply. Top Right Boi's Path: Draw a path of orthogonally connected cells from Top Right Boi in row 9 column 1 to his home in row 1 column 9. The path may not touch itself, not even diagonally. Other than his starting position, Top Right Boi MUST NEVER visit the bottom left corner of any 3x3 box. Conversely, Top Right Boi MUST visit the top right corner of every 3x3 box before returning home. The 9 top right corner cells in the grid must all contain different digits. As the bottom left corner cells are lawless wastelands, there is no such restriction on their digits. Any cell Top Right Boi visits will have it's value modified to be equal to Top Right Boi's current value, regardless of the digit in that cell. When Top Right Boi visits a cell in the top right corner of a 3x3 box, his value changes to be the digit in that cell, and will remain as that value until the next top right corner cell he visits (For clarity, this means that all top right corner cells have their digits as their values). Because Top Right Boi is beginning his journey from the horrid bottom left of the grid, his value will be 0 until he reaches the first top right corner cell along the path. Cells not on the path retain the value of their digits. Cages: Values in a cage must sum to the number in the top right corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage, but values may. Kropki: If two values are separated by a black dot, one is double the other. If two values are separated by a white dot, they are consecutive. XV: If two values are separated by an X, they sum to 10. If two values are separated by a V, they sum to 5. Not all possible Kropkis or XVs are necessarily shown.
2733: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a lines do not repeat and sum to the indicated value. Each line contains a unique collection of digits. Digits in cages do not repeat.
2734: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells that share a border never contain consecutive digits. In every 3x3 box, digits separated by a single knight's move (in chess) have a greatest common divisor of 1. (So, for example, 2 and 4 could not be so separated as they have a divisor of 2.)
2737: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each marked circle is either a Killer Quad OR a normal Quadruple, with each to be determined by the solver. In a Killer Quad, digits surrounding a circle must sum to the indicated total. In a Quadruple, digits marked in a circle must appear in its surrounding cells.
2738: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in cages. If the sum of a cage is a 1-digit number, that number must be in the cell pointed at by the cage's northwest corner. If the sum is a 2-digit number, it must be in the domino formed by that cell and the one to its left. (Example: if the sum of the cage in Box 3 was 9, then r1c6 would be 9. If it's sum was 12, then r1c5 would be 1 and r1c6 would be 2.) Every set of 4 adjacent digits on a peach line must contain a digit from each of the X-pair (ten-pair) subsets of {1,9}, {2,8}, {3,7}, and {4,6}. A 5 may not appear on a peach line. Digits on a line may repeat if allowed by other rules.
2739: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Digits in a cage must sum to the value indicated in the top left corner.
2740: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shadow sums: A clue outside the grid gives the sum of all numbers in that row/column which are smaller than the number immediately before them, when reading from the direction of the clue.
2741: Normal sudoku rules apply. A number outside the grid gives the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row or column. Digits placed on a purple line must be a non-repeating set of consecutive digits, in any order.
2742: Normal sudoku rules apply. A cage's product (the result of multiplying its digits together) exactly equals the number of cages with that product. Note: if a cage has only one digit, that digit is considered to be the cage's product.
2743: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the circled cell.
2744: Normal sudoku rules apply. No two instances of the same constraint type may share digits. So, although digits may repeat on a clue, they may NOT repeat across different occurrences of that clue type. Eg if an arrow has the digit X, X may repeat along that arrow, but X may not appear on any other arrow. Clue types: 1) Quadruples: In an orange circle, the question mark contains the set of all the (possibly repeating) digits appearing in the surrounding cells. 2) Renban: Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order. 3) Arrows: Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. 4) White dot: Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. 5) Black dot: Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other).
2745: Normal sudoku rules apply. All thermometers are slow thermos. Digits must increase or stay the same on each step from the bulb to the tip.
2746: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some cells in the grid contain a given digit, and these have all been circled. A circled given digit indicates how many times that digit appears as a circled given digit in the grid. Unfortunately, most of these given digits are obscured by fog. Entering a correct digit will clear the fog in that cell, and maybe other cells too. No guessing is necessary. A black dot sits between two digits where one is double the other. The two digit number to be discovered in the blue frame (reading left to right) will indicate the total number of circled given digits that exist in the grid.
2747: Normal sudoku rules apply. There are ten lines in the grid. Each of these lines contains digits that sum to 10.
2748: Normal sudoku rules apply. Mod-3 Rows: Each row in the puzzle is a mod-3 line. That is, any set of three horizontally adjacent digits must contain one digit from (1,4,7), one digit from (2,5,8), and one digit from (3,6,9). 159 Indexing: Digits in columns 1, 5, and 9 indicate the column in which the digits 1, 5, or 9 (respectively) appears in that row. (Eg if r4c5 is an 8 then r4c8 is a 5 as the 5 must appear in the 8th column). Renban: Each purple line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Little Killer: Digits along the positive diagonal sum to a value that is (strictly) less than 24.
2749: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grey regions contain the same digits in the same arrangement without rotation or reflection. The digits in a cage sum to the number given in the cage.
2750: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide the blue line into segments. Digits on each segment along the blue line have the same sum. The digit in a red cell gives the placement of that cell's column number in its row (i.e. if row 6, column 5 contained a 9, that would place a 5 in row 6, column 9). The digit in a blue cell gives the placement of that cell's row number in its column (i.e. if row 6, column 4 contained a 9, that would place a 6 in row 9, column 4). Digits in cells with Stars are odd.
2751: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear fog from surrounding cells. 𝗖𝗮𝘃𝗲: Shade some cells such that all unshaded cells form a single orthogonally connected region and all shaded cells are connected to the edge of the grid. Digits in circles either give the size of the shaded region in which it lies or the total number of unshaded cells which can be seen in all directions from the unshaded circled cell, including the cell itself. Shaded cells block vision. 𝗟𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁: Some circled cells are endpoints of lines in the grid. All lines move orthogonally. Lines do not cross or branch, except at circled cells. The digit in a circle gives the total number of cells along each line attached to the circle of the same shading as the circled cell, including the endpoints. 𝗦𝗽𝗹𝗶𝘁 𝗣𝗲𝗮𝘀: Digits along a line strictly between two circles must sum to a two-digit number, where the tens digit is in one circle and the ones digit is in the other. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Not all X or V are given.
2752: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. The digits in a cage sum to the value indicated. There are circles in the grid connected by lines. The digits on the lines must be strictly in-between the digits in the circles. For the red and blue Between Lines, all circles connect across to both ends on the opposite side (e.g. r4c3 connects to both r4c7 AND r6c7).
2753: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. Orthogonally adjacent cells cannot contain consecutive digits. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least five. The digits along a grey arrow line sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle.
2755: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and sum to the given total. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the circle. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb to the tip.
2756: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. The middle 3x3 box is a magic square; each row, column, and 3-cell diagonal of this box all have the same sum. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the arrow's bulb.
2757: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a red line must alternate between prime (2,3,5,7) and composite (4,6,8,9). The digit 1 is neither prime nor composite. The digits in each cage form a prime number when read rightwards or downwards. Digits in the circle must appear within the surrounding four cells. Digits in cells joined by a white dot must be consecutive and digits in cells joined by a black dot must be in a 2:1 ratio.
2758: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot be a knight's move apart. Adjacent digits may not sum to 5 or 10. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum.
2759: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits do not repeat along a marked blue diagonal. Adjacent digits along an orange line have a difference of at least four. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with the same sum. The central 3x3 box must form a magic square, with the total of each row, column and 3-cell diagonal being equal.
2760: Normal sudoku rules apply. A black dot sits between two digits where one is double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given. The single grey line is a palindrome ie its digits read the same forwards and backwards. Blue lines in the grid are Region Sum Lines ie The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments; each segment along a line has the same sum. (NB Different lines may have different sums). Eg r5c2+r5c3+r6c2+r6c3=r7c2+r8c2=r7c3+r8c3. The salmon coloured lines in the grid are entropic lines ie Any set of three sequential cells along an entropic line must contain a low digit (123), middle digit (456) and high digit (789). Digits may repeat on a line, if allowed by other rules.
2761: Normal sudoku rules apply. A white diamond between two cages means that the difference between their cage totals is equal to the topmost/leftmost digit in the column/row in which that diamond appears. A black diamond between two cages means that the ratio between their cage totals is equal to the topmost/leftmost digit in the column/row in which that diamond appears. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Not all possible diamonds are necessarily given.
2762: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat on a beige hitline. A circled digit on a hitline indicates how many digits match their position number along that line, starting at the end with the square (which is 'position 1'.) Eg: If a line reads 97325, then the 2 would be circled because there are two digits in their correct positions: 3 is in the 3rd position, and 5 is in the 5th position.
2763: Place a digit from 1-9 in each cell such that there are no repeats in any row, column, or box. Cells separated by a single knight’s move (in chess) may not contain the same digit. Adjacent digits on a green line must differ by at least 5. A digit in a red cell indicates the position of its column number within its row. For example, if R2C1 is a 3, then R2C3 is a 1.
2764: Yin-Yang: Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 is entirely shaded or unshaded. Araf: Divide the grid into orthogonally connected regions, each containing exactly two number clues. The number of cells in each region is strictly between its two number clues. 1. Each Araf region is itself a valid Yin-Yang. In other words, all shaded cells within a region are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells within a region are orthogonally connected. 2. In each Araf region, one clue is shaded and one clue is unshaded. 3. One of the clues in an Araf region gives the exact count of shaded cells in its region. This clue may be shaded or unshaded. For answer-check, in all unshaded cells without a given number, enter the size of the Araf region containing that cell. (Enter only the 1s digit for two-digit numbers.)
2765: Normal sudoku rules apply. All lines are both Index Lines and Entropic Lines. Ie Index Lines: The digit in the Nth cell along a line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. Entropic Lines: Any set of three sequential cells along a line must contain a low (1,2,3), middle (4,5,6), and high (7,8,9) digit. Sum Dots: Digits around the brown diamond may repeat and must sum to the given total.in the cage.
2766: Normal sudoku rules apply. There are 9 VAMPIRES (digits 1-9 once each) in the grid; one in every row, column and box. There are also 9 VICTIMS (digits 1-9 once each) in the grid; one in every row, column and box. The value of a vampire cell is the sum of its digit plus the digit of the victim cell in the same box. The value of a victim cell is always 0. The value of a natural cell is its digit. Every cage contains either a vampire or a victim. The total shown for each cage is the sum of the two VALUES of the cells contained therein. Along a green line, adjacent cells must have VALUES that differ by 5 or more.
2767: Normal sudoku rules apply. Chiaroscuro: Shade some cells so that all groups of orthogonally connected shaded cells have an even number of cells and all groups of orthogonally connected unshaded cells have an odd number of cells. Two groups cannot have the same shape and size, counting rotations and reflections as the same. Digits cannot repeat within a Chiaroscuro group. A digit in a circled cell is equal to the size of the Chiaroscuro group which contains that cell. If a cell has a given number in the upper left corner, then the digits in the Chiaroscuro group which contains that cell must sum to that number.
2768: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits within a cage sum to the small number written in the top left of that cage. The sum of the digits along the red line that has two circles as its endpoints must equal to the sum of two digits in both circles. Along the green line, two adjacent digits have the difference of at least 5. Along the grey palindrome line, digits form a sequence that reads the same backwards as it does forwards. Along each teal line, the set of three sequential cells must contain one digit from set {1,4,7}, one digit from set {2,5,8} and one digit from set {3,6,9}. A black dot sits between two digits where one is double the other, while two digits connected by a white dot have difference of 1. Not all black dots and white dots are given.
2769: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a small white circle indicates how many times that digit appears in small white circles in the puzzle. 3x3 box borders divide blue lines into segments; the digits on each segment must have the same sum. (Different lines may have different sums.)
2770: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each main diagonal must contain all of the digits 1 to 9, once each. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
2771: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid contains nine "three-sum" cells, one in each row, column, and 3x3 box. Each digit from 1-9 is a "three-sum" exactly once. “Three-sum” digits count as their nominal value increased by 3. For example, a “three-sum” 7 would have a value of 10. The sum of the value of the digits on a line within a box (the line's 'region sum') must be the same for each box that line passes through.
2774: 6x6 sudoku rules apply: each row, column, and 2x3 box must contain all the digits from 1 to 6. A clue outside the grid with an arrow shows the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. A clue outside the grid without an arrow shows the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 6 in the row or column.
2775: Place the digits 1-6 once each in each row, column and 2x3 box. Digits on a thick grey line read the same in either direction. Digits on a thin line must be strictly between the digits placed in the circles at the ends of that line. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.
2776: Place the digits 1-6 in each row, column and 2x3 box without repetition. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat (if allowed by other rules). Digits in a dotted cage sum to the given total. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
2777: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer digits increase from the bulb. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal. Digits in a cage sum to the indicated total. Digits on an arrow sum to the total in the connected circle. Cells shown in grey contain the same digit. Cells separated by a black dot are a 1:2 ratio.
2778: Place each of the digits 1-8 in every row, column and 2x4 box without repetition. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. If a number is shown, that is the sum of the cage. Digits separated by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
2779: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit inside a white circle must appear in one of the four cells surrounding that circle. Digits in columns 1, 5, and 9 indicate the column in which the digit 1, 5, or 9 (respectively) appears in that row. Eg if the r4c1 is a 6 then, in row 4, the 1 must appear in the 6th column (ie r4c6).
2780: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the value shown in the upper left corner of the cage. Each line in the puzzle is EXACTLY TWO of modular, entropic, or parity. Modular Lines: Any set of three adjacent digits along a modular line has three different remainders when divided by 3. Entropic lines: Any set of three adjacent cells along an entropic line must contain a low digit (123), a middle digit (456), and a high digit (789). Parity Lines: Digits along parity lines alternate odd/even.
2781: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits inside each cage is equal to the small number in the top left corner and digits cannot repeat within a cage. The sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in that arrow’s circle.
2782: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages may not repeat and must sum to the given total in the top left corner.
2783: Normal 6 by 6 rules apply. Refer to each puzzle for specific rules.
2784: Normal sudoku rules apply. Renban: Pink lines must contain a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order. German Whispers: The digits in adjacent cells along green lines must differ by at least 5. Digits can repeat on green lines if allowed by other rules.
2785: Normal sudoku rules apply. Anti-king: Cells that are diagonally adjacent may not contain the same digit. Dynamic Fog: The grid is mostly covered in fog. Correctly placing digits will reveal the fog in that cell and possibly other cells. Parity Parity: Beneath the fog is a checkerboard pattern of yellow and blue cells. Each digit appears in one of the colors exactly as many times as its value. For example, 7 will appear either exactly seven times in blue or exactly seven times in yellow.
2786: Pick six digits from 1-9. Place those six digits in each row, column and marked region. Digits on a yellow line form a Fibonacci sequence. The line starts with a small digit followed by a consecutive digit. From there, every next digit will be the sum of the previous two digits. For example, 1-2-3-5-8 or 4-5-9 are both valid.
2787: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Each pink line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, which can appear in any order. Each gray line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. These groups of cells cannot overlap; every cell is part of exactly one group. Lines may share endpoints, but otherwise don't overlap.
2788: Normal sudoku rules apply. Quadruples: Digits in circles must appear at least once in the four surrounding cells.
2789: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Correctly placing a digit will clear any fog in its own cell, and potentially clear fog in other cells too. Each row, column, and 3x3 region contains exactly one given digit whose exact location is to be deduced. No two givens are identical digits, i.e. each of the digits 1 to 9 is given exactly once. A clue outside a row or column indicates the sum of all digits up to the given digit (the given digit itself is not included in the sum). Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the circle from which the arrow emerges. Digits joined by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive.
2790: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line is divided into multiple segments, with the divisions at each point where the line changes region or enters/exits the grid. On a given line, each segment has the same sum (different lines may have different sums). Numbers on lines outside the grid (to be determined) are Hitpoints clues: a clue's value equals the sum of all digits in that row/column which equal their distance from the clue.
2791: Normal 6x6 Sudoku rules apply. ie Place the digits 1-6, once each, in every row, column and 2x3 rectangle. Draw a path along interior gridlines from the robot to the exit. The path cannot touch itself. The robot computes the difference between each pair of digits it passes between, and writes these differences to the grey memory cells in reading order. (All memory cells must be written to and no difference goes unrecorded).
2795: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end.
2797: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column and 3x3 box). The purple line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. The digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the cage’s top left corner. Digits may not repeat in a cage.
2798: Normal sudoku rules apply (Place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row, column and 3x3 box). Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end.
2799: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog; placing a correct digit will clear the fog in that cell and possibly elsewhere in the grid. Each of the following constraint types may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g., if a parity line contains a 5, then no other parity line cell in the puzzle may contain a 5: 1) Digits in a cage must sum to the total given; 2) Digits joined by an X sum to 10; 3) Adjacent digits along a red parity line (PR) must alternate between odd and even digits; 4) A purple renban line (RB) must contain a set of consecutive digits in any order; 5) A yellow nabner line (NB) must contain a set of nonconsecutive digits in any order; 6) Any set of three digits along an orange entropic line (ENT) line must contain one digit from each of the following sets: 123; 456; 789; 7) Any set of three digits along a teal modular line (MOD) must contain one digit from each of the following sets: 147; 258; 369; 8) Pairs of digits equidistant from the centre of a pink zipper line (ZIP) must sum to the digit in the centre of that line, notated by a small circle. Lines in the puzzle never intersect or share cells.
2800: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single snaking line connecting two particular cells (to be discovered) which forms a palindrome, ie; its sequence of digits reads the same in either direction. The palindrome line should pass through the centres of cells, and may move both orthogonally and diagonally, but may not branch or cross itself. A digit on an arrow indicates how many cells it sees (in the indicated direction) that are NOT ON the palindrome. The arrow cell itself is not included in the count. Digits in a cage do not repeat, and the clue in the top left corner indicates the total of any digits in the cage that are NOT ON the palindrome.
2801: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages do not repeat, and sum to the small clue, if given. Grey circles contain 1 or 9. One grey loop is Entropic, one is German Whisper, and one is Region Sum; the solver must determine which is which. Entropic: every 3 cells along the line contain one low digit {123}, one middly digit {456}, and one high digit {789}. German Whisper: adjacent cells along the line differ by at least 5. Region Sum: box borders divide the line into segments with the same sum.
2802: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 2-cell red or blue line can be read as a square number in one direction or the other (eg 25 or 52). The central grey cell is also a square number.
2803: Latin Square rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row and column). The grid is covered in a checkerboard pattern of yellow and blue cells. Each digit appears in one of the colours exactly as many times as its value. For example, 7 will appear either exactly seven times in blue or exactly seven times in yellow. Digits may not repeat along any negative diagonal (those going from the top left to the bottom right). Cells separated by a single knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits in grey circles must be odd.
2804: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in adjacent cells separated by a white dot differ by exactly 1. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by 5 or more. The digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.
2805: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells a king's move apart are not allowed to contain identical digits. The digit in the central cell of each box is less than or equal to the box number. Boxes are numbered in normal reading order. Each horizontal 3x1 region that is completely contained in a single box sums to the same value. Each vertical 1x3 region that is completely contained in a single box sums to the same value. The digit in the top-left cell and the digit in the bottom-right cell of the grid sum to 3.
2806: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a black circle must appear in one of the four cells touching that circle. A digit in a blue circle indicates how many blue circles contain that digit. Digits along a pink circle form a non-repeating consecutive sequence. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
2807: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the attached circle. Digits do not repeat along each of the indicated diagonals.
2808: Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie Place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row, column and 3x3 box). Penrose Lines: On a pink line, a sequence of increasing digits repeats from the bulb end. The sequence must fully complete and repeat at least once (and, each time it repeats, it must repeat fully). For example, along a penrose line, digits could read: 137137137.
2809: Divide the grid into eight non-overlapping 2x4 regions, which can each be placed either horizontally or vertically. It must be determined which one of the digits 1-9 is missing from the grid. The other eight digits should each appear once in every row, column and region. RENBAN (pink) - digits along the pink line form a non-repeating consecutive set, which can appear in any order. NABNER (yellow) - no two digits on the yellow line may be consecutive (or the same.) REGION SUM (darker blue) - on the blue line, digits in each region have the same total. GERMAN WHISPER (green) - adjacent digits on the green line must have a difference of at least 5. PARITY (red) - digits on the red line must alternate between odd and even. PALINDROME (grey) - the string of digits on the grey line reads the same in either direction. SAME DIFFERENCE (turquoise) - each pair of adjacent digits on a turquoise line has the same difference. This difference value can be different for different turquoise lines. KROPKI - two digits connected by a black dot have a 2:1 ratio (ie one is double the other.)
2810: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line can be divided into one or more segments such that every segment in the grid sums to the same total. (For the avoidiance of doubt, this means that segments from both the 78-cell line and the 2-cell line have the same sum!) The digit in the grey square is even.
2811: Normal sudoku rules apply. The cell with the gray square is even. Every 5 must have a 1 directly above it or a 9 directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both. Digits in column 1 indicate the column in which the digit 1 appears in that row (e.g. if r4c1 is a 6, r4c6 is a 1). The same is true of column 5 and the digit 5, and column 9 and the digit 9. An X between two cells means that the digits in those cells must add up to 10.
2815: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid 'wraps around' (the top connects to the bottom, and the left edge to the right edge). DUTCH CELLMATES: Every digit in the grid needs to have a digit at least 4 greater in the cell below it, or a digit at least 4 smaller in the cell above it. It may have both, but doesn't need both. KILLER CAGES: Cages chained to each other have the same sum.
2816: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every three-cell-segment of a teal modular line contains one digit from the groups {147}, {258} and {369}. The sum of the digits on a thin gray line equals the sum of the digits in the attached circles. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Purple lines contain a set of distinct consecutive digits in any order. Digits in cages do not repeat. Gray circles indicate odd and gray squares even digits. The digits on the MARKed diagonal sum to 60.
2817: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on blue lines can not be between or equal to the digits in the diamonds at the ends of the line. The digits in the diamonds at the ends of a line must differ by at least 4. A diamond terminates a line segment.
2818: Normal sudoku rules apply. German whispers: Adjacent digits on a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits in grey circles must be odd and digits in grey squares must be even. In cells separated by a black dot, one digit must be double the other. Not all dots are given. Renban: Digits placed on purple lines must be a non-repeating set of consecutive digits, in any order. Digits separated by an X must sum to 10. Not all Xs are given.
2819: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each digit in column 1 indicates the position of the 1 in its row. (eg if R5C1 is a 6, then R5C6 is a 1 as the 1 must appear in the 6th position). Column 5 operates the same way for the digit 5; and column 9 for the digit 9. Each digit in row 1 indicates the position of the 1 in its column. (eg if R1C5 is a 6, then R6C5 is a 1). Row 5 operates the same way for the digit 5; and row 9 for the digit 9. On thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Along the marked diagonal, digits must not repeat.
2820: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits must not repeat in cages. Digits on thermometers increase from the bulb end. Digits on lines must be between the digits in the circles on each end. These lines also act as thermometers i.e. digits on lines must increase from the "low" circle to the "high" circle.
2821: Normal sudoku rules apply. The central 3x3 box is a magic square (each row, column and diagonal in that box sum to the same number). Digits on the thermometer increase from the bulb end. Cells connected by a purple line sum to 10. In the cage, digits that are a (chess) king's move apart from other caged digits must not repeat and must not sum to 5, 10 or 15.
2822: Normal sudoku rules apply. Lines contain digits in order with a constant difference (e.g. 1-2-3, 4-6-8, 7-4-1). Lines of the same colour cannot contain repeated digits. Cells separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other).
2823: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide the blue line into segments. Along this blue line, each segment’s digits sum to the same total. The sum of all digits on the blue line and pink line combined is 89. A black dot between two cells indicates that one digit is double the other.
2825: Divide the grid into polyominoes and fill each cell with a number equal to the size of its polyomino. Polyominoes of the same size may not share an edge. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or unshaded. All odd polyominoes are shaded, while all even polyominoes are unshaded. Numbers on cells with an arrow indicate the number of polyominoes of the SAME shading/parity seen in the direction of the arrow. Arrows do not count their own cell, but may count their polyomino if a cell within its polyomino is visible in the direction of the arrow.
2826: Cave: Shade some cells such that all orthogonally connected groups of shaded cells (the wall) touch the edge of the grid, and all unshaded cells (the cave) are orthogonally connected. Suguru: Each orthogonally connected group of shaded (wall) cells contains the digits 1-N (where N is the size of the group). Suguru digits may not repeat in a row, column, or shaded group. Fillomino: Divide unshaded cells into polyominoes and fill each cell with a digit equal to the size of its polyomino. Polyominoes of the same size may not share an edge. All numbers in the puzzle are 1-9. A Fillomino Polyomino may not border a Suguru digit with the same value. An unshaded circled clue indicates the total number of unshaded cells seen in the four orthogonal directions, including the clue cell. A shaded circle clue indicates the size of the shaded region.
2827: Masyu: Draw a closed, non-branching, non-crossing loop along dotted gridlines. The loop must visit all given circles and follow these rules for movements: The loop must turn on black circles, and go straight through at least one vertex on both sides of the turn. The loop must go straight through white circles. It must also turn on at least one of the vertices it visits on either side of the white circle. Gray circles act as either a black or a white circle (the solver must deduce which). Star Battle: The Masyu loop divides the grid into regions. Place exactly one star into each row, column, and region, such that no two stars touch, not even diagonally. For the solution check to work, place a 1 into every cell containing a star in the final grid and a 0 into all other cells.
2828: Normal sudoku rules apply. Nurikabe: Shade some cells (representing water) such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, but never fully cover a 2x2 area. Groups of orthogonally connected unshaded cells form islands. Two separate islands cannot touch one another orthogonally, but may touch diagonally. Digits may not repeat on an island. Each island contains exactly one numbered clue, which gives the product of the sum of the digits on the island and the size (number of cells) of the island, e.g. an island filled with 346 is would have a '39' clue (13x3). A '?' may represent any number (not necessarily single-digit). A cell with arrow(s) may be land or water, and the digit gives the total number of island cells in the indicated directions combined, not including itself. Not all arrows are given.
2829: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat along the indicated diagonal. Numbers outside the grid are simultaneously full rank clues and sandwich clues. A '?' can be any number. Full rank Each complete row and column can be read from both directions to form 36 distinct 9-digit numbers. The clues outside the grid give the rank of the 9-digit number read from that position when all the numbers are ranked from smallest (1) to highest (36). Sandwich: A number outside the grid represents the sum of the digits sandwiched between the '1' and '9' in its respective row or column.
2830: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a marked diagonal cannot repeat. Digits separated by an X sum to ten. Digits separated by a V sum to five. Not all XV pairs are shown. Numbers in a cage must be a perfect square (2-digit cages read left-to-right), and each perfect square can be used only one time.
2831: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.
2835: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat on marked diagonals. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive. Digits joined by a black dot are in a ratio of 2:1.
2836: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers on an arrow sum to the number on the arrow's origin (circle or pill). Pills are read from left to right. Some circles and pills do not have an arrow. Pink pills are the sum of the two pills or circles below them. Digits with a white dot between them are consecutive. Digits with a black dot between them are in a ratio of 2:1.
2837: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers in circles and pills are CONSECUTIVE powers (first power, second power, third power, etc.) of the number in the top circle in each of the three stacks. Numbers in pills are read from left to right. Digits in cages do not repeat and sum to the number shown. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive.
2842: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column. No two 5s in the grid have the same digit in the cell immediately above.
2843: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide the blue Region Sum Lines into segments with the same sum. Gold Palindrome lines must read the same forwards or backwards.
2844: Place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row, column and irregularly-shaped marked nine-cell region. Cells separated by a black dot contain two digits where one digit is double the other. A magic square is a square of NxN cells in which each row, column and both main diagonals sum to the same total. (In this puzzle digits CAN repeat in a magic square.) The entire 9x9 grid is a magic square. In the centre of the 9x9 magic square is a 7x7 magic square. In the centre of that is a 5x5 magic square. And in the very centre is a 3x3 magic square. The dotted lines clarify the positions of the magic squares.
2845: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide a blue line into segments. Each segment along a line has the same sum. (This segment sum can be different for different lines).
2846: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orthogonal neighbours (ie cells sharing an edge) are never consecutive. In the positive diagonals (ie diagonals sloping from SW to NE), the sum of neighbours is at most 11.
2847: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least five. Digits increase from the bulb to the end of the thermometer. A digit in a square counts the number of odd digits (including itself) on its line or thermometer.
2848: ⚠️ We can no longer contain them. The new batch of eggs looks set to hatch within days. Please urgently review studies 1-8 in order to gain vital understanding about these bizarre creatures. All we currently know is that they're always at least two cells long, and seem incapable of moving diagonally. Normal sudoku rules apply. In each puzzle, you must use any rules you learned from the previous puzzle!
2849: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colour each cell in the grid either red or blue, such that no 2×2 square is a single colour and the cells of each colour form a single orthogonally connected region. Every line that passes through at least one red cell is an alternating-parity line (i.e. each pair of consecutive digits along the line must include one even and one odd digit). Every line that passes through at least one blue cell is a region-sum line (i.e. box borders divide the line into segments with equal sums; these sums may vary between lines). Any line that passes through both red and blue cells is also a renban (i.e. it contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order).
2850: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with equal sums (the sum may vary between different lines). The black dot connects two digits, one of which is double the other.
2851: Normal sudoku rules apply. Exactly nine cells in the grid are "rooters". The value of a rooter equals the square root of its digit (in all other cells, the value equals the digit). No two rooters share a row, column, box, or digit. A black dot connects two cells where one value is double the other (not all such dots are necessarily given). Values on thermometers strictly increase from bulb to tip. The sum of the values along an arrow equals the value in the attached circle. Along green lines, neighbouring values differ by at least 5. On each purple line, the set of values consists of consecutive integers in any order. All cages have the same product of values (digits or values may repeat within a cage if allowed by other rules). The grid is partially covered in fog. Entering correct digits may clear some fog (not necessarily beneath or around the entered digit). No guessing is required.
2852: Normal sudoku rules apply. All blue (“+”) cages have the same SUM; all yellow (“×”) cages have the same PRODUCT. Both constants are to be determined by the solver. Digits may repeat within a cage if allowed by sudoku. The grid is partially covered in fog. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. Usually a correct entry will clear its own cell, but not always — some fog is extra dense! No guessing is required.
2853: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as a German Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 5). Cells with small numbers in the corner are on the loop. This number gives the sum of all loop cells (including itself) seen from that cell in all horizontal/vertical directions combined, where non-loop cells block the vision. Digits may repeat in a sum if allowed by other rules.
2854: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along SLOW thermometers digits stay the same or increase as they move away from the bulb.
2855: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide a blue line into segments. Each segment along a line has the same sum. (This segment sum can be different for different lines). Digits on a pink line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order. Adjacent digits on a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle.
2856: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the following constraint types may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle E.g., if an orange line cell contains a 5, then no other orange line cell in the puzzle may contain a 5. Constraint types: 1) A digit in a grey square is even; 2) A digit in a grey circle is odd; 3) For digits in cells separated by a white dot, one must be one greater than the other; 4) For digits in cells separated by a black dot, one must be double the other; 5) Adjacent digits along an orange line must differ by 4 or more.
2857: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a (chess) knight’s move cannot contain the same digit. Any three consecutive cells along a green (modular) line must contain one digit of each residue class modulo 3: {147}, {258} and {369}. Digits joined by a black dot are in 1:2 ratio, digits joined by a white dot are consecutive, and digits joined by a green dot are both in the same residue class modulo 3.
2858: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the slow thermometer line increase or stay the same starting from its only bulb. The position of the single bulb is to be determined and it is on one of the cells marked with circles.
2859: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells a chess knight's move apart may not contain the same digit. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive. All possible white dots are given. Digits joined by a V sum to 5. All such pairs are given. The grey line is a palindrome: its digits read the same in either direction.
2860: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by one move of a chess knight may not contain the same digit. For each line, the digits in the two cells marked with dots are ‘look-and-say clues’ ie in at least one way of reading them, one digit indicates how many times the other digit appears on the line. (eg if the marked cells contain 78 it can mean the line has seven instances of 8, or eight instances of 7). Adjacent digits along an orange line must have a difference of at least 4.
2861: Normal sudoku rules apply. Doppel-Dög loop: Draw an orthogonal non-branching closed loop that doesn't cross or touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop "starts" at the cell marked with the dog and is considered to be oriented in the direction indicated by the arrow (i.e. r6c6 and r6c7 are in the loop). A cell on the loop with a digit D will have a value equal to the cell D steps away along the loop in the orientation given by the arrow. Cells not on the loop will have a value equal to the digit in them. Adjacent digits (not values) along the loop must have a difference of at least 5. Values in a cage sum to the indicated total. Cells marked with a circle are not part of the loop and have a digit that equal to the count of the, up to 8, neighbouring loop cells. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the values of the loop cells in the indicated row/column.
2862: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade each cell light or dark so that cells of the same colour are orthogonally connected and each 2x2 contains both colours. Dark cells have double their digits as values. (Light cells are unaffected.) Dots split lines into segments with equal value-sums. Values may repeat on segments but digits may not.
2863: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat along the marked diagonal. Digits an equal distance from the centre of a lavender line sum to the central digit of that line.
2864: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits separated by a white dot have a difference of one, while digits separated by a black dot are in a 1 to 2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other). Not all possible dots are given. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) do not contain the same digit. Cells separated by a single king's move (in chess) do not contain the same digit.
2865: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog; placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid. Each of the following constraint types may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g., if a renban line contains a 5, then no other renban line cell in the puzzle may contain a 5: 1) Little Killer: Black numbers with an arrow outside the grid give the the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal; 2) X-Sums: Red numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the first X digits in that row or column, where X is the first digit in that row or column; 3) Digits on a purple Renban (RB) line form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits NB All Renban lines are exactly three cells long; 4) Neighbouring digits on a green German Whisper (GW) line must have a difference of at least 5; 5) The 3x3 box borders divide blue Region Sum (RS) lines into segments. Each segment along a line has the same sum.
2866: Normal sudoku rules apply. In each cage, there is one digit that equals the sum of the other three digits in that cage. Digits may repeat in cages if allowed by sudoku rules.
2867: Normal sudoku rules apply. If a white dot separates digits, they are consecutive. If a black dot separates digits, one is double the other. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5.
2868: Normal sudoku rules apply. Two cells separated by a single Chess knight's move must contain different digits. Digits within a cage must sum to the clue in the cage’s top-left corner. The clue outside the grid gives the sum of all digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat on this diagonal if allowed by the other rules.
2869: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the number in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage. The numbers outside the grid give the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row or column.
2870: Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and 2x3 box. Doublers: Place one Doubler in every row, column, and box. Each Doubler must contain a different digit. The value of a Doubler is 2 times the digit in its cell. The value of a non-Doubler is the digit in its cell. Standard Region Sum Line, Renban, Nabner, Thermo, Kropki, XV, and Quadruple rules apply, with respect to cell values ie: Region Sum Line: Box borders divide the blue line into segments with equal sums of values. Renban: Values along the pink line must form a set of non-repeating consecutive values in any order. Nabner: The two values on the yellow line must have a difference of at least 2. Thermo: The value on the tip of the thermometer must be larger than the value on the bulb. Kropki: Values separated by the white dot are consecutive. Values separated by a black dot are in a 2:1 ratio. V: Values separated by the V sum to 5. Quadruple: The value 2 must appear at least once in the four cells surrounding the white circle.
2871: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells along gray lines between two filled circles must have values between those in the circles. The sum of the digits along a red line connecting two circles is equal to the sum of the digits in the circles. The digit in the circle is odd. The digit in the square is even. Digits may repeat on lines of either type if allowed by other rules.
2872: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. The purple line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5.
2873: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey line is a "slow thermometer" with an invisible bulb at one end. Digits on a slow thermometer either increase or stay the same, as they move away from the bulb, but they never decrease.
2874: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Each pink line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, which can appear in any order. Each grey line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. These groups of cells cannot overlap; every cell is part of exactly one group. Lines may share endpoints, but otherwise don't overlap.
2875: Fill the grid with digits from 1-9 so that no digit repeats in any of the 9 rows, 11 columns, or 9 boxes. Along each of the 6 grey lines, digits increase in one direction. If a line has a bulb, the bulb is the smaller end. Digits touching a white dot are consecutive. Digits touching a black dot are in a 2:1 ratio. (For clarity, thermometer and kropki clues "connect up" as if the grid were un-skewed).
2876: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
2877: Divide the grid into 9 regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1-9 exactly once in every row, column, and region. The digits along the arrow sum to the three-digit number displayed in the attached pill. The arrow passes through the centres of all cells that are not part of the pill (note that consecutive arrow cells are not necessarily adjacent; for example, a portion of the arrow follows r7c1 → r7c3 → r8c1). The arrow functions as a ‘region sum line’: along the arrow, every maximal sequence of digits within the same region has the same sum. I.e. when all non-pill cells are arranged in sequence according to the order in which the arrow visits their centres, this sequence will be composed of disjoint contiguous segments with equal sums. Two consecutive cells in this sequence belong to the same segment if and only if they are part of the same region. The inequality sign points to the smaller digit.
2878: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit will remove the fog from its cell and possibly other cells in the grid. One cell in each row, column and box is a doubler. The value of a doubler cell is equal to twice its digit. Each of the digits from 1 to 9 appears in a doubler cell. On each of the constraints below, values do not repeat anywhere in the puzzle. For example, if there is a 2 on a parity line, 2 or double 1 can't appear anywhere else on a parity line, but double 2 could because it has a value of 4. 1) Adjacent values on a thin green line differ by at least 5; 2) Values on a thick purple line form a set of consecutive numbers with no repeats; 3) Adjacent values on a hollow red line must alternate between odd and even; 4) A value on an orange circle must be greater than 5; 5) A value on a blue square must be lower than 5.
2879: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits are not allowed to repeat on any positive diagonal (i.e. any diagonal going from the lower-left part of the grid to the upper-right part of the grid). A digit x in a black circle indicates exactly how many of the up to 8 neighboring cells (i.e. orthogonally and diagonally adjacent cells) contain a digit that is in a 1:2 ratio with x. All black circles are given. The sum of the digits in Phistomefel's ring (marked by the cage) is prime.
2880: Normal sudoku rules apply. INFLUENCER CELLS: The grid contains nine 'influencer cells', each in a different row, column and box, and each containing a different digit. Every cell in the grid has a value equal to its own digit plus the digits in any orthogonally adjacent influencer cells. Eg: a cell containing a digit 2 would have a value of 10 if it neighbours an influencer 3 and an influencer 5, because 2 + 3 + 5 = 10. CAGES: The small clue in the corner of a cage indicates the total value of the cells in that cage. REGION SUM LINES: 3 x 3 box borders divide blue lines into segments. The values on each segment have the same sum, though this sum can be different for different lines.
2881: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along an orange line have a difference of at least four. Each cage has digits that sum to 3. The central digit of the puzzle is even.
2882: Normal sudoku rules apply. The purple lines in the grid are “renban” lines. Ie Digits on a line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order.
2883: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit N placed inside a circle or semicircle indicates that exactly N full circles in the grid contain the digit N. Two semicircles together count as one full circle. For example, if there are four semicircles containing the digit 5 and three full circles containing the digit 5, then the total count is 2+3=5 circles with the digit 5.
2884: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in that arrow’s circle. German Whispers: Adjacent digits along a green line must differ in value by at least 5. Renban: Purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order.
2885: Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin Yang: Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 may be all shaded or all unshaded. A cell that is a ‘doubler’ has value equal to twice its digit. Two Truths and a Different Truth: For all the following constraints, if shaded cells are treated as doublers and unshaded cells are normal then two of the clues are correct and the third is incorrect. If unshaded cells are treated as doublers and shaded cells are normal then the same two clues are incorrect and the third is correct: a) Renban: Values on a pink line form a set of consecutive numbers with no repeats; b) Arrows: Values on an arrow sum to the value in that arrow's circle; 3) Values on an X sum to 10; 4) Values on a white dot are consecutive. Values on a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); 5) A value on a grey circle is odd. A value on a grey square is even.
2886: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells that are a knight's move apart in chess cannot contain the same digit. Digits on a line of any color form a set of non-repeating consecutive numbers (in any order).
2887: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a snake connecting the two green spots. The snake must be one cell wide, may only move orthogonally, and may not touch itself (not even diagonally.) Adjacent digits along the snake must have a difference of at least 5. A digit in a coloured circle indicates how many times that digit appears in a circle of that colour. All circles of one colour are on the snake. All circles of the other colour are not on the snake.
2888: From each clue outside the grid, draw a path which begins in the nearest cell of the grid and then travels orthogonally from cell to cell until arriving at a fish. All empty cells must be used by a path. Paths may not cross themselves, each other, or fish. A number at the beginning of a path indicates how many cells in the grid the path occupies, including the cell with the fish. To avoid confusion among the anglers, no two fishing lines of the same length may touch. This includes both orthogonal and diagonal touching. Answer Check: For each ? clue, fill each cell along the corresponding path with the digit equal to the length of the path. If the length is a double digit number, fill the cells with the one's digit of the length.
2889: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide blue lines into segments. The digits on each segment of the same line must sum to the same total. Digits on pink lines form a non-repeating, consecutive sequence in any order.
2890: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage must appear cloned somewhere in box nine, without rotations or reflections. All cages marked with x must have the same total, to be deduced by the solver. Cells separated by a grey dot must either be consecutive, or have a 2:1 ratio (ie one digit would be double the other).
2891: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every run of five digits on the yellow line contains a digit from {1,6}, a digit from {2,7}, a digit from {3,8}, a digit from {4,9}, and the digit 5.
