The grey line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. These groups of cells cannot overlap. Digits an equal distance from the centre of the purple line must sum to the digit in the centre of that purple line. Adjacent digits along the green line must differ by at least 5. Digits on the pink line form a set of consecutive integers in some order.
2892: Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column, and 3x3 box. Draw a 1 cell wide loop through the centers of some cells. The loop only moves orthogonally and cannot branch or touch itself, even diagonally. A digit in a circle on the loop indicates how many circles on the loop contain that digit. Similarly, a digit in a circle off the loop indicates how many circles off the loop contain that digit. Black dots separate digits where one is double the other. Additionally, exactly one cell touching a black dot is on the loop, and the other is off the loop. White dots separate consecutive digits. Additionally, the two cells touching a white dot are either both on the loop, or both off the loop. Not all dots are necessarily given.
2893: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. The two main diagonals each contain every number from 1 to 9 exactly once. The cells on a purple line contain a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, but not necessarily in order.
2894: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the number in the top left corner of the cage. Digits do not repeat within a cage. Digits separated by an V sum to 5.
2899: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each circle has a value equal to the four digits around the clue arranged in ascending order. Eg if the four digits were 4,3,6,4 then the value of the circle would be 3446. Assign each circle a rank according to its value's position in a list of the all of the circles' values. The lowest rank would have rank 1, the next lowest would have rank 2 etc. Place each circle's rank into the cell at the tip of the arrow emerging from that circle. NB clues with the same value would have the same rank and would have the same digit in the tip of their circle's arrow. Digits in a cage sum to the given total.
2901: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells with squares in them contain even digits. In this grid, the digit '4' is the only even digit that is allowed to see itself diagonally.
2902: Place the digits 0-8 in every row, column, and 3x3 box of the grid without repeats. Digits separated by an X sum to 10, digits separated by a V sum to 5. All Xs and Vs are given. Digits may not repeat along either marked diagonal. Digits placed on a purple line must be a non-repeating set of consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order.
2903: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits connected by an olive dot must be from different parities (1 even/1 odd) and differ by at least 5. Digits connected by a lavender dot must be consecutive and from different entropic sets (123/456/789). Digits in killer cages do not repeat and must sum to the number in the top left of the cage.
2904: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on green lines differ by at least five and each line contains exactly one repeat digit. Once a digit has appeared on a line as a 'repeat digit,' it may not do so again. Digits cannot be a knight's move (in chess) away from themselves. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the total in the top left corner.
2905: Lines: Draw two non-branching lines in the grid - one green and one blue - that connect the centres of cells. The lines must only move orthogonally (i.e. not diagonally). Neither line may touch itself, even diagonally. The two lines may, however, touch or cross each other, but only at discrete points (i.e.if the two lines meet in the centre of one cell they cannot continue in the same direction into the centre of their next cell). The green line must form a closed loop; and, the ends of the blue line may not be on any intersections with the green line. Projected Sums: Clues outside the grid give the sum of digits on lines along the indicated direction. Coloured clues count only the line of that colour. Black clues count digits on both lines. If both lines pass through a cell, that cell's digit only counts once in the projected sum. German Whispers: Along the green line adjacent digits must differ by at least 5. Modular Lines: Along the blue line, in every run of three cells, the three digits in those cells must each have a different remainder when divided by 3. Clones: The two cages are exact clones of each other. They contain the same digits in the same positions and they contain the same lines (including colour) in the same positions. Digits may repeat within the clone if otherwise allowed.
2906: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to 23.
2907: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in a cage and must sum to the number in the top left corner of the cage. Adjacent digits along a thicker orange line must differ by at least 4. The 3x3 box borders divide the thinner blue line into segments, each of which has the same sum. Digits in orange circles count the total number of odd digits along the line connected to the circle, including the circled cell. Digits on a thin green line with circles at both ends sum to a two-digit number; the 'tens' digit of this sum is in one circle and the 'units' digit is in the other circle.
2908: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every constraint in the puzzle is a straight line: every horizontal line is a renban, every vertical line is a German whisper, and every diagonal line is a region sum line. Different lines of the same type do not share cells. The grid is partially covered in fog. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is required. A renban line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order. Adjacent digits on a German whisper line must differ by at least 5. Box borders divide a region sum line into segments each of which must have the same total (different lines may have different totals).
2909: Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin-Yang: Shade some cells in the grid so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2×2 region is entirely shaded or entirely unshaded. A shaded cell containing digit x has value x+10; an unshaded cell has value equal to its digit. Region sum lines: Blue lines are divided into segments by box borders. All segments along a single line must have the same sum of values (this sum may differ between lines). Cells connected by a black dot have values, one of which is double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals their own cell and may also lift fog elsewhere in the grid. No guessing is required.
2910: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.
2911: Normal sudoku rules apply in the 9x9 central grid. Numbered Rooms: All outside cells on the thermo must contain a digit. That digit must also appear in the Nth position looking into the grid in the row/column, where N is the digit in the first position. Slow Thermometer: Digits on the slow thermometer must not decrease, starting from the bulb end (the circle). The white dot separates consecutive digits. The black dot separates digits where one is double the other. The X separates digits that sum to 10.
2912: Standard Fillomino rules apply: divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells, and place a number in every cell equal to the size of its region (ie the number of cells that region contains). Regions of the same size cannot share an edge. Some numbers are already given. Every Fillomino region contains a unique cell (called the Top Right Boi!): looking at the region, there can be no cell in the region that is either further to the east or further to the north than the Top Right Boi cell.
2913: Place the digits 1–9 exactly once in each row and each column of the grid. Draw a directed path that moves orthogonally between cell centres and visits every cell of the grid exactly once. Each of the 27 cages can be entered by the path at most once (i.e. the path must visit all cells of a cage in a single continuous run before leaving it). The path acts as a thermometer with respect to cage totals: as the path moves away from its starting cell, the sums of the cages it visits must strictly increase. Digits may not repeat within a cage.
2914: Place a digit from 1-7 in each cell. Each digit must appear exactly once in each row, column, and box, except for the digits 1 and 3, which may appear any positive number of times. Every 1 and 3 must be part of at least one adjacent pair of cells which reads as '13' either from left to right or from top to bottom. Digits in a cage do not repeat (including 1 and 3) and sum to the total shown in the top left corner.
2915: Normal sudoku rules apply. No digit can appear a chess knight's or a chess king's move away from itself. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the oval which is a 2-digit number reading left-to-right. Adjacent digits along the arrow (including the oval) have a difference of at least 4.
2916: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits may not be a chess knight's move apart. Each pink line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits between 1 and 9 in that row or column.
2917: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9, plus the letters R, B and C, so that no letter or digit repeats in any row, 3x4 box, or column. 3x4 boxes are numbered 1-12 in normal reading order. The value of an R equals its row number. The value of a B equals its box number. The value of a C equals its column number. BLACK KROPKI: If two values are joined by a black dot, one is double the other. RENBAN: Values along a pink line form a non-repeating consecutive sequence, arranged in some order. GERMAN WHISPER: Adjacent values on a green line have a difference of at least 5. ARROWS: Values along an arrow sum to the value in the attached circle. SAME DIFFERENCE: Adjacent values on a turquoise line have the same difference. This difference may be different for different turquoise lines.
2918: Fill each cell (octagons and squares) with a digit from 1-9. Cells sharing an edge can't have the same digit. Each horizontal row and vertical column contains a non-repeating consecutive set of digits (like 2345678) in any order. A value in an external cell represents the rank of the number formed by reading the digits in the indicated 5-cell diagonal from that direction, where (1) is the lowest such row or column and (20) is the highest. If two ranks are tied, the value in both external cells is the lower of the two ranks being shared.Eg, if the lowest four ranks are '12453', '13524', '13524' and '15432', the values in the relevant external cells would be (1), (2), (2) and (4) respectively.
2919: Each ball may move sideways or downwards (diagonally or straight) any number of times, but may NOT move upwards, on its journey. Balls may not enter any cell more than once. Balls may not enter a grey shaded cell or a "bumper" cell (given digit). Each ball must visit both of the "target" cages (shaded yellow) along the way. No path shares any cells, and while they may cross other paths diagonally, no path crosses itself. Box borders divide the BLUE path into segments with the same sum. Adjacent digits along the GREEN path must differ by at least 5. Digits along the RED path must be 5 or higher.
2920: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colour each cell in one of two different colours, where cells containing the same digit must have the same colour. If an orthogonally connected group of cells of the same colour has one or more circles in it, the circled cell(s) contain the size of that group.
2921: Fill the grid with nine non-overlapping 3x3 regions, such that each region contains the digits 1-9 once each and no digit repeats in any row or column. Digits along a marked diagonal sum to the clue outside the grid. Blank cells don't count towards the total.
2922: Normal sudoku rules apply. Reading from the bulb to the tips, digits along a thermometer must either increase or stay the same. Adjacent digits along the green line have a difference of at least five. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum. Each cage has digits that sum to 8.
2923: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in its black circle. Digits may repeat along an arrow if allowed by other rules. A digit x in a circle (including black arrow circles and red circles) indicates exactly how many of the up to 8 neighboring cells (i.e. orthogonally or diagonally adjacent cells) contain a digit that differs by at least 5 from x.
2924: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. A black dot sits between two digits where one is double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given. Inequality signs between two cells point towards the smaller digit.
2925: Divide the grid into five regions, each containing 5 orthogonally connected cells. Place a digit from 1-5 in each cell so that digits do not repeat in a row, column or region. 'Marbles' join cells that share a region, and no two marbles share a region. Draw a 'Marble Run' from any cell in the top row to a 3 in a bottom corner. The marble run line is formed entirely of L-shaped line segments: a downwards movement (to gain speed) and then a horizontal movement of the same distance. Adjacent cells on the Marble Run are in different regions. Use the pentomino information provided around the grid to discover a secret code and enter it at the top of the grid to reveal the final rule.
2926: Place each digit 1–7 exactly once in each row and column of the 7×7 grid. The grid is covered by 16 jigsaw pieces. Each piece covers the same sum. If a cell is covered by more than one piece, its digit is split between those pieces proportionally to the area covered. Eg if R4C4 contains the digit x, then this cell contributes ¼·x to the sum of the piece covering R3C3, ½·x to the sum of the piece covering R3C5, and ¼·x to the sum of the piece covering R5C5.
2927: Within the main grid (inside the thick border), fill every cell with a digit from 1-5 such that digits do not repeat in a row or column. Full Rank: A value in an external cell represents the rank of the number formed by reading the digits in that row or column from that direction, where (1) is the lowest such row or column and (20) is the highest. Mod 3 lines: Any 3 adjacent cells along a line must contain a complete set of residues modulo 3 (there will be a residue 0, 1, and 2, with residue defined as the remainder of the cell value after dividing by 3). N.B. If two ranks are tied, the value in both external cells is the lower of the two ranks being shared. For example, if the lowest four ranks are "12453", "13524", "13524" and "15432", the values in the relevant external cells would be (1), (2), (2) and (4) respectively.
2928: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of two orthogonal neighbours is at most 13 (ie no domino in the grid can sum to more than 13). The sum of two 'point symmetric' cells is always 10. (Point symmetric cells are pairs that are mirror images of each other across the exact centre of the 9x9 grid (the middle of the central 3x3 box). ie Rotating the grid 180° around this central point maps a cell directly onto its symmetric partner). So, for example, r7c1's symmetric counterpart is r3c9.
2929: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. If two digits are separated by a black dot one digit is double the other. Additionally, a black dot always separates a shaded and an unshaded cell. Not all dots are necessarily given. Shaded digits in the grid represent skyscrapers of that height, with taller skyscrapers obscuring smaller ones. A clue outside the grid shows the number of all visible skyscrapers from the clue's direction. Unshaded digits do not affect the outside clues.
2930: Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid. Adjacent cells cannot sum to 10. Grey lines are palindromes that read the same in both directions. If two digits are separated by a black dot one is double the other. Not all possible black dots are necessarily shown. A cell marked with a grey circle contains an odd digit. No guessing is required.
2931: Normal sudoku rules apply. Outside clues are Sandwich clues, indicating the sum of the cells between the lowest & highest values (usually 1 & 9) seen in their row or column. R0C0 applies this to each of row 0 & column 0 individually. Apart from value 0, every Sandwich clue is unique. (If multiple instances of 0 are seen by R0C0's clue, which is 'lowest' is to be determined by the solver.) Cells across white dots contain consecutive values. Cells across black dots contain one value double the other (1:2 ratio).
2932: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each row, column, and 3x3 box contains two 'indexer' cells: a 'row indexer' and a 'column indexer'. The digit in a row indexer gives the position of the column indexer in that row. The digit in a column indexer gives the position of the row indexer in that column. Positions are counted left-to-right in rows and top-to-bottom in columns . Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the upper left corner, if given. Indexer cells cannot appear in cages.
2933: Normal Sudoku rules apply, but once again strange things are afoot... Fog has filled the land, thicker than ever before, and within it, lurk many Creatures of the night! Yet fear not! If you can find them, friendly Wisps will aid you in navigating the fog. There is one Wisp in each row, column, and 3x3 box, marked by a pale blue dot. Cells containing a Wisp contain either their row, column or box number (read in normal reading order). No two Wisps can contain the same digit. Fog cleared by Wisps leaves an eerie blue light. The Monsters: Zombies: marked by a green dot, zombies have an infectious bite. Orthogonally adjacent cells are even when the zombie's number is even, or odd when the zombie's number is odd. Vampires: marked by a red dot, vampires suck the power from their victims. Orthogonally adjacent cells sum up to the vampire's number. Headless Horsemen: marked by an orange dot, horsemen have a knight's reach. Cells a chess-knight's move away from the horseman can't contain the same digit as the horseman's number. Poltergeists: marked by a grey dot, poltergeists throw everything into disarray. Orthogonally adjacent cells are either all higher than the poltergeist's number, or all lower. Fog: the land is covered in dynamic fog. Putting in correct digits will clear the fog for that cell. Finding a Wisp will clear more fog. No guessing is required. The monster under your bed will know if you cheat!
2934: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a directed path through the centres of some cells in the grid, starting in one blue circle and ending in the other. The path may move only orthogonally north (↑), orthogonally east (→), or diagonally southwest (↙), and it may not visit any cell more than once. The path must function both as an entropic line and as a region sum line. Every black dot in the grid must be crossed by the path. A white dot joins two cells - neither of these cells may be visited by the path. Along an Entropic line, every set of three consecutive cells along the line must contain one low digit (1,2,3), one middle digit (4,5,6), and one high digit (7,8,9). Along a Region sum line. the 3x3 box borders divide the line into segments; and all such segments must have the same sum. A white dot between two digits means they must be consecutive. If two digits are separated by a black dot one is double the other. One of the dots contains an inequality sign pointing to the smaller digit.
2935: Normal sudoku rules apply. Exactly one cell in each row, column, and box is a "doubler", and doubler cells contain a complete set of the digits 1-9. A cell's value is equal to its digit, except that a doubler cell may or may not have a value equal to its digit multiplied by two. The same cell may have different values for the purpose of different clues. The sum of the values inside each cage is shown. The sum of the values along an arrow is equal to the value in the connected circle. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum of values. Along a green line, values differ from their neighbors by at least 5. A purple line contains a non-repeating set of consecutive values in any order. Values in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.
2936: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partly covered in fog. Placing correct digits may clear fog revealing other clues. No guessing is required. A digit in a square indicates the total number of digits smaller than itself that it 'sees' in all the four cardinal directions (North, East, South, West) along its row and column. In each direction, it 'sees' ALL digits smaller than itself until vision is blocked by a digit greater than itself or the edge of the grid. (For clarity it does not see itself). If a black dot separates two digits, one of those digits is double the other.
2937: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a 1-cell wide loop that moves strictly orthogonally and doesn't branch or intersect itself. The loop doesn't touch itself, not even diagonally. Neighbouring digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 5. A digit in a circle indicates how many times that digit must appear in circles. The circled digits also indicate how many of the (up to 8) surrounding cells are on the loop. Circles are never on the loop. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.
2938: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a 1-cell wide loop that moves strictly orthogonally and doesn't branch or intersect itself. The loop doesn't touch itself, even diagonally. The loop acts as a German whispers line. Neighbouring digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 5. A digit in a circle indicates how many times that digit must appear in circles. The circled digits also indicate how many of the up to 8 surrounding cells are on the loop. Circles are never on the loop.
2939: Normal sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row, column and 3x3 box.) Cages within the same 3x3 box must sum to the same total. Any cage can only contain either all odd digits or all even digits.
2940: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage has a two-digit total to be placed by the solver inside the cage. Place the tens digit in the leftmost cell of the topmost row of the cage, then write the total from left to right. If the cage shape doesn’t allow a left-to-right placement, write the units digit directly below the tens digit instead. If the total consists of two identical digits (e.g., 22, 33, 44), write only a single digit. Digits may repeat within a cage, provided normal sudoku rules are not broken. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle.
2941: Normal sudoku rules apply. A binary code is a sequence of numbers (“bits”) that are either on or off. In this puzzle, Odd digits represent bits that are 'OFF'(O) and Even digits represent bits that are 'ON'(E). This gives us the following representation of the digits 1-9: 1 → OOOE 2 → OOEO 3 → OOEE 4 → OEOO 5 → OEOE 6 → OEEO 7 → OEEE 8 → EOOO 9 → EOOE The digit in an arrow cell dictates the parity (odd or even) of its four orthogonal neighbours. These four neighbours must match the binary code of the digit with the small arrow. The arrow points to the first bit of the binary code. (read from left to right.) The full code must wrap around the central cell clockwise. Eg If a 6 is placed in an arrow cell, its code is OEEO. Therefore, its four neighbours (starting from the arrow direction, moving clockwise) must be Odd, Even, Even, Odd.
2942: Fill each cell with a digit from 1-9. Cells sharing an edge can't have the same digit. Each horizontal row and vertical column contains a non-repeating consecutive set of digits (like 23456) in any order. The blue circles and red squares combined form a complete set of the digits 1-9. A digit in a blue circle indicates how many of that digit appear in the entire puzzle. A digit in a red square indicates that the digit does not appear exactly that many times in the puzzle. EG if there were four 4s and six 5s in the grid, the 4 would go into a circle and the 5 in a square.
2943: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as an entropic line. Each set of three adjacent digits along the loop must be one low [123], one medium [456], and one high digit [789]. The loop must enter every cell of every cage. The sum of all digits in any given cage is the same for every cage (that sum must be determined by the solver).
2944: Dr. Norma L. Dokes! A virus is spreading and causes people to eat each others brains! Please perform some measurements in the village and bring the results to the hospital. We need to see how severe the spread is. But be careful - It is highly contagious! NORMA L DOKES - Normal sudoku rules apply. INFECTIONS - The 3x3 boxes are numbered in normal reading order, 1 to 9. Each digit matching its own box number is a 'patient zero'. Each row and column contains a 'patient zero'. Patient zeroes are infected. Infected cells infect every orthogonally adjacent cell with a smaller digit. Infections keep spreading until no infected cell has a smaller uninfected orthogonal neighbour. (Every infected cell can be traced back to one or more patient zeroes.) PATH - Draw a 1-cell wide path from the doctor () to the hospital (). The path only moves orthogonally and may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The path may not contain infected cells. MICROSCOPES () are on the path and count the number of infected cells in the (up to 9) surrounding cells. KROPKI TABLETS (white dots) join consecutive uninfected digits.
2945: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the number in the corner of the cage. Digits in cells separated by a black dot must be in a 2:1 ratio, digits in cells separated by a white dot must be consecutive - not all dots are shown. Digits along a purple Renban line must be a set of consecutive digits in any order. Digits along a red palindrome must read the same forwards or backwards. Digits along the blue diagonal line must not repeat.
2946: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat along the marked diagonal. Every 2×2 square of cells must contain all three possible remainders modulo 3 (i.e. at least one digit from each of the sets {1,4,7}, {2,5,8}, and {3,6,9}). Draw a path starting in the top-left corner cell and finishing in the bottom-right corner cell, visiting every 3×3 box at least once. In a single step, the path may move only east (→) or southwest (↙). Any three consecutive digits along the path must have three different remainders modulo 3. Box borders divide the path into segments; each segment is a renban, i.e. it must contain consecutive, non-repeating integers in any order.
2947: Normal sudoku rules apply. The cells in the grid are numbered from 1 to 81 in normal reading order ie 1 at the upper left, ..., 9 at the upper right until 81 at the bottom right. The digit in a cell with a square number is itself a square (1,4,9) while the digit in a cell with prime number is a prime (2,3,5,7). In addition, any vertical or horizontal straight line of three cells never contains a consecutive set of digits.
2948: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a line between two circles must have values between the digits in those circles. Each circle digit must be consecutive with at least one digit on the line. For example, (2)-7-3-5-(8) is a valid fill for a Snug Between Line.
2949: Normal sudoku rules apply. The two digits on an arrow give the coordinates of a particular target cell somewhere in the grid. The digit on the arrow's shaft indicates the target cell's row, and the digit on the arrowhead indicates the target cell's column. The difference between the two digits should be placed into the target cell. No two arrows target the same cell. Also: A pink arrow contains two consecutive digits; a green arrow contains two digits with a difference of at least 5; and, on a black arrow, one digit is double the other.
2950: Normal sudoku rules apply. One cell in each row, column and region is a nullifier cell. Nullifier cells have a value of zero. In graves (cages), values must sum to the day, month or year of the date on the grave. Digits cannot repeat within graves. Escape the graveyard by carefully plotting an orthogonally connected path between the green and red cells. The path may not cross the highest or lowest values in a grave.
2951: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits on a (slow) thermometer do not decrease from the bulb end. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. A cage shows its sum. A purple line uses a set of consecutive digits in any order. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the connected circle. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5.
2952: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the number given in its corner. Digits may not repeat within a cage. In any row or column, no more than two consecutive digits may have the same parity (i.e., be both odd or both even). Eg A sequence such as 2–4–5–7 is valid; but 2–4–6–3 is not valid, since three even digits appear consecutively.
2953: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide the blue line into segments whose values have an equal sum. Consecutive digits along the orange line have a difference of at least four. Consecutive digits along a green line have a difference of at least five. If cells are connected by a black dot, one is double the other. A cell with a gray circle contains an odd digit.
2954: Place the digits 1–9 exactly once in each row and each column. Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2×2 area is entirely shaded or entirely unshaded. Within each cage, the sum of the shaded digits equals the sum of the unshaded digits. Digits MAY repeat within a cage. The corner cells with grey diamonds contain the same digit.
2955: Normal sudoku rules apply. Nurikabe: Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected (water), but no 2x2 area is entirely shaded; groups of orthogonally connected unshaded cells form islands. An island may be of size 1. Every cell with a circle clue is unshaded, and each island contains exactly one circle cell. The digit in this circle cell gives the size of the island. Note that an island may occupy a full 2x2 area (unlike water). Digits may not repeat within an island. Every blue line must contain at least one shaded and at least one unshaded cell. Switching between shaded and unshaded cells divides each line into segments with the same sum. Different lines may have different sums. Digits may repeat on a line if allowed by other rules.
2956: In each NxN grid, place the digits 1-N once in every row, column and box; in the slanted 6x6 grid, digits should be entered only in the middle of cells. A digit may not appear in the same position in multiple 4x4 grids. Each arrow contains a 2-digit number, with the 10s digit on the shaft and the 1s digit on the head; the number on an arrow gives the sum of the first X digits seen in a straight line in the indicated direction, where X is the first digit seen. Arrows only see cells that contain digits, i.e. blank spaces, such as those not belonging to any grid, are not seen.
2957: Normal sudoku rules apply. Circle a digit in each row, column, and box. Each circled digit must be different. Shade some cells, such that within any row, column, or box, the number of shaded cells is equal to the circled digit. A digit in a diamond is not circled, and equals the sum of the circled digits in its row and column. Shaded digits within a cage sum to the value given in the top left of the cage.
2958: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. The digits 1 to 9 appear once each on both blue diagonals. The digits along an arrow sum to either a single digit number in that arrow's circle or a two digit number (reading left-to-right) in that arrow's oval.
2959: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the small total given in the top left corner of the cage. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Within the grid, digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Grey lines are palindromes which read the same forwards and backwards. Digits separated by a white dot have a difference of one. Not all possible dots are given.
2960: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some cells contain ghosts. Not all ghosts are visible! Each ghost with the digit N is staring at another ghost with the digit N, exactly N diagonal steps away. A headstone shows the sum of the ghosts in its column. (For the avoidance of doubt, the eyes indicate the direction the visible ghosts are staring in!)
2961: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 boxes are numbered in normal reading order. Each digit matching its box number is an "inoculation site". Each row and column contains an inoculation site. They are infected. Infected cells infect every orthogonally adjacent cell with a smaller digit. Infections keep spreading until no infected cell has a smaller uninfected orthogonal neighbour. (Every infected cell can be traced back to one or more inoculation sites.) All uninfected cells form one orthogonally connected area. Each orthogonally connected group of infected cells touches the grid's edge. A digit in a blue circle is uninfected and counts the number of infected cells in its 8 surrounding cells. Green lines connect 2 infected digits that differ by 5 or more. Pink dots join consecutive uninfected digits.
2962: Normal sudoku rules apply. No domino in the grid can contain digits summing to 10. There is some fog in the grid; placing a correct digit might remove it. No guessing is required. Digits in a grey box cannot repeat. There are lines in the grid that connect boxes; the digits in a box are summed to arrive at a value. That value applies to the following rules: 1) Zipper: when box values equidistant from the centre box on a pink line are summed together, they are equal to the centre box's value on that line. The centre box is notated by a pink circle; 2) Modular: every run of three boxes on a teal line must have a different remainder when divided by 3 (ie one value from each of 0 mod(3), 1 mod(3), and 2 mod(3)); 3) Box values on a purple line make up at a set of consecutive, non-repeating values; 4) The box values connected by a blue line must be the same; 5) Box values joined by a white dot have a difference of 1.
2963: Each row, column, and box contains two 1s, two 3s, and one each of 2, 4, 5, 6, and 7. Cages sum to the totals shown. Digits MAY repeat in cages. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
2964: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colour each cell either yellow or blue. All cells of the same colour must be orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area may be all one colour. A purple frame contains two cells of the same colour, and displays the total of the digits of that colour within that 3x3 box (reading left to right, or downwards.) If two digits are joined by an X, they sum to 10. If two digits are joined by a black dot, then one is double the other.
2965: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a green line differ by at least 5. Digits along an orange line differ by at least 4. A magenta line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Digits along a gray thermometer increase from the bulb. Box borders divide a blue line into sums of equal value. Every three digits along a peach line includes one number each from {1,2,3}, {4,5,6}, and {7,8,9}. Every three digits along a cyan line includes one number each from {1,4,7}, {2,5,8}, and {3,6,9}. Digits separated by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
2966: There exist nine non-overlapping 3x3 square regions which must be located. Each region contains the digits 1-9 once each, such that no digit repeats in any row or column. Cells outside these regions do not contain digits, but have a value of 0. Adjacent values along a green line differ by at least 5. Cells an equal distance from the centre of a silver line have equal values.
2967: Normal sudoku rules apply. A blue line is divided by the 3x3 box borders into sums of equal value. A magenta line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive values in any order.
2968: Place the digits 1-9 at most once in every row, column, and 3x3 box. There are nine 3x3 boxes, which overlap at the dashed lines. Adjacent cells on a green line have a minimum difference of 5. Adjacent cells on an orange line have a minimum difference of 4. Any three adjacent digits on a teal line cannot be from the same set of modulo 3 residuals, that is {1,4,7}, {2,5,8}, or {3,6,9}. Any three adjacent digits on a peach line cannot be from the same set of low, middle, or high digits, that is {1,2,3}, {4,5,6}, or {7,8,9}. Cells separated by a black dot have values in a ratio of 1:2. Cells separated by a white dot have values with a difference of one. Cells separated by an X sum to 10; cells separated by a V sum to 5.
2969: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each set of three adjacent digits on a peach line contains one each from the sets of {1,2,3}, {4,5,6}, and {7,8,9}. Each set of three adjacent digits on a teal line contains one each from the sets of {1,4,7}, {2,5,8}, and {3,6,9}. A black dot joins two digits of which one is double the other. Each main (9-cell) diagonal contains only three distinct digits.
2970: Normal sudoku rules apply. The two digits on an arrow give the coordinates of a particular target cell somewhere in the grid. The digit on the arrow's shaft indicates the target cell's row, and the digit on the arrowhead indicates the target cell's column. The sum of the two digits should be placed into the target cell. No two arrows target the same cell. Also: A pink arrow contains two consecutive digits; a yellow arrow contains two non-consecutive digits; a green arrow contains two digits with a difference of at least 5; and, on a black arrow, one digit is double the other.
2971: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a purple line form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. A digit in a square indicates the number of cells it sees in its row and column that are smaller than itself, where digits larger than itself block vision.
2972: Place the digits 1-9 in every row, column and each marked 9-cell region. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Every 2x2 square of cells must contain at least one digit from (1,4,7), at least one digit from (2,5,8), and at least one digit from (3,6,9). Cells that are orthogonally adjacent cannot contain consecutive digits. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. The cell with a circle must contain an odd digit.
2973: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each row, column, and 9-cell region must contain the digits 1–9 exactly once. Regions consist of 9 orthogonally connected cells. Cages within the same region must have the same total (without repeating digits within a cage). Digits within a cage must be all odd or all even. A cage cannot cross region borders. Each region must contain at least two cages. Cages marked with X and Y have different totals. A white dot separates consecutive digits. A black dot indicates one digit is double the other. Not all possible dots are necessarily given.
2974: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along each line sum to 9.
2975: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by an X sum to ten and cells separated by a V sum to five. Not all possible Xs and Vs are necessarily given. Any vertical or horizontal straight line of three cells never contains a consecutive set of digits (in any order).
2976: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits on a pink “renban” line contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order. Adjacent digits on a green “German Whisper” line must have a difference of at least 5.
2977: Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally connected cells, such that every cell is part of exactly one region. Place the digits 1-9 exactly once in each row, column and region. Brown clues to the left and above the grid are Sandwich clues: They indicate the sum of the digits between the 1 and 9 in that row or column. In rows and columns that have a Sandwich clue, all the digits between the 1 and 9 must be in the same region, and the 1 and 9 must not belong to that region. All regions that do not touch the edge of the grid are Pie filling: Black clues below the grid indicate the sum of the digits within Pie filling in that column.
2979: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and sum to the total shown. Consecutive digits cannot border each other in the same cage. There is 1 negator in every row, column and box, forming a set of the digits 1-9. If negators appear in a cage they subtract their value from the sum of the other digits. Each diamond is a friendly square. Friendly cells are cells which match either their row number or their column number. Digits may never repeat in friendly cells, but not all digits need appear as a friendly cell. The circular white dot joins consecutive digits.
2980: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring values along a green line differ in value by at least 5. Values on the whisper outside the main grid provide a hit points clue for their respective row or column. A valid ‘hit points’ clue sums the digits in its row or column that are in their corresponding numbered cell, for example a 3 in r4c3 would contribute to the clue in r4c0 and any other digit would not. All hit points clues are a minimum of 1. For the solution check to trigger please only enter small digits outside the grid.
2981: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 9 blue circles must contain a set of the digits 1-9. Lines are hit point lines. The blue circles show the total of the line's sum which is made up from digits in their correct position along the line. (Eg a line reading 14325 would have the total 9 as 1 is in the first position, 3 in the third and 5 in the 5th but 4&2 are not correct being in the second and 4th position respectively). Digits may not repeat along lines. Some lines have a square at the end. These squares mark the position of the first digit in the sequence. For lines without squares, the solver must determine in which direction they go, but they must always start at one end of the line and finish at the other. White dots mark consecutive digits, not all white dots are necessarily given. The rat's nose contains an odd digit (this last rule does not appear on the card in the video!).
2982: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with the same sum. A pink line contains a non-repeating consecutive sequence, in any order. A digit in a circle must appear in a cell touching the circle.
2983: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog, placing a correct digit will clear the cells surrounding that cell. Digits on a purple renban line a set of consecutive digits in any order without any repeats. Digits in a dotted cage do not repeat. The cage shows its sum. Adjacent digits on a green German Whisper line differ by at least 5. A clue outside the grid sums the digits between the 1 and 9 in its respective row/column. Digits separated by a black dot have one digit double the other.
2984: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit cannot appear more than its own number of times across all lines in the grid. For example, there cannot be more than six 6s placed on lines. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Digits along a purple line form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order.
2985: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digit in a blue diamond equals the number of cells in the same row or column whose digits match their distance from the diamond (e.g., any 1 exactly one cell away, any 2 exactly two cells away, any 3 exactly three cells away, etc.). The digits in blue diamonds do not repeat. Both cells with a grey diamond contain the same digit.
2986: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. In each positive diagonal (ie diagonal sloping from the South-West to the North-East), neighbouring digits differ by only 1 or 8.
2989: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along each main diagonal must not repeat. Adjacent digits on a green German Whispers line must have a difference of at least 5. Adjacent digits on a dark blue Factor line must have an integer quotient. A digit in a circle indicates how many times that digit appears in circles.
2990: Normal sudoku rules apply. All cells are either island or water. Each purple cell is an island cell. Each island must contain exactly one purple cell. Different islands may not touch orthogonally. The water cells are orthogonally connected and may not contain any 2×2 areas of water. Each island also contains a set of non-repeating digits that sums to the purple cell total if given. If no total is given, the sum is 6, 9 or 25. The number in the purple cell is the number of cells in the island. Totals are not necessarily in the top left most cell of an island. All islands are normal except one - Treasury Island, which has no given total. On this island, X's mark the spot - i.e. Treasury Island can be evenly divided into non-overlapping dominoes that each sum to 10; also, the purple cell's digit is inconsequential and digits may repeat.
2991: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. Digits on arrows may repeat if allowed by other rules. Digits on a purple renban line must be consecutive and non-repeating, but can be in any order.
2992: Normal sudoku rules apply. Exactly one cell in each row, column, and box is a 'halver', and halver cells contain a complete set of the digits 1-9. The value of a halver cell is equal to its digit divided by two. The sum of the values inside each cage is shown, and digits cannot repeat within a cage (but values can). The sum of the values along an arrow equals the value in the connected circle. Values on thermometers strictly increase from the bulb. Values in cells separated by a V sum to 5. Values in cells separated by an X sum to 10.
2993: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Draw a one-cell-wide loop that moves orthogonally through the centers of some cells. Adjacent digits along the loop are not consecutive. Numbers left of the grid indicate the number of cells on the loop in their row. Numbers above the grid indicate the sum of cells on the loop in their column. O, E, and P represent an odd, even, and prime number respectively.
2994: Normal sudoku rules apply. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is necessary. All circles are outside the grid, and each must be filled with a digit. This digit indicates how many digits in its row or column match their distance from the circle. Eg: if a row with a circle at its left-hand end reads 123459786, then all of the digits except 6 and 9 match their distance from the circle, so the circle would contain a 7. A digit in a circle also indicates how many times that digit appears in a circle. Adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5. Any 3 adjacent digits along a hollow peach line must contain one digit from {1, 2, 3}, one digit from {4, 5, 6} and one digit from {7, 8, 9}. Small white dots divide stripy blue lines into at least 2 segments, with the digits on each segment having the same total. If a black dot sits between two digits, then one is double the other.
2995: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along arrows sum to the digit in the attached circle. Digits along purple lines form a consecutive set. Digits in cages sum to the small number printed in the corner. Digits in cells separated by a chess King's move may not contain identical digits.
2996: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colour the grid using two colours, such that all cells of the same colour are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is fully one colour. Odd clues outside the grid give the first odd digit seen from that direction; even clues give the first even digit seen from that direction. Each such odd or even clue is a single digit and only sees digits of one yin yang colour, while digits of the other colour are completely meaningless for that clue. Which colour corresponds to each clue must be determined. Some clues are covered in fog. Placing correct digits in the grid may lift some of the fog to reveal more clues.
2997: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as a German Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 5). Clues outside the grid are Japanese Sums ie they give the sums of loop segments in the respective row or column, in order, where cells not on the loop separate segments. A question mark indicates any digit from 0 to 9, but no clue may have a leading zero. An asterisk denotes an arbitrary number of Japanese sum clues. This could be zero, one, or multiple.
2998: Fill the grid with digits 1-9 so that each row, column, and box contains exactly 8 unique digits. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the attached bulb. Digits along a thermometer must not decrease from the bulb end to the tip. Two cells connected by a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Clues outside the grid give the number of digits visible from the clue's position, given that each digit blocks the view of any digits behind it that aren't larger than it. Along a blue line, box borders divide the line into smaller segments with the same sum. Digits can repeat along a segment if allowed by other rules.
2999: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every digit on a line of colour C counts how many times that digit appears on all lines of colour C. For example, if there is a 3 on a green line, then there are exactly three 3s on all green lines combined. German whispers (decorated with squares): Adjacent digits along a green line differ by at least 5. Parity lines (decorated with circles): Adjacent digits along a red line have different parity (i.e., one of them is even and the other is odd). Region sum lines (no decorations): 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments of equal sum. The sum may be different for different lines.
3000: Place a digit from 0 to 9 in each non-black cell so that no digit repeats in a row or column. Regions of the same color have the same sum (white is a color). Along diagonal lines, digits increase in one direction. Small square outlines all contain different digits.
3001: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1-6, once each, in every row, column and box.) The digits along a purple arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. The grey line consists of non-overlapping segments, each of which sums to ten.
3002: Fill each cell with a digit from 1-9. For every row 'n' and column 'n' there are exactly 'n' unique digits. The remaining cells are filled with repeats. Divide the grid into three regions. A region is an area of orthogonally connected cells. No 2x2 area may be entirely in one region. Identical digits may not appear in different regions. Adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5. No two digits anywhere on a yellow line may be consecutive (or the same). Any group of 3 adjacent cells on an orange line must contain one low digit (1, 2 or 3), one medium digit (4, 5 or 6) and one high digit (7, 8 or 9). Adjacent digits on a turquoise line always have the same difference. This difference must be determined for each turquoise line. Digits joined by an X sum to 10. A digit on a blue arrow indicates how many region borders (separating two regions) are seen in the direction of the arrow. (Region edges at the outer perimeter of the grid don't count.)
3003: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments of equal sum. (The sum may be different for different lines). Each grey line is a palindrome i.e. reads the same forwards as it does backwards. Adjacent digits along the green line must differ by at least 5.
3004: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 black box borders split grey thermometer lines into segments. Starting from the bulb, the sum of each segment must increase. Additionally, within each segment, starting from the original bulb, digits must also increase. Every 2x2 square of cells completely sitting within a red cage must contain a low digit (1,2,3), middle digit (4,5,6) and high digit (7,8,9). Digits connected by a white dot are consecutive. If a black dot sits between two digits, one is double the other.
3005: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every set of four sequential digits on a hollow peach line must contain one each from {19}, {28}, {37}, and {46}. A 5 may not appear on a peach line. Digits on a line may repeat if allowed by other rules. The 3x3 box borders divide the blue lines into segments with the same sum. (Different lines may have different sums.) Digits in a cage must sum to 20.
3006: Horseshoes: Digits do not repeat along a line. The two digits at the ends of each line (marked with white circles) sum to the number displayed in the middle of that line.
3007: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as a Dutch Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 4). Japanese Sums: Clues outside the grid give the sums of loop segments in the respective row or column, in order, where cells not on the loop separate segments. A question mark indicates any digit from 0 to 9, but no clue may have a leading zero. An asterisk denotes an arbitrary number of Japanese sum clues. This could be zero, one, or multiple.
3008: In the main 7x7 grid fill the cells with the digits 1-7 such that there are no repeats in rows or columns. Build nine 7-cell orthogonally connected regions such that digits do not repeat in a region. Regions will cover both inside grid and outer clue cells (but not the given clues or greyed out outside areas). Two solid black region borders in the grid have been given. Blank outer clue cells are numbered rooms clues and must contain digits for solution check to work. Outside clues in rectangles are given numbered rooms clues. (A fully grey cell is to be left empty.) A clue's digit must also appear in the Nth position looking into the grid in the row/column, where N is the digit in the first position. Circles count the number of outside cells that circle's region contains. All possible circles are given.
3009: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9, so that no digit repeats in any row or column. Each 3x3 box must be filled using only 3 distinct digits (with repeats being allowed.) Adjacent digits along a turquoise line always have the same difference. This difference must be determined for each turquoise line. 3x3 box borders divide darker blue lines into segments, which each have the same sum. This sum must be determined for each darker blue line.
3010: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits a knight's move (in chess) apart must be different. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. The black dot indicates digits with one being double the other, the white dot indicates consecutive digits. Not all dots are necessarily given. Digits in circles appear at least once in the four surrounding cells.
3011: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Digits along a pink line must form a non-repeating group of consecutive digits, but they may appear in any order along the line. Each grey line can be divided into segments of contiguous cells where the digits in each segment sum to 10. These segments cannot overlap, and every cell is part of exactly one segment. Digits may repeat freely on grey lines and within sums.
3012: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid indicates the sum of the first set of all ascending digits starting from the first cell from the corresponding side. Sets may consist of only one digit.
3013: Normal 6x6 Sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1-6, once each, in every row, column and 2x3 box). Values increase along the grey line from the bulb. Values outside the grid are the sum of the indicated diagonal.
3014: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the total in the top left corner. Digits in box 5 (ie the central 3x3 box) must not see a digit of the same parity a knight’s move away. A “King's move constraint” is only applied to even digits: ie an even digit cannot repeat a king's move away from itself. Cells connected by an X sum to 10. ALL possible Xs are given. A white dot connects two consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are given.
3015: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Digits along a pink line must form a non-repeating group of consecutive digits, but they may appear in any order along the line. Each grey line can be divided into segments of contiguous cells, where the digits in each segments sum to 10. These segments cannot overlap and every cell is part of exactly one segment. Digits may repeat freely on grey lines and within 10 sums.
3016: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits a king's move (in chess) apart must be different. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Box borders divide blue lines into segments with the same sum. Each of the digit in a circle appears at least once in the four cells touching the circle.
3018: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits don’t repeat in a cage and sum to the given total, if indicated. All instances of five of the nine digits, to be determined, constitute an area of orthogonally connected cells, a "labyrinth". The other four digits are considered "walls". An arrow appears in a "dead end" of the labyrinth pointing to the only way out, i.e. the only labyrinth cell to which it is connected. All arrows are given. A white dot joins consecutive digits (not all white dots are given).
3019: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid hides a labyrinth: a single continuous region of orthogonally connected cells. All remaining cells are walls. A 2×2 block may never consist entirely of labyrinth cells or entirely of wall cells. Arrows mark ALL dead ends of the labyrinth, each pointing toward the only cell they connect to. Walls form isolated tetrominoes (4 orthogonally connected cells). Wall cells from different tetrominoes can't touch each other, even diagonally. Digits within a tetromino do not repeat and sum to 12. A white dot between two cells indicates that their digits are consecutive. An X between two cells indicates both that the cells are of different types (one labyrinth cell and one wall cell) and that their digits sum to 10. (Not all white dots and Xs are given.)
3020: Normal sudoku rules apply. In a cage, digits don't repeat and sum to the indicated total. An X between two digits indicates they sum to 10. All Xs are given!
3021: Normal sudoku rules apply ie Each row, column, and 3×3 box must contain the digits 1–9 exactly once. A golden dot between two cells indicates that their sum is divisible by 4. ALL possible golden dots are given. Golden dots take precedence over the black dots ie if two cells could have black dot and a golden dot, only the golden dot is shown. A black dot between two digits indicates that one is double the other. Not all possible black dots are given. A white dot between two digits indicates they are consecutive. Not all possible white dots are given. The sum of two adjacent cells separated by a 3x3 box border are even. Note that the sum of two adjacent cells not separated by a 3x3 box border may still be even.
3022: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some intersections of the grid lines are marked by a number and an operator (+, -, x, /) in a circle. The number is the result of the arithmetical operation, applied to BOTH pairs of diagonally opposite cells. An "E" in the circle indicates that all four adjacent digits are even; an "O" indicates that all four adjacent digits are odd.
3023: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. Cells that are visited twice by an arrow count twice for the total value. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
3024: Normal sudoku rules apply. Help Cecil the Spider to build a web using silky threads. A single silky thread must start at a white spot and connect to another white spot that is either one or two cells away in a straight line (horizontally, vertically or diagonally.) Any further and the thread will break! Two silky threads may not cross each other. The digit on a white spot indicates how many silky threads attach to it. The two white spots connected by a silky thread may not contain the same digit. If a black insect sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a stripy green insect sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. If a spotty red insect sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. The digit being thought about by Cecil the Spider indicates how many of the afore-mentioned insects have been caught on silky threads.
3025: Normal sudoku rules apply. Battlefield: Consider the first X cells and the last Y cells of each row and column, where X is the number in the first cell and Y is the number in the last cell. These groups of cells will either overlap or leave a gap. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the cells in the resulting gap or overlap. ALL cells that are part of an overlap in BOTH their row and column are red. ALL cells that are part of a gap in BOTH their row and column are green.
3026: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9, so that no digit repeats in any row or column. Each box may only contain three distinct digits. Digits along a purple arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. Adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5. Adjacent digits along a turquoise line always have the same difference. This difference must be determined for each turquoise line. No two digits on a yellow line may be the same or consecutive. If two digits are separated by a black dot, then one is double the other.
3027: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits on a renban (purple lines) form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. If two digits are separated by a black dot then one digit is double the other.
3028: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply within the 6x6 grid. (ie place the digits 1-6, once each, in every row, column and 2x3 box.) Cells outside the grid contain “skyscraper clues”, which indicate the number of digits “visible” in that direction in the 6x6 grid (where higher digits block the view of lower digits). Eg a row reading 216453 would have a clue of 2 from the left (as the 2 and 6 would be visible); and a clue of 3 from the right (as the 3, 5 and 6 would be visible). Each cage sum is the same, and digits may repeat within a cage. Digits in cells separated by a gold dot are not consecutive. (The "solution checker" does not consider the skyscraper clues outside the grid.)
3029: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Neighbouring digits on a curved line must differ by at least 4. Digits on the star-shaped line must form a set of consecutive digits.
3030: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the total of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that column. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least five. Digits in a circle must be placed at least once in the four cells touching that circle.
3031: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, even diagonally. The loop acts as a German Whisper line, so all adjacent digits along the line must have a difference of at least 5. A (loopwich) clue outside the grid indicates the sum of the digits sandwiched between the first and last loop cell in their row or column. (Both loop and non-loop cells between the 2 ‘crust’ cells are summed)
3032: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a snake in the grid. A snake is a one-cell-wide path of orthogonally connected cells which may not touch itself orthogonally or diagonally. Arrow cells are always on the snake, and count the total amount of snake cells seen in all indicated directions (If R8C6 sees 4 cells up its column and 2 cells along the diagonal then it would be a 6). Arrow cells do not count themselves. Circle cells are the head and tail of the snake, and count the total number of snake cells in their box. Cages represent different zones which dictate how the snake functions through each zone. In the GW Zone the snake functions as a German Whisper Line, along which adjacent digits differ by at least 5. In the ENT Zone the snake functions as an Entropic Line, along which any three consecutive cells contain a low digit {1,2,3}, a medium digit {4,5,6}, and a high digit {7,8,9}. Where the snake crosses between different zones the connection doesn’t need to be either Entropic or German Whisper. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
3033: Normal Sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-6 in each row, column, and box. Ambiguous Thermos: Digits strictly increase along the gray lines from bulb to tip. The bulbs of the lines need to be deduced by the solver. The bulb will always be on one end of the line, never in the middle. Little Killer: Numbers outside the grid are the sum of the digits pointed to along the indicated diagonal. Digits are allowed to repeat along those diagonals as normally allowed by the other rules.
3034: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single non-intersecting loop through the centers of some cells that moves horizontally or vertically and passes through every circle clue. The loop must turn on black circles and pass straight through the cells on either side. The loop must go straight through white circles and turn in at least one of the cells on either side. The loop acts as a modular line. Each set of three adjacent digits along the loop must be one each from the sets [147], [258], and [369]. The digit in each given circle clue counts the total number of loop cells in all straight loop segments coming off of the cell (counting the cells where the loop turns, and counting the clued cell itself once).
3035: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on green tinsel have a difference of at least 5. The digit on a gold bauble indicates exactly how many times that digit appears on green tinsel.
3036: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits a knight’s move away cannot be the same. Colors used in this puzzle are blue (b), white (w) and red (unshaded). The squares outside the grid indicate the order of the runs of contiguous cells that must be shaded the color of the clue. The number in the square indicates the sum of the cells in the run OFF BY 1! There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs of the same color, but that is not required for runs of different colors. All shaded runs are given.
3037: Parity Counter Lines: the two digits at the ends of each line indicate the number of odd and even digits in that line, including the end digits themselves. One digit counts odd digits; the other counts even digits. BitClock: A BitClock is a group of five cells: a central arrow cell and its four orthogonally adjacent neighbours (up, right, down, left). The arrow shows where the pattern starts, and the pattern is then read clockwise around the four neighbours. The digit in the central arrow cell tells you the odd/even pattern of those four neighbours, using a simple 4-bit code. In those neighbour cells, an even digit means the “bit” is ON; while an odd digit means the “bit” is OFF. Each arrow cell digit has its own fixed 4-bit pattern (see table below). Eg If a 3 is placed in an arrow cell, its code is OOEE.Starting from the direction of the arrow and reading clockwise, the four orthogonal neighbours must be Odd, Odd, Even, Even. Digit Codes: 1 → OOOE2 → OOEO3 → OOEE4 → OEOO 5 → OEOE 6 → OEEO 7 → OEEE 8 → EOOO 9 → EOOE
3038: Normal 6x6 Sudoku rules apply. (ie place the digits 1 to 6, once each, in every row, column and 2x3 box). MINESWEEPER: Shade some cells ('mines') and leave the others unshaded ('cleared'). Two cleared cells are shown (although one of these still needs its digit to be entered). Each digit in a cleared cell indicates how many mines are in the (up to 8) surrounding cells. No two 2x3 boxes have the same number of mines.
3039: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. No two cells sharing an edge sum to 5 or 10.
3040: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits cannot repeat along the blue diagonal line.
3041: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a path from r1c9 to r9c1. The path moves orthogonally and visits all 3x3 regions. Adjacent digits on the path must have a difference of at least 4. r1c9 and r9c1 are the only island cells on the path. All cells are either island or water. Each lavender cell is an island cell; the number in it is the number of cells in that island. Each lavender island must consist of exactly one lavender cell, and a set of non-repeating digits that sum to the total in the lavender cell, if given (r6c8's island total is a prime number). r1c9 (Canada) and r9c1 (Japan) are non-lavender island cells. Both islands' digits have the same product. The digits on the flags are inconsequential. Different islands may not touch orthogonally. The water cells are orthogonally connected and may not contain any 2×2 areas of water. Cage totals are not necessarily in the top left most cell of an island.
3042: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum (this sum may be different for different lines).
3043: Normal sudoku rules apply. A circle's neighbourhood includes the cell containing the circle, and any cell touching it (on an edge or corner). The digit in the circle is the number of cells in its neighbourhood that have the same odd-even parity as the circled digit. Digits in circles also indicate how many circles in the puzzle contain that digit.
3044: Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-9 in every row, column, and box, without repetition. Yin Yang: Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is fully shaded or fully unshaded. A clue that is in cells that are all shaded or all unshaded is RIGHT. A clue that has at least one cell shaded and at least one cell unshaded is very, very WROGN. See below for exact definitions of WROGN clues. RIGHT Cages: Digits in cages must sum to the value in the top left corner of the cage. RIGHT Kropki: Where digits are separated by a black dot, one must be double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given. RIGHT Renban: Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. RIGHT Nabner: No two digits on a gold line can be consecutive, regardless of their position on the line. Digits may not repeat on lines. RIGHT Quadruples: Digits in a Quadruple circle must be placed at least once in the four cells touching that circle. WROGN Cages: Digits in cages must not sum to the value in the top left corner of the cage. WROGN Kropki: Where digits are separated by a black dot, neither is allowed to be double the other. WROGN Renban: No two digits on a purple line can be consecutive, regardless of their position on the line. Digits may not repeat on lines.(ie, WROGN renban lines are RIGHT nabner lines). WROGN Nabner: Digits on a gold line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. (ie, WROGN nabner lines are RIGHT renban lines) WROGN Quadruples: Digits in a Quadruple circle must not be placed at all in the four cells touching that circle.
3045: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells shaded gray must be larger than their orthogonal non-fortress neighbors. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle.
3046: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid indicates that in that row or column, there exist two digits which sum to the clue, such that the digits between them also sum to the clue. If there are multiple clues in a row or column, the sequences of clued digits appear in the same order as the clues, and those sequences do not overlap.
3047: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green German Whispers line must differ by at least 5. Digits separated by IX must sum to 9. Digits separated by XI must sum to 11.
3048: Normal sudoku rules apply. Indigo lines are filled with a repeating sequence of different digits. The sequence must appear at least twice along the line and must always appear in its entirety. Different lines may contain different sequences. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Digits separated by a black dot must have a ratio of 2:1 (i.e. one must be double the other).
3049: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with the same sum.
3050: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Correctly placing digits may clear fog somewhere in the puzzle. Correct digits do not necessarily clear fog from their own cells. Counting constraints: A digit on a constraint indicates the total number of times that digit appears on ANY of the constraints below. No cell contains more than one constraint. A) German whispers: Adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of at least 5; B) Dutch whispers: Adjacent digits along an orange line must have a difference of at least 4; C) Nabner lines: No two digits on a yellow line may be the same or consecutive; D) Renban lines: Pink lines are filled with a consecutive set of non-repeating digits; E) Counting circles: A digit in a black-outlined counting circle indicates the number of times that digit appears in a counting circle; F) Odd circles: A digit in a gray circle must be odd; G) Kropki: Digits separated by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2 (i.e. one is double the other).
3051: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide blue lines into segments with the same sum. The segment sum is a concatenation of the two digits on the extreme ends (e.g. a line with segments summing to 36 will have a 3 on one end and a 6 on the other). Different lines may have different segment sums. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot must have a ratio of 2:1 (i.e. one must be double the other).
3052: "Do the best you can until you know better. Then, when you know better, do better." Normal sudoku rules apply. Echo Lines: Indigo lines are filled with a repeating sequence of one or more different digits. The full sequence must appear at least twice along the line and must always repeat in its entirety. Different lines may contain different sequences. Nabner lines: No two digits on a yellow line may be the same or consecutive. Killer Cages: Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the given total.
3053: ill the grid with the digits 0-3 so that each digit appears TWICE in every row, column, and marked 4x2 box. Reconstruct the maze by drawing thick walls along certain cell edges. The wall around the maze perimeter has been drawn already. The digit in a circle indicates how many of that cell's 4 edges contain a wall. The finished maze must have a valid route from the red R (rat) to the blue C (cupcake), without passing through any walls or visiting any cell more than once. No diagonal moves are possible in this maze, due to the brown wall spots on the corners of cells. An edge containing a purple arrow does not contain a wall, and sits between two different digits, with the arrow pointing towards the smaller digit. An arrow can only be passed through in the direction it's pointing. Adjacent digits along the path must sum to at least 3.
3054: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits may not be a knight's move apart. Each row, column, and box contains exactly two stars. Stars may not touch orthogonally or diagonally. Stars also contain digits and behave as normal Sudoku cells. Any digit orthogonally adjacent to a star must differ from the star's digit by at least 3. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of star digits along the indicated diagonal (only star cells count).
3055: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each purple line contains a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. In this puzzle, the largest digit on each line must be at one of the line’s ends.
3056: Place 1-6 in each row, column and 3x2 box. Each of the following constraint types may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g., if a purple line contains a 5, then no other purple line in the puzzle may contain a 5: 1) Digits on a purple line must be consecutive. 2) Any set of three digits along a turquoise line must have at least one digit from each of the following sets: (1, 4), (2, 5), (3, 6). 3) Digits in cells separated by a V must sum to 5. 4) One digit is double the other in cells separated by a black dot. 5) A blue square must contain an even digit.
3057: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey line can be divided into segments of contiguous cells, where the digits in each segment sum to 10. These segments cannot overlap and every cell is part of exactly one segment. Using red, green, and blue, colour in all circles such that: Orthogonally adjacent circles are different colours; and the digit inside a circle appears that many times in circles of that colour.
3058: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot have a difference of 3. Digits along a line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. A clue outside the grid indicates the sum of the first X numbers in the row/column where X is the first digit seen.
3059: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each Invader sums to 10 with a digit in some orthogonally adjacent cell. Digits connected by a 𐌔 always have the same difference. Strategically place 3 turrets into cells in the bottom row. Each turret has as many missiles as the digit in its cell, and can pivot to fire them upwards or diagonally. A turret can destroy an Invader on a digit N by shooting it N times. Each Invader is only shot by one of the turrets. All Invaders must be destroyed!
3061: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a circle is odd and counts the number of odd digits that can be seen in all orthogonal directions combined, including itself. Even digits block the view.
