A digit in a square is even and counts the number of even digits that can be seen in all orthogonal directions combined, including itself. Odd digits block the view. ALL circles and squares are given.
3062: Normal sudoku rules apply ie Place the digits 1 to 9 once each in every row, column, and 3x3 box. Coordinate Arrows: Digits on an arrow spell out the coordinates for the digit that is their sum. The row number is written on the start of the arrow, the column number is written on the arrow tip. For example, read from shaft to tip, if an arrow contained the digits 14 then there must be a 5 in r1c4. All the arrows must correspond to different coordinates. Digits may repeat on an arrow if allowed by other rules
3063: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade the grid such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is entirely shaded or unshaded. Circles are unshaded, and count the number of shaded cells in the (up to 8) neighbouring cells. Digits along a green line sum to a concatenation of the two digits in the connected circles. For example 3_436_1 would be a valid fill as 436 sums to 13 which can be made from the connected 3 and 1.
3064: Normal sudoku rules apply. 9 cells in the grid are “doublers”, one in every row, column, and 3x3 box, each containing a different digit. The value of a doubler cell is double the digit in that cell. Values on an arrow spell the coordinates for the value that is their sum. The row value is on the start of the arrow and the column value on the tip. Eg if an arrow contained the values 15, then a 6 (or a doubled 3) is placed in R1C5. Each arrow indicates a different cell.
3065: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits inside the grid represent the heights of skyscrapers, and clues outside the grid indicate the number of skyscrapers visible in that row or column, looking in that direction. The cell with a gray circle contains an odd digit.
3066: Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally connected cells, such that every cell is part of exactly one region. Place the digits 1-9 exactly once in each row, column and region. Adjacent digits along a line must either be consecutive and belong to a different region or have a 1:2 ratio and belong to the same region. (A 1:2 ratio means one digit will be double the other.) If 1 and 2 are adjacent along a line, they can satisfy either condition.
3067: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide the blue line into segments. Each segment's total is found by summing the digits on that segment. The segment totals must increase from one end of the line to the other.
3068: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the attached bulb (the two-digit number is read left to right). Digits separated by the dot are not consecutive.
3069: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a grey thermo increase from the bulb to the tip. Any set of three sequential cells along a line must contain a digit that is 1 mod 3 (147), and a digit that is 2 mod 3 (258). and a digit that is 0 mod 3 (369). Vertical columns on a keypad are a good reference. All lines in this puzzle conform to both rulesets. In the case where thermos share a bulb the entire line is considered for the modular logic.
3070: Normal sudoku rules apply. From each square, draw a valid hitline moving through the centres of cells. Each hitline must occupy at least two cells. Hitlines may travel orthogonally and diagonally between cells, but may not branch, share cells, or cross themselves or each other. Digits may not repeat on a hitline. The small white clue on a square indicates the total sum of all the digits along that hitline that match their position number, with the square itself being position 1. Eg: if a hitline reads 82195 then its square would have a 7 clue, as this is the sum of 2 and 5 which are the only two digits on the line which match their position number (they are in the 2nd position and 5th position.)
3071: Normal sudoku rules apply. Purple lines contain a set of distinct consecutive digits in any order. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. The gray line is a palindrome. No two cells sharing an edge contain digits summing to 5 or 10.
3072: Normal sudoku rules apply. On either main diagonal (marked with a thin blue line), digits may not repeat. The 3x3 box borders divide thick blue lines into segments; each segment on a line has the same sum. Different lines may have different sums.
3073: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid indicates the presence of a thermometer that is fully placed in the direction of the arrow where all the digits on the thermometer add to the number of the clue and the bulb is always the closest to the clue. Digits on a thermometer are all different and strictly increasing from the bulb to the tip. Thermometers are mimimally three cells long and they include all possible digits. i.e. the first digit behind the thermometer may not be larger than the last digit on the thermometer, and the last digit before a thermometer may not be smaller than the digit in the bulb. Thermometers may overlap other thermometers.
3074: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a small white dot must be consecutive. Draw a closed loop into the grid that travels orthogonally between cells and doesn't visit the same cell more than once. The loop must not visit any big circles. The loop acts as an entropic line, i.e. three adjacent digits along the loop must contain one digit from {1,2,3}, one digit from {4,5,6} and one digit from {7,8,9}. The number of loop turns is different in each 3x3 box. A digit in a big circle indicates the number of times the loop turns in that box.
3075: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach the cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. The paths may not share cells except for where they meet at the cupcake cell. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz and Phinx may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If two digits are joined by a blackcurrant, one is double the other. If two digits are joined by a grape, they have a difference of at least 5. If two digits are joined by a red X, they sum to 10. Finkz and Phinx may not pass directly through a red X. In this experiment, a cell may only be visited by Finkz or Phinx if its digit matches its row number, column number or box number. (Boxes are numbered 1-9 in normal reading order from top left to bottom right.)
3076: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on thermometers increase from bulb to tip. Each cell represents a ‘skyscraper’ whose height is the digit in that cell. Taller skyscrapers obscure the view of smaller ones. Clues outside the grid tell how many skyscrapers are visible looking across the row or column from the direction of the clue.
3077: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in the connected circle, and these digits can repeat if allowed by other rules. Along the green line, digits differ from their neighbours by at least 5. Digits in cells with a shaded circle are odd. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive.
3078: Normal sudoku rules apply. Fog will clear as correct digits are placed. There is a red cage from r3-r9 and c3-c9 in which Japanese sums colorings will take place, with clues given in c1-2 and r1-2. Clues are colored pink, and if there is a cage there, the sum of the run of pink cells is known to be the small digit in the corner * 10 + the value in the cage. So if a cage had a little 1 and a 4 was placed in it, the JSS clue would be 14. If there is no cage, you know there's a run of coloring, but not what it sums to. The clues inside the grid (r1-2 and c1-2) indicate the sums of the contiguous runs found in that row or column that must be shaded. There must be an unshaded cell between runs of the same color. If a row or column is unclued (no pink cells at all), there is no shading in that row or column. Cells joined with a V sum to 5. 4 colored dots in the grid, Green, Red, Blue and Yellow are ratio dots and may represent any ratio from 1:2, 1:3, 1:4, 1:5, 1:6, 1:7, 1:8, or 1:9. It's up to the solver to determine which dot is which type. A pink line is either Renban (consecutive sequence of digits in any order) OR German Whisper (neighbouring digits differ by at least 5. Each line must be determined individually. A circle is odd.
3079: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat on the marked diagonal. Digits in a cage may not repeat and sum to the small number in the top left corner of the cage.
3080: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each of the 8 blue lines into segments with the same sum. (This sum may be different for different lines).
3081: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single closed loop representing the car’s path, viewed from above. The car drives clockwise around the grid through cell centers and moves strictly orthogonally. The path may touch itself orthogonally but must not cross or branch. Cages are obstacles which the car can never enter. The loop must visit each region at least once. The digit in any cell the loop passes through determines the car’s movement: Odd digits (1,3,5,7,9): go straight. Even digits (2,4,6,8): turn, using absolute numpad directions: 2 → Up 4 → Left 6 → Right 8 → Down In each 3×3 box, the sum of the odd digits on the loop equals the sum of the digits inside the cage(s) in that box (multiple visits of the loop contribute to the same total). A region without a cage indicates the sum of odd digits for that region is zero.
3082: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into galaxies: orthogonally connected groups of cells that have 180 degree rotational symmetry about their centers (marked with a small dot). All cells must be part of a galaxy; no galaxies overlap. Galaxies are either red-shifted (moving away from the observer), or blue-shifted (moving towards the observer). The measured value of each galaxy is shown; it is the sum of the digits in that galaxy PLUS (blue-shifted) or MINUS (red-shifted) the number of cells in the galaxy. Dots with a solid black outline indicate "Renban" galaxies, whose digits form an unbroken consecutive sequence in any order. Conversely, dots without a solid black outline indicate galaxies whose digits do NOT form such a sequence. Digits may not repeat within a galaxy. Five single-cell galaxies — "Dark Stars" — are NOT marked: their locations must be deduced by the solver. All cells (max 8) around a Dark Star belong to regular galaxies. No 3x3 box contains more than one Dark Star. Digits do not repeat amongst the Dark Stars.
3083: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, share cells, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz and Phinx may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Find nine copycat cells in the maze; one in each row, column and 3x3 box, and each containing a different digit. The value of a copycat cell equals the digit in the cell that is 180° rotationally opposite it in the grid. Eg: if r1c3 is a 6 and r9c7 is a copycat cell, then r9c7 will have a value of 6, regardless of what digit it contains. If two cells are joined by a blackcurrant then the value of one is double the value of the other. If two cells are joined by a redcurrant then one has an even value and the other has an odd value. If two cells are joined by a grape then their values have a difference of at least 5. In this experiment, in any 3x3 box, the total value of the cells visited by Finkz is the same as the total value of the cells visited by Phinx. (This total must be determined for each box.)
3084: Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing correct digits may reveal fog somewhere in the grid. Cells that are a knight's move (in chess) apart may not contain identical digits. Cells connected with a gray circle contain digits that are consecutive or in a 1:2 ratio (or both). Box borders divide blue lines into segments with the same sum. Different blue lines can have different sums.
3085: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a GW (“German Whisper”) line must differ by at least five. Any set of three adjacent cells along an Ent (Entropy) line must contain a low digit (123), a middle digit (456), and a high digit (789). If two digits are separated by a black dot, one is double the other. Not all black dots are necessarily given. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all white dots are necessarily given. Digits along grey lines (“Ten Lines”) must be broken into one or more contiguous groups of cells that sum to ten. Such groups cannot overlap. Digits may repeat within such sums if allowed by other rules. Eg 513173 is a valid fill for a length 6 line, because it can be broken into 5131 and 73, each of which sum to 10. Adjacent digits along a DW (“Dutch Whisper”) line must differ by at least four. Digits along a PR line alternate odd/even. No two digits along a Nab (“Nabner”) line can be consecutive, regardless of their position on the line.
3086: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and must sum to the given total.
3087: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits strictly increase along each thermometer starting from the bulb end. Additionally, the digits on each thermometer of the same colour sum to the same total. Green thermometers and blue thermometers may sum to different totals.
3088: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a main diagonal (marked in blue), digits may not repeat. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. The green central 3x3 box forms a "magic square": each row, column and 3-cell main diagonal of this box must sum to the same total.
3089: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colour the grid using two colours, such that all cells of the same colour are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is fully one colour. Outside clues give the sum of the first three digits seen from that direction but each outside clue ONLY sees digits of one colour, while digits of the other colour are completely meaningless for that clue. Which colour corresponds to each clue must be determined. (Each clue sees at least three digits of its colour.)
3090: Normal sudoku rules apply. Black dots separate digits where one is double the other. In cages, digits do not repeat, and sum to the given value.
3091: Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally-connected cells. Regions cannot overlap. Place the digits 1-9 once in each row, column, and region. Each region has a corresponding colour. A note outside the grid indicates that the region of that colour contains a run of one or more orthogonally-connected cells (bounded on either side by a region border or the edge of the grid) in that row or column, and the number in the note (if given) is the sum of the digits in these cells. If a region contains multiple sets of orthogonally-connected cells in the same row or column, a note only applies to one of them. When two notes overlap, the note above has a lower sum than the note below (this applies even if a sum is hidden or not given).
3092: Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally-connected cells. Regions cannot overlap. Place the digits 1–9 once each in every row, column, and region. In cells with arrows, the digit equals the number of cells in its own region (including itself) visible in the arrow directions; sight is blocked by region borders or the edge of the grid.
3093: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a thin grey line must be between the digits in the circles on the ends of that line. Digits on a thick blue line must NOT be between the digits in the diamonds on the ends of that line. Digits in those diamonds must differ by at least 4. A black dot joins two digits where one is double the other. A white dot joins two consecutive digits. Disjoint Groups: Cells with the same position in the boxes contains number from 1 to 9 i.e no number can repeat in the same position in the boxes.
3094: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat on either marked diagonal. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum. A white dot joins two consecutive digits. Digits in a cage sum to the total shown. The value of x is consistent throughout the puzzle and must be determined.
3095: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat a (chess) knight’s move away from each other. Box borders divide a thin blue line into segments with the same sum. Digits placed on a thick magenta renban line must be a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, in any order. On a black dot, one digit is double the other.
3096: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on the red line alternate between even and odd digits. White dots separate consecutive digits that are adjacent to each other along the red line. All dots along the red line are given. If two cells both have a red line, but the cells are not adjacent along the path of the line, no dot will be given even if the digits are consecutive. For example, r2c6 and r2c7 both have a red line passing through them, but because the line does not travel immediately from r2c6 to r2c7, the lack of a dot does not mean anything. There are four single cell cages at the corner of the grid. These individual cages act as a single combined cage. The 4 digits must sum to 16. Digits cannot repeat on the marked diagonal.
3097: Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing correct digits may clear some fog. Digits separated by an X sum to 10, digits separated by a V sum to 5. Purple (Howling Mad) lines indicate a sequence of digits where no other specified line type could go: Renban: Consecutive non-repeating digits; Nabner: Non-consecutive non-repeating digits; Parity: Alternating even/odd; Entropy: Every 3 digits has a [1,2,3], [4,5,6], and [7,8,9] digit; Modular: Every 3 digits has a [1,4,7], [2,5,8], and [3,6,9] digit; Dutch Whisper: Adjacent digits differ by at least 4; Region Sum: Box borders divide lines into segments with the same sum. Howling Mad lines are always three cells long and are always either strictly vertical or strictly horizontal. Lines cannot overlap each other. No set of digits appears on more than one line. For example, if one line contains 1, 2, and 4, no other line can contain all three of those digits. Given those rules, no further lines are possible.
3098: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single king's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
3099: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach the cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. The paths may not share cells except where they meet at the cupcake cell. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz and Phinx may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If two digits are joined by a blackcurrant then one is double the other. If two digits are joined by a redcurrant then one is even and the other is odd. If two digits are joined by a grape then they have a difference of at least 5. In this experiment, Finkz and Phinx both visit the same number of cells. Before reaching the cupcake, the Nth digit visited by Finkz and the Nth digit visited by Phinx always have the same difference (to be deduced.) This difference equals the digit on the cupcake cell. Eg: if the 3rd digit visited by Finkz is 5 and the 3rd digit visited by Phinx is 9, the cupcake cell would contain a 4.
3100: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a killer cage cannot repeat and sum to the indicated total.
3101: Normal sudoku rules apply. Both main diagonals are marked with a blue line. On either diagonal, no digit can repeat. Digits along an arrow sum up to the digit in that arrow's circle. If two digits are adjacent on a black line, then one digit is double the other. If two digits are adjacent on a magenta line those digits are consecutive. The grid is covered in fog; placing correct digits will clear the fog in that cell and may also clear fog in other cells. No guessing is necessary.
3102: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the circle of that arrow. Digits on a (‘double arrow’) line sum to the sum of the two circles at the end of the line. All double arrow lines are straight.
3103: Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Regions do not overlap. Place the digits 1–9 once each in every row, column, and region. Suns: The digit in a sun counts how many of the up to nine cells in the 3×3 square centered on that sun belong to the same region as the sun (including the sun cell itself). Example: If R4C1 = 3, then exactly three of the cells R3C1, R3C2, R4C1, R4C2, R5C1, and R5C2 belong to the same region as R4C1.
3104: Fill each cell of the main 9x9 grid such that every row, column and 3x3 box contains a 0 and eight different digits from 1-9. No two rows, no two columns and no two boxes may be missing the same digit. For each 0 in the grid, the digits missing in its row, column and region must be three different digits. The cells outside the grid must filled in with the digits that are missing from the corresponding row/column/box. Adjacent digits on an orange Dutch whisper line must differ by at least 4.
3105: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1-6, once each, in every row, column and 2x3 block.) The digit in a coloured square indicates how many circles of that colour contain a digit bigger than itself.
3106: In each N-by-N Latin Square, place the digits 1 to N once each in every row and column. Each circle has an odd sum. Each square has an even sum.
3107: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat along a marked diagonal. Adjacent digits on a line must have a difference of at least 5. No two digits on a line can be consecutive, regardless of their position on the line. Digits may not repeat on a line. (All lines are thus both German Whisper and Nabner lines)
3108: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach the cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. The paths must only converge at the cupcake cell. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz and Phinx may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but they may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Digits may not repeat within a cage. All cages have the same total, to be deduced. An electricity symbol indicates the cage's shock value. Cages with a shock value of 5 or higher may not be entered. Cages with a shock value lower than 5 are safe to enter. If a red X sits between two digits, they sum to 10. In this experiment, both paths must be a valid 'between line', ie: the highest and lowest digits on a path can be found at its ends (on the rat and the cupcake cell, in some order) and not anywhere else along that path.
3109: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue's digit must appear in the Nth position looking into the grid in the row/column, where N is the digit in the first position.
3110: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected and no 2x2 square is completely shaded or unshaded. Every dot must touch a shaded cell. Adjacent digits within the shaded region must differ by at least 5. If two digits are joined by a black dot one must be double the other. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive.
3111: Placing correct digits might clear some fog. Each row, column, and region contains the digits 1-9 once each. A region is an orthogonally connected collection of cells. The shape and position of the regions have to be determined. There are 9 blue circles (with thicker outline) in the grid. Each blue circle belongs to a different region. Additionally there are black circles (with thinner outline). These can be in any region and a region can have more than 1 black circle. The digit in a circle counts the number of cells that the circle sees from its own region in the row and column up to the first border including itself. A small magenta arrow counts the number of region borders seen in the direction it points. If a cell has more than arrow, they see the same amount of borders in each indicated directions. The outer edges of the grid do not count as borders. On a white dot, digits are consecutive. On a black dot, one digit is double the other.
3112: Normal sudoku rules apply. Magnets: A digit in a magnet cell (M) is the sum of all digits seen in the indicated direction up to the first cell seen that contains a digit larger than M.
3113: Normal sudoku rules apply. On each line, there is exactly one cell whose value is greater than the sum of any other two cells on that line.
3114: Place the digits 1 to 9, once each in every row, column and region. Note that isolated cells (like r1c1) are part of the region of the same colour on the other side of the grid). Digits cannot repeat within a bold outlined region. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) in the grid cannot contain the same digit. No domino in the grid can contain consecutive digits.
3115: Divide the grid into nine non-overlapping regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1–9 once each in every row, column, and region. In each region, place a circle in the leftmost cell of its topmost row. Every circled digit counts how many cells of its own region (including itself) are visible in its column (region borders block the view). The nine circled cells together form an extra region, i.e. they are orthogonally connected and contain the digits 1–9 once each.
3116: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid hides a labyrinth: a single continuous region of orthogonally connected cells. A 2×2 block may never consist entirely of labyrinth cells. There are no dead ends in the labyrinth (every labyrinth cell is connected to at least two other labyrinth cells). All remaining cells are walls. Walls form isolated groups of exactly four orthogonally connected cells. “Isolated” means that wall cells from different groups cannot touch each other, not even diagonally. Digits within a group of walls do not repeat and sum to 14. An X between two cells indicates that their digits sum to 10. ALL Xs ARE GIVEN. An X is always framed when it lies between two cells of the same type: either labyrinth cells or wall cells.
3117: Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid. The digits along an arrow sum to a two-digit number (reading left-to-right) in that arrow's oval. Cells separated by an X sum to 10 and cells separated by a V sum to 5. Not all possible Xs and Vs are necessarily given.
3118: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits then one is double the other. Finkz and Phinx may only pass directly through a purple arrow if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two digits it sits between. The digit on a pink motion sensor indicates the number of cells that are visited within the (up to 9) cells immediately surrounding the sensor. The sensor itself is counted, if visited. The digit on a grey camera indicates the total SUM of the digits in any visited cells that the camera's lens points towards (before a wall is reached, which blocks vision.) In this experiment, both paths are valid 'modular lines'. Any set of 3 successive cells along a path contain one digit from each of the groups [1,4,7], [2,5,8] and [3,6,9].
3119: Normal sudoku rules apply. Red (circled) clues are sandwiches, i.e. they indicate the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9 in the corresponding row or column. Blue clues are X-sums, i.e. they indicate the sum of the first X digits in the corresponding row or column, where X is the digit in the first cell.
3120: Place the digits 1-5 once each in every row and column. AREA 51: Extend the fence into a loop that doesn't touch itself; if a digit N appears inside the enclosed area at all, it appears exactly N times in the enclosed area; the enclosed area sums to 51.
3121: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line differ by at least 5. Cells separated by an X sum to 10.
3122: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each horizontal blonde line sums to a 2 digit number. These two digits are at the start and end of its row, in some order. Each vertical brunette line also sums to a 2 digit number. These two digits are at the top and bottom of its column, in some order.
3123: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orthogonally adjacent cells do not sum to 5 or 10. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. Cells separated by a flower sum to 13.
3124: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Shade some cells in the grid such that they form an orthogonally connected area. All unshaded cells must be part of an orthogonally connected group that contains all the digits 1 to N exactly once, where N is the size of that group. All groups must be connected to the outside of the grid. All circles (including arrow bulbs) are unshaded.
3125: Normal sudoku rules apply. Any set of three adjacent cells along a peach line contain a low digit (123), a middle digit (456), and a high digit (789). Digits along a pink line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in some order. Digits along a red line alternate between odd and even. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive.
3126: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit N on a cell with an arrow indicates that there is a straight line N cells long starting from the cell the arrow clue is on and extending in the direction of that arrow. This line acts as a region sum line: box borders divide the line into segments with the same sum. Each line must cross at least one box border.

An index cell may contain two digits, but may not have a value greater than 6. If an index cell has a value of zero, the value being indexed does not appear in the row. Nothing in these rules prevents a value from repeating in a row, even if one instance of that value is referenced by an index cell. The sum of the values along an arrow is equal to the value in the connected circle.
3196: Normal sudoku rules apply. Any sequence of five cells along the long purple lines must contain a run of five consecutive digits in any order without repeats. Lines shorter than five cells must contain a run of consecutive digits in any order without repeats.
3197: Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin Yang: Shade some cells such that i) all shaded cells are orthogonally connected; ii) all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected; and iii) every 2x2 contains both shaded and unshaded cells. Yin Yang Split Lines: Yin Yang borders split lines into 2 or more segments with the same sum. (If 2 cells are adjacent along the line, they are in the same segment if and only if they have the same shading). Digits may not repeat within a segment. Every line contains shaded and unshaded cells. Segment Counters: A digit in a circle on a line indicates how many total segments that line has.
3198: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single 1-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells into the grid that does not branch or enter any cell more than once. The loop must pass through all given dots, and all given dots must be in the middle of a straight loop segment (i.e., the distance from a dot to the next turn along the loop must be identical in both directions). Digits separated by a grey dot are consecutive or one is double the other. Adjacent digits on the loop not separated by a dot must NOT be consecutive or where one is double the other.
3199: Normal sudoku rules apply. MODULAR ARROWS: A digit on an arrow counts how many cells in the indicated direction have the same remainder mod-3 as itself, including itself. (Eg a 4 on an arrow would indicate that exactly four digits (including the 4 itself) in that direction were selected from the digits 1, 4 & 7 (because each of 1,4 & 7 have the same remainder (ie 1) when divided by 3).
3200: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each letter from ABCDEFGHZ stands for a different digit from 1-9. Each labeled gray letter cell in the grid contains that digit. Where a ? is used, it always represents a two digit total. Ie the leading question mark is never 0. Digits in cages sum to the total given. Digits cannot repeat within cages. Digits along indicated diagonals have the indicated sum. Digits may repeat along such diagonals. Circles within the grid are quadruples. The indicated digit appears in at least one of the four surrounding cells. Digits with a door are numbered rooms. The indicated digit appears a number of cells into that row or column given by the first number in that row/column. Digits with a building are skyscrapers. They indicate how many digits are seen from the perspective of the clue if digits are only seen if they are the highest digit encountered so far.
3201: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells are either 'sea' or 'land'. No 2x2 block is filled with just sea or land. All sea cells are connected orthogonally. Cells with arrows are dead ends, that is, sea cells that point to the only other sea cell they touch. Land cells form 'islands' that don't touch each other, even diagonally, comprising four orthogonally adjacent, different digits, summing to 14. On an X, the two digits sum to 10, and on a red dot, they sum to 12. All arrows, X's, and red dots are shown. On an X, the two cells are both sea or both land.
3202: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, share cells, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. The digit on a grey camera indicates the total SUM of the digits in any visited cells that the camera's lens points towards (before a wall is reached, which blocks vision.) A video camera cell itself may not be entered. In this experiment, all of the low digits in the grid (1s, 2s and 3s) must be visited, but none of the high digits (7s, 8s, and 9s) may be visited. The two rats' paths must be perfect reflections of each other across the positive diagonal (marked with a thin pink line).
3203: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits a king's move, as in chess, away must be different. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Purple lines contain a set of distinct consecutive digits in any order. Black dots indicate some places where one digit is double the other, white dots indicate consecutive digits.
3204: Normal sudoku rules apply. Two adjacent digits on a purple line must have consecutive values. Two cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
3205: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide blue lines into segments with the same sum. Different lines may have different sums. An inequality sign points to the lower of the two digits it sits between.
3206: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a pink line must form a non-repeating group of consecutive digits, but they may appear in any order along the line. Using red, green, and blue, colour all circles such that: Orthogonally adjacent circles are different colours; and the digit inside a circle appears that many times in circles of that colour.
3207: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments; each segment along an individual line must have the same sum.
3208: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along each line, the hexagon is referred to as 'position 1', the next cell along is 'position 2' and so on. Digits never repeat along a line. PURPLE LINES are thermos. Digits along thermos always increase as you move away from the hexagon. Eg: 24579 would be a valid thermo. TURQUOISE LINES are index lines. On an index line, the digit in the Nth position indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. Eg: 32154 would be a valid index line. The 3 in the 1st position indicates there is a 1 in the 3rd position, and so on. LIGHT BROWN LINES are hitlines. Digits can be in any order on a hitline, but the digit in the hexagon indicates how many digits along the hitline match their position number. Eg: A hitline might read 27315. The 2 on the hexagon indicates that exactly two digits match their position number; in this case, 3 in the 3rd position and 5 in the 5th position. SHENANIGANS: One of the digits 1-9 (to be determined) is the 'mischief digit.' Every line follows one (AND ONLY ONE) of the three line rules above, but any line containing the mischief digit has been painted the wrong colour. (Any line NOT containing the mischief digit is the correct colour.)
3209: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells along a pink line form a set of consecutive, non-repeating values in any order. A black dot separates two cells where one is double the value of the other. Place Werewolf cells into the grid so that there is exactly one Werewolf cell in each row, column and box; each Werewolf cell must contain the digit that matches its Box number (counted from left-to-right, top-to-bottom); the value of a Werewolf cell is unique from other Werewolf cells and is selected from the remaining digits within its box (e.g. if the digit 1 in Box 1 has a value of 4, the digit 2 in Box 2 could have neither a value of 2 nor 4).
3210: Normal sudoku rules apply. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, share cells, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. BLACKCURRANTS: If two digits are joined by a blackcurrant, one is double the other. REDCURRANTS: If two digits are joined by a redcurrant, one is odd and the other is even. TELEPORTS: Entering a teleport will cause a rat to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, for any path segment connecting two teleports, no other cells along the segment may equal either of the two teleport digits at its ends, or lie numerically between them. Eg: if a path segment joins two teleports with the digits 3 and 6, then the other digits along this path segment may not include a 3, 4, 5 or 6.
3211: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the first X digits, where X is the first seen digit. A and B represent two numbers to be determined by the solver. Any three adjacent digits along a teal modular line have different residues modulo 3 (i.e. one digit from {1,4,7}, one from {2,5,8}, and one from {3,6,9}).
3212: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat on the thin blue main diagonal. Cells that appear in the same relative position of their 3x3 box may not contain the same digit. So, for example, r5c1 (the middle left cell of its 3x3 box) could not contain the same digit as r8c7 (the middle left cell of its 3x3 box.) Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the cage’s top left corner. Digits on a pink line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. The 3x3 box borders divide the thick blue lines into segments; each segment along an individual line must have the same sum.
3213: Place a digit from 1-9 in each cell of the main 7x7 grid. Digits may not repeat in a row, column or 3x3 box of this grid. The grid contains nine 3x3 boxes, which overlap at the dashed lines. Clues in pills refer to the digits missing from the associated row or column, but pills do not need to be filled. Thick purple pills are X-sum clues, i.e. the digits missing from that row or column can form a 2-digit number, which is the sum of the first X digits from the direction of the pill, where X is the first digit seen. The digits missing from a row with a pill containing a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); The digits missing from a row with a pill containing a white dot are consecutive; The digits missing from a column with a pill containing an X sum to 10.
3214: Normal sudoku rules apply. There's a one-cell wide 'river' of orthogonally-connected cells snaking from R9C9 to R1C2 without branching or touching itself orthogonally (but it may touch diagonally). Digits along the 'river' differ by at least 5. All remaining cells are 'land'. 'Bridges' (=) only cross single 'river' cells, and are the sum of the two 'land' cells at each end of the 'bridge' (e.g. if the river cell was a 5, the two land cells could be 2&3 or 1&4). Diagonal 'bridges' only cross 'river' corners. Placing a correct digit will clear fog in its cell, and may also clear fog in other cells.
3215: Normal sudoku rules apply. Any sequence of four cells along the thinner purple lines must contain a run of four consecutive digits in any order without repeats. The thicker red line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Cells separated by an X sum to ten. Cells separated by a V sum to five.
3216: Normal sudoku rules apply. If the digit N appears in any of the four cells adjacent to a circle then it appears exactly N times adjacent to a circle across the grid. The 3x3 box borders divide blue lines into segments; each segment along an individual line has the same sum. Adjacent digits on red lines alternate between odd and even. Adjacent digits on green lines differ by at least 5. Digits on a pink line form a non-repeating consecutive set in any order.
3217: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along a 'double arrow' line is equal to the sum of the digits in the attached circles. Digits do not repeat along the marked diagonals.
3218: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Along a thermometer digits must increase from the bulb end. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order.
3219: Normal sudoku rules apply. Fog will clear when neighboring digits are filled in. Neighboring digits along the grey line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Each letter (except X and V) corresponds to a unique digit. A cell with a letter in it contains its corresponding digit.
3220: SOMEDOKU: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 so that each row N and column N contain exactly N distinct digits, with the rest of the cells in that row / column being repeats. For example, only 3 distinct digits appear in row 3, and any of these can be repeated multiple times in order to fill the row. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz and Phinx must both reach the cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. BLACKCURRANTS: If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. REDCURRANTS: If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. GRAPES: If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. CAGES: Digits may not repeat within a cage. Each cage has the same total, to be deduced. If the digit on a cage's electricity symbol is 5 or higher, the cage may not be entered. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, both rats visit the same number of cells. Any pair of cells (one on each path) that are an equal distance from the cupcake cell sum to the digit on the cupcake cell. Thus, both paths combined form a valid 'zipper' line, with Finkz and Phinx at the ends and the cupcake cell in the middle.
3221: Normal sudoku rules apply. All arrows act as both modular arrows and entropic arrows. A digit on a modular arrow counts how many cells in the indicated direction have the same remainder mod-3 as itself, including itself. A digit on an entropic arrow counts how many cells in the indicated direction are in the same entropic group (123, 456, 789) as itself, including itself.
3222: Normal sudoku rules apply. Lines in the puzzle act as both Zipper lines and Nabner lines. Ie On these lines, digits at equal distance from the lavender central cell must sum to the digit in that central cell. Additionally, along each gold Nabner line, no two digits may be consecutive, and digits do not repeat along the line.
3223: Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin Yang Doublers: Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthoganally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 may be all shaded or all unshaded. A shaded cell has a value equal to twice its digit. An unshaded cell has a value equal to twice its digit minus one (double the digit first, then subtract one). Uniqueness: On each of the constraints below, values do not repeat anywhere in the puzzle. For example, if there is a shaded 5 (value 10) on a renban, shaded 5 can't appear anywhere else on a renban, but unshaded 5 could because it has a value of 9. Renban: Values on a purple line form a set of consecutive numbers with no repeats. Arrows: Values along an arrow sum the value in that arrow's circle. X: Two cells joined by an X have values that sum to 10. Black Dots: Two cells joined by a black dot have values where one is double the other.
3224: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Digits on the slow thermo may not decrease starting at the bulb. Outside clues on the slow thermo must contain a digit, and that digit indicates the length of the first ascending sequence in that direction. For example, a row with 142536 gives a left clue of 2 (1, 4) and a right clue of 1 (6). ie a sequence can be only one cell.
3225: Every gold circle contains a different digit. In any row or column, its circle indicates the number of distinct digits that appears in that row or column. Any of these digits can be repeated any number of times in order to fill the row / column. Eg: one particular row has a circle containing a 3, meaning that row only contains three distinct digits - a valid example would be 173777131. Entering a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is necessary. Along a lavender line, digits that are the same distance from the central spot sum to the digit on that central spot. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. If a red dot sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a black dot sits between two digits, one is double the other.
3227: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column, and 3x3 box). In cages, digits do not repeat and sum to a value that must be deduced. Each cage shares a side with exactly one other cage with the same sum.
3228: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells that are orthogonally adjacent cannot contain consecutive digits. Digits on a grey line read the same forwards and backwards. Correctly placing the first digits in the grid will reveal the hidden cell in the Eye of the Storm.
3229: Normal sudoku rules apply. A pink line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, in any order. A number outside the grid indicates the sum of all the digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that row or column.
3230: Normal sudoku rules apply. A solid pink line contains an unordered set of consecutive digits, without repeats. A hollow green line’s adjacent cells have a minimum difference of 5. A dashed blue line is divided by 3x3 box borders into segments with equal sums. On a black dot, one digit is double the other. On a white dot, the digits are consecutive.
3231: Normal sudoku rules apply. The product of the digits along a hollow orange line is equal to 300. Every set of three sequential digits along a teal modular line contains digits with three different remainders when divided by 3. (I.e. one digit from {1,4,7}, one from {2,5,8}, and one from {3,6,9}). Additionally, the total sum of the modular lines is equal to 300.
3232: Normal sudoku rules apply. Arrows indicate the direction in which the first three digits in that row or column (nearest the arrow) increase or decrease. For instance, r7c1 is less than r7c2 which is less than r7c3. If no arrow appears adjacent to a row or column, the three nearest digits must not be in increasing or decreasing order (that is, the central digit must be the highest or lowest).
3233: For the final preliminary 'free-roam' trial, the nine shortlisted rats were placed in a 9x9 space, and their movements were observed and recorded. Each of the digits 1-9 appeared in each row and column. OBSERVATIONS: Every cell in the grid was visited, exactly once; No rat's path contained any repeated digits; No rat chose to move diagonally at any point; Every 2x2 area was visited by at least 2 rats; No two rats started on the same digit; No two rats ended on the same digit; All blackcurrants and redcurrants were eaten; and No grapes were eaten. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5.
3234: Sudoku: Fill all rows, columns and marked 3x3 boxes with the digits 1-9 without any repeats. Chaos Construction: Divide the grid into 9 additional regions of 9 orthogonally connected cells. Each extra region contains the digits 1-9 without repeats. Circles: A digit in a circle indicates how many cells (including itself) overlap between its 3x3 box and its additional region.
3235: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column and 3x3 box.) Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the number given in its upper left corner. Cells surrounding a white circle must contain at least one copy of the digits within the circle.
3236: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a 1-cell wide loop in the grid, passing through the centres of some orthogonally adjacent cells. The loop does not touch itself, not even diagonally. A digit on the loop indicates how many times that digit appears on the loop. A digit in a cell containing an arrow counts how many loop cells are in the indicated direction (not including the cell with the arrow). Multiple arrows in the same cell count loop cells independent of one another (so if r6c4 is a 3 then there are three loop cells to its north and three loop cells to its north east).

3238: Normal sudoku rules apply. 3239: Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid – no guessing is required. 3240: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along SLOW thermometers, digits either stay the same or they increase as they move away from the bulb. Along green lines, adjacent digits differ by at least 5.

3243: Normal sudoku rules apply. The values of the digits along a line must lie between the two values of the circles at either end of that line.
3244: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments; each segment along an individual line must have the same sum.

3246: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage may not repeat and sum to the two-digit number in the two left-most cells in the top row of that cage.
3247: Normal sudoku rules apply. Nine copycat cells exist in the grid. They all contain the same digit (to be deduced), but they all have a different value. You can use the circles at the bottom to keep track. The value of a copycat cell equals the digit in the cell that is 180° rotationally opposite itself. 3248: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along each length-3 line, the digits ascend from one end of the line to the other. In every 3x3 box, the digits in every horizontal or vertical threesome are never consecutive in some order.
3249: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid gives the sum the digits between the 1 and 9 in that row/column. Cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. 3250: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. 3251: Normal sudoku rules apply. On each line the sum of the odd digits equals the sum of the even digits. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. The digit in the grey square must be even.
3252: Normal sudoku rules apply. Within a cage, digits must not repeat and they sum to the small number in the top left corner.
3253: Normal 6×6 sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the two-digit number shown in the attached pill (read left to right in base 10).
3254: Normal sudoku rules apply. In every row, column, and 3x3 box, one cell has a value of ten. These cells form a complete set of the digits from 1 to 9. The sum of the values in each cage is unique.
3255: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. 3256: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each arrow indicates that the sum of the odd digits must equal the sum of the even digits in the first x cells seen in the direction of the arrow where x is the digit in the cell next to the clue.
3257: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits between the 1 and 6 in that row or column. If two digits are either side of a V, the V ‘points’ to the smaller digit.
3258: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the first X digits in that clues row or column, where X is the digit in the cell next to the clue.
3259: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. 3260: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from the surrounding area.
