3261: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum. Digits in a circle must appear at least once in the surrounding four cells.
3262: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide the blue lines into segments; each segment along an individual line must have the same sum.
3263: Normal sudoku rules apply. Anti-giraffe: cells (1,4) apart cannot contain the same digit. (eg the digit in r1c5 cannot appear in r2c1/r2c9/r5c4/r5c6.) Cells joined by black dots contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other); cells joined by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Along a thermometer, digits increase from the bulb end. The digits in the black cage sum to 12. The blue cages contain the same pair of digits.
3264: Place a digit from 0-8 in each cell such that no digit is repeated in any row, column or 3x3 box. 5x5 Latin Square: The digits in red circles are all from the same set of five of the numbers from 0-8 (which five are to be determined). None of these repeat in any of the diagonal lines of red circles. Each diagonal of the 5x5 latin square can be read as a 5-digit number and the 20 resulting numbers (each line is read from both directions) can be ranked in numerical order. The position in the rank (lowest is 1, highest is 20) of some of the diagonals are given by the blue cages attached to that diagonal. N.B. Two-digit numbers are read from left to right and do not start with 0. There are no tied ranks in this puzzle. The two digits separated by the white dot differ by 1.
3265: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orange lines are both index lines and entropic lines. Index lines: starting with the diamond at position 1, the digit at position N along the line indicates the position of the digit N on the line. Entropic lines: every set of 3 consecutive digits along the line contain one low digit (1,2,3), one medium digit (4,5,6) and one high digit (7,8,9). The arrow points to the smaller of the digits in the cells it occupies.
3266: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits inside a gold cage (which may repeat) equals the sum of the digits in the cells outside which share an edge with cells inside.
3267: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each question mark acts as a stand-in for a digit, which must be deduced for each question mark. Each circle contains 2 digits. The 2 digits must appear in at least one of the four cells surrounding that circle (if a digit repeats in a circle, it must appear twice). Digits along an arrow sum to a two-digit number. This number is a concatenation of BOTH digits in the attached circle. For clarity: A circle with the digits {1, 9} would be surrounded by at least one copy each of the digits 1 and 9 and could have arrows that summed to either 19 or 91. Its arrows could not sum to 11 nor 99, this would require a {1, 1} circle surrounded by two 1s or a {9, 9} circle surrounded by two 9s respectively.)
3268: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a yellow safety strip are in a 2:1 ratio (ie one is double the other.) Extend the 'gap' (ie the grey lines) along cell edges so that it forms a single loop, which cannot touch itself. Even and odd digits may not touch except across the gap. Draw a path from cell centre to cell centre from the blue dot to the red pin, which may move orthogonally or diagonally. It can't cross or touch the gap, except at yellow safety strips. Adjacent digits on the path differ by at least 3.
3269: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits that are in a 1:2 ratio. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Neighboring digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Neighboring digits along an orange line must differ by at least 4. A pink line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. Along a gray thermometer, digits must strictly increase from the bulb end. Each set of three consecutive cells along a peach entropic line must contain one low (123), one medium (456) and one high (789) digit. Box borders divide the blue region sum line into segments with the same sum. The sum of all digits that belong to one constraint type (e.g. all digits on black dots) is the same for each of the eight constraint types in this puzzle and must be deduced by the solver.
3270: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of all continuously diagonally adjacent digits with the same parity, up to (and not including) the first digit with the opposite parity along the indicated diagonal from the direction of the clue (digits may repeat if allowed by other rules).
3271: Normal sudoku rules apply. On lines, the sum of the even digits and the sum of the odd digits are almost equal - that is, they are off by one. Digits may repeat on lines if sudoku allows.
3272: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line contains a square number reading from left to right (or in the case of the line in r3c1, from top to bottom). eg If r8c7 was a 2 then r7c8 must be a 5 (to give the square number 25). (As an aide memoire, all 2-digit squares and 3-digit squares (without zeroes or a repeated digit) are: 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 169, 196, 256, 289, 324, 361, 529, 576, 625, 729, 784, 841, 961).
3273: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. A clue outside the grid gives the digit that must be placed in the Nth position in that row or column, where N is the digit in the cell next to the clue.
3274: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. The grey regions contain the same set of digits in the same arrangement. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 3. Digits on a magenta line form a non-repeating, consecutive set in any order. Digits on a grey thermometer strictly increase from bulb to tip. Digits in a cage do not repeat, and sum to the small number in the top left of the cage. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits either side of a white dot are consecutive. On a black dot one digit is double the other.
3275: Normal sudoku rules apply. Solid pink lines contain an unordered set of consecutive digits, without repeats. Hollow blue lines are divided by 3x3 box borders into segments with sums of equal value. Cells separated by a black dot have one digit double the other. Cells separated by a white dot have consecutive digits.
3276: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage contains a letter. The same letter represents the same pair of digits across the grid. Different letters must represent different pairs. The order of digits within cages does not matter.
3277: Normal sudoku rules apply. No 5 in the grid may be a chess queen's move away from another 5. Every set of 4 adjacent digits on a hollow peach line must contain a digit from each of the X-pair (ten-pair) subsets of {1,9}, {2,8}, {3,7}, and {4,6}. A 5 may not appear on a peach line. A white dot between two digits indicates that those digits are consecutive. A black dot between two digits indicates that one digit is double the other.
3278: The digit in each red cell is greater than each orthogonally adjacent neighbour in a white cell. Each digit in a blue cell is less than each orthogonally adjacent neighbour in a white cell.
3279: Divide the grid into 9 non-overlapping regions, each consisting of orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1–9 exactly once in each row, column, and region. A digit in a circle equals the number of distinct columns occupied by its region. There are 9 circles in total, and exactly one pair of circles share the same digit. A digit in a square equals the number of distinct rows occupied by its region. There are 9 squares in total, and exactly one pair of squares share the same digit. A digit in a diamond equals the number of distinct regions that appear anywhere in its row or column, including its own region (regions seen in both the row and column are still counted once). The sum of every circled and squared digit within a region is the same for each of the nine regions. The grid is covered in fog, placing correct digits clears the fog somewhere in the grid.
3280: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. The sequence of digits along a gray line reads the same in both directions. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive.
3281: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single road that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, and which eventually closes into a loop. The road must pass through every house. Borders marked with traffic lights are controlled intersections that the road cannot cross. The bold 3×3 borders divide the road into segments. Within each segment, all digits must be pairwise prime (that is, any two digits in the same segment share no common factor greater than 1). A digit in a house equals the length of the segment containing it, while a digit in a speed camera counts how many road cells appear in the ENTIRE row of that camera, including the camera cell itself. Note: A segment does not necessarily contain a house. Any segment of length 1 must contain the digit 1.
3282: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Draw a single route that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, which eventually closes into a loop. The loop must pass through every planet. Thick black borders represent black holes that the route cannot cross. A digit in a satellite dish equals the number of loop cells in the 3×3 box centred on that cell. Along the loop, one parity forces the route to turn (making a 90° angle) while the other forces it to continue straight (making a 180° angle), it is up to the solver to determine which parity corresponds to which behaviour. Any two cells that are adjacent along the loop must contain non-consecutive digits unless the loop is passing through a white dot (where consecutive digits may appear).
3283: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Draw a single electricity cable that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, which eventually closes into a loop. The loop must pass through every hut. Water drops mark river borders that the loop cannot cross. Any two cells that are adjacent along the loop must contain non-consecutive digits, unless the loop is passing through a white dot (where consecutive digits may appear). Any two huts directly connected by the loop form a segment (including both huts). A digit in a hut equals the length of the longest segment containing it.
3284: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits a king's move (in chess) apart must be different. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Digits on a purple line do not repeat and are a set of consecutive digits in any order. On a black dot, one digit is double the other. Red cells indicate the position of the cell's column number in that row, e. g. a 4 in r6c3 implies a 3 in r6c4.
3285: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells containing a grey square must contain even digits. Three adjacent cells in any direction (orthogonal or diagonal) never contain three consecutive digits in some order.
3286: Finkz must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Fill the grid with the digits 0-9. Divide the maze floor into pentomino shaped regions (groups of five orthogonally connected cells.) Every cell belongs to exactly one pentomino region. Every thick maze wall sits between two separate regions. All five cells of a region must be filled with the same digit. Regions that touch along an edge (even through a wall) may not contain the same digit, and must not be the same shaped pentomino (rotations and reflections count as the same shape.) Most of the maze is obscured with fog. Correctly filling a pentomino will clear some fog somewhere. No guessing is necessary. A purple probe is a diamond shaped device built into a wall between two neighbouring pentomino regions. The digit on the attached circle indicates the total number of cells visited within those two neighbouring regions. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. If a goldenberry sits between two digits, they are not consecutive (or the same.) A purple arrow sits between two different digits and points towards the smaller digit. Finkz may only pass through a purple arrow in the direction it's pointing. If a floor panel is illuminated with a blue square, it lies on Finkz' path and indicates that a spike in brain activity was detected in response to that digit. Two cells visited adjacently along the path may never sum to a prime number. (Note: 0 and 1 are not prime.)
3287: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must strictly increase from the bulb end. Additionally, the sum of the digits along a thermometer must be divisible by the number of cells the thermometer uses.
3288: Normal sudoku rules apply. Totals of orthogonally adjacent cages differ by at least 7. No two cages have the same total.
3292: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a pink line form a set of consecutive digits in any order. Blue/red lines are thermos, which increase, starting from the bulb. Box borders divide a grey line into segments with the same sum. The digit in a yellow circle is odd. There is a hidden thermo that begins and ends at cells α and Δ (not necessarily in that order). It only moves orthogonally, and may not cross the renban line.
3293: Normal sudoku rules apply. The two puzzles must be solved in tandem. The puzzles overlap at the Loop in R9C9 (so eg. R9C7 in North Side and R1C6 in South Side contain the same digit). All cells with an airplane contain the same digit across both puzzles. Red Line: Parity line (cells alternate in parity). Purple Line: Zipper line (digits an equal distance from the center sum to the digit in the center). Yellow Line: Nabner line (no two digits can be consecutive or identical). Blue Line: Region Sum line (box borders divide the line into segments with an equal sum). Green Line: German Whisper line (adjacent digits differ by 5 or more). Orange Line: Dutch Whisper line (adjacent digits differ by 4 or more). Brown Line: Slow thermo (moving from the bulb, each digit is the same or higher). Pink Line: Renban line (a set of consecutive digits in any order).
3294: Normal sudoku rules apply. The two puzzles must be solved in tandem. The puzzles overlap at the Loop in R9C9 (so eg. R9C7 in North Side and R1C6 in South Side contain the same digit). All cells with an airplane contain the same digit across both puzzles. Red Line: Parity line (cells alternate in parity). Purple Line: Zipper line (digits an equal distance from the center sum to the digit in the center). Yellow Line: Nabner line (no two digits can be consecutive or identical). Blue Line: Region Sum line (box borders divide the line into segments with an equal sum). Green Line: German Whisper line (adjacent digits differ by 5 or more). Orange Line: Dutch Whisper line (adjacent digits differ by 4 or more). Brown Line: Slow thermo (moving from the bulb, each digit is the same or higher). Pink Line: Renban line (a set of consecutive digits in any order).
3295: Normal sudoku rules apply. Several (invisible) killer cages are present in the grid. Digits in a cage cannot repeat, and sum to the clue in the top-left-most cell of the cage (top-most is evaluated first, followed by left-most). Cages cannot overlap. Only the number for each cage is visible, and it is up to the solver to determine the rest of the cells each cage visits. Every cage visits at least two 3x3 boxes and has an equal number of cells in each 3x3 box visited.
3296: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must sum to the small number in the top-left corner of the cage. Adjacent digits along a rose octagon line must differ in value by at least 6.
3297: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along each arrow must sum to the digit in the circled cell. No digit on a golden line can be consecutive with any other digit on that line. A white dot between two cells indicates that the digits are consecutive. Not all such dots are shown.
3298: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a line that occupies N cells, every pair of adjacent digits must have a difference of at least N. If a black dot sits between two digits, one is double the other.
3299: Normal sudoku rules apply. One cell in each row, column and box is a “doubler cell”. Doubler cells have a value equal to twice their digit. Each digit from 1 to 9 appears once in the set of doubler cells. Each grey line can be divided into one or more consecutive, non-overlapping sections each of which contains values summing to ten. Digits in a cage do not repeat. Values in a cage sum to the total in the upper left corner of the cage. Values on a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one value is double the other).
3300: Normal sudoku rules apply. Correctly placed digits clear fog from their own cell and possibly other cells – no guessing is necessary. The sum of the digits inside each cage is equal to the small number in the top left corner, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cage sums are in the left-most cell in the highest row reached by the cage, and all cage sums are given. Purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Lines do not branch or overlap.
3301: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the LAST N digits, where N is the FIRST digit in the indicated row/column.
3302: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. If the digits in a cage sum to N, there are exactly N cages whose digits sum to N.
3303: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits in circles must appear in a cell that touches the circle. Digits on pink lines are consecutive.
3304: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a circle equals the sum of all orthogonally adjacent cells. All circles are given.
3305: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide blue lines into segments. The digits on each segment of the same line must sum to the same total. eg r4c9 + r5c9 + r6c9 = r7c8 + r7c9. Digits in cells joined by a yellow dot are not consecutive.
3306: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in the connected circle. Purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Along orange lines, every set of three adjacent cells contains one low digit (1-3), one middle digit (4-6), and one high digit (7-9). Digits in cells with a shaded circle are odd.
3307: Normal sudoku rules apply. All outside cells on a clue must contain a digit. That digit must also appear in the Nth position looking into the grid in the row/column, where N is the digit in the first position. The sum of the digits in the circles is equal to the sum of the digits on the attached line. Digits are allowed to repeat in the circles and on the lines as normally allowed by other rules.
3308: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits in a Quadruple circle must be placed at least once in the four cells touching that circle.
3309: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with the same sum.
3310: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each digit 1-9 is depicted in this puzzle by a strange symbol. Deduce which symbol stands for which digit, and keep track using the key on the right.This grid contains numerous blob-like alien creatures, each consisting of two horizontally adjacent cells. Some blobs are shown; the others are invisible and must be located. Blobs do not overlap each other. Some blobs are clones of each other, ie: they contain the exact same two digits in the same order. A blob's left-hand digit always indicates exactly how many instances of that blob (including itself) exist in the grid. If there is a circular label in the centre of a blob, its symbol indicates the sum of the blob's two cells.
3311: Normal sudoku rules apply. No digit may appear more than once on a particular clue type. Clue types: 1) Adjacent digits on a green line differ by 5 or more; 2) Purple lines must contain a set of consecutive non-repeating digits in any order; 3) Any sequence of 3 adjacent digits along a teal line must contain a complete set of residuals modulo 3, i.e: one from (1,4,7), one from (2,5,8) and one from (3,6,9); 4) Digits along a red line must alternate between odd and even; 5) Digits may not repeat within a cage; 6) The grey circle contain an odd digit. The grey squares contain even digits. 7) Cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); 8) Cells separated by a white dot must be consecutive.
3312: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orthogonally adjacent cells may not both contain even digits. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in its circle.
3313: Normal sudoku rules apply. Two cells connected by a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits on a magenta line form a set of consecutive, not-repeating digits in any order.
3314: Normal sudoku rules apply. A greater-than symbol points towards the smaller number. Draw two metro lines that travel orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, either with themselves or with each other, which eventually close to form two loops. Thick black walls cannot be crossed by the lines. One loop must lie entirely inside the other, so the outer loop completely surrounds the inner loop. Every station must lie on a loop. All cells on the same loop share the same parity (the two loops may have the same or different parities). A digit in a red sensor equals the number of cells visited by either loop in the 3×3 box centred on that cell. A digit in a station equals the total number of stations containing that digit. The mirror cell has mirrored parity, meaning its parity is considered to be the opposite of its real parity. If a loop passes through it, treat the cell according to this mirrored parity.
3315: Normal sudoku rules apply. The nine marked cells contain the digits 1–9, each exactly once. If a marked cell contains the digit N, then every vertical group of N consecutive cells in its column has remainders 0, 1, ..., N−1, in some order, when its digits are divided by N. Such a group may start anywhere in the column; it does not need to contain the marked cell. For example, if a marked cell contains 4, then every four consecutive cells in its column have remainders 0, 1, 2, 3 modulo 4, in some order.
3316: Normal sudoku rules apply. The cell marked with a blue diamond contains an even digit, while the cell marked with a red diamond contains an odd digit. Two cells marked with yellow squares must contain the same digits; similarly, two cells marked with yellow circles must contain the same digits. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached pink circle. The sum of the digits along the pink line that connects the two pink circles must equal to the sum of two digits in both circles. Within a cage, digits sum to the small number written in the top left of that cage. Along the green line, two adjacent digits have the difference of at least 5. The 3x3 box borders divide the thicker grey line into smaller segments with the same sum of digits along each segment.
3317: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 5 in the grid must have a 1 directly above it, or a 9 directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both. For two adjacent digits along a coloured line, dividing one by the other gives an exact integer (one is a multiple of the other.)
3318: Fill the grid with the digits 2, 5, and 0, such that there are three 2's, three 5's, and three 0's in every row, column, and region. Bulbs are 1, 2, or 3 digit numbers read from left to right and are the product of the digits along the arrow. No leading 10's or hundreds digits can be 0.
3319: Normal sudoku rules apply. Complete each equation in the grid so that the right hand side is exactly one greater or one less than the value of the left hand side, using standard arithmetic operations. Two-cell pills represent two-digit numbers. Adjacent digits along a red line differ by at most 2.
3320: Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin–Yang: shade some cells in the grid so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2×2 region is entirely shaded or entirely unshaded. Every shaded cell containing digit x has value 1/x; every unshaded cell has value equal to its digit. Product/Sum cages: each cage has a corner mark in the leftmost cell of its top row identifying its type. If it shows Σ=X, the values in the cage sum to X; if it shows Π=X, the values in the cage multiply to X (X is not necessarily an integer). Digits or values MAY repeat within a cage. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals their own cell and may also lift fog elsewhere in the grid. No guessing is required.
3321: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along the marked diagonals the differences between neighbouring digits increase from left to right, such that the difference of the first pair is 1, of the second pair 2, of the third pair 3, etc.
3322: Normal sudoku rules apply. Entering enough correct digits in cells will reveal more of the puzzle – no guessing is required. A pair of 2-digit numbers read from left to right are circled. This pair of numbers must add to 90. Each time the fog clears, another pair will appear - each time summing to 90. Digits in a cage must sum to the total given in the cage’s upper left corner. Digits on a purple “Renban” line form a set of consecutive numbers. Any three adjacent digits on a teal “Modular” line must include one digit from each of the sets {147}, {258}, {369}. Any two adjacent cells on a green German Whisper line have a difference of at least 5. Cells separated by a white dot have a difference of 1.
3323: Normal sudoku rules apply. SNAKE: Draw a snake, one cell wide, that starts and ends at two neighbouring cells within the same 3x3 box. The snake only moves orthogonally, and visits every cell in the grid apart from the large grey rock in the central cell. The snake may not enter any cell more than once. INSECTS: The snake must eat every insect, and these divide the snake into segments. Adjacent segments along the snake have consecutive totals. No two segments have the same total. GREY PEBBLES: The snake must not pass directly through any grey pebbles. Digits joined by a grey pebble are either consecutive, or have a 1:2 ratio (so one digit would be double the other). EGGS: One of the four digits surrounding an egg indicates the number of spots on that egg.
3324: Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin Yang: Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is fully shaded or fully unshaded. Shaded cells act as fortress (maximum) cells: shaded cells must be larger than all orthogonal neighbors of the cell that are unshaded. A digit in a cell with an arrow counts the total number of shaded cells seen in the direction of the arrow (not counting the cell itself).
3325: Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally-connected cells. Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 9, once each. Zipper lines: Digits an equal distance from the centre of the purple line must sum to the digit in the centre of that purple line. Different zippers don't share cells with each other. The digit in the centre of a purple line counts how many regions contain at least one cell on that purple line. Some region borders are given. Entering a correct digit clears fog in its cell, and may or may not clear fog in other cells. No guessing is necessary.
3326: Digits (1-9) may not repeat in any row, column, region or cage. Digits on a purple (renban) line must form a non-repeating consecutive set (in any order). A white dot between cells shows they contain consecutive digits, and a black dot between cells indicates that one is double the other - all black dots ON LINES are shown. The 'K' cell may NOT contain a prime factor of 700,000 (2, 5 or 7).
3327: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Tower Fortress: Cells that are part of the gray tower must be greater than all orthogonally adjacent non-tower cells. Note: any cell that the tower even partially covers is considered a fortress cell. Rapunzel's Sausage: The difference between the sums of two linked sausages on a chain must be exactly equal to the number of sausages in that chain. Rapunzel's Face: The digit on Rapunzel's face shows how many numbers of the opposite odd/even parity to itself appear on the whole sausage chain.
3328: Normal sudoku rules apply. Dots divide lines into segments with equal sums. Digits may repeat on lines but not within a segment.
3329: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the order of the runs of contiguous cells that sum to the number in the square and are shaded the color of the clue. There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs of the same color. All runs are given. For many clues, the run’s sum is unknown. If the clue contains a single question mark, the clue is a one-digit number. If the clue contains two question marks, the clue is a two-digit number. There are 13 three-digit emergency or crisis numbers represented by the listed clues. Every clue with a printed numeric value is part of one of these numbers; no unknown clue (? or ??) is part of any number. Each number is formed by reading clue values in order. For example, the number 615 could appear as a 6 followed by a 15. Identifying the actual emergency or crisis numbers is not necessary to solve the puzzle.
3330: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments. Along any individual blue line, all segments have the same sum. Different blue lines may have different sums. If a circled cell on a blue line contains the digit N, then the digit N appears in exactly N segments of that blue line (including the segment containing the circle).
3331: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits a king's move (in chess) apart must be different. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. On thermos digits increase from bulb to the tips.
3332: Normal Sudoku rules apply. A greater than sign points to the smaller number. Draw a single route for the airplane that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, and eventually closing into a loop. The route starts at the airplane, passes through every country, and returns to its starting point. Thick black borders represent heavy turbulence that the airplane cannot cross. If a digit N appears on the route, then the digit N appears exactly N times in cells not on the route. If two countries are directly connected by the route, their digits differ by the length of the segment connecting them. If a country and the airplane are directly connected by the route, the digit in the airplane equals the length of the segment connecting them. Note: Segment lengths include both endpoints. Two objects are directly connected by the route if no other object lies between them along the route.
3333: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single path through the centres of cells. The path may not branch, cross itself, or visit any cell more than once. Segments of the path alternate between diagonal segments, joining two cells that touch at a corner, and vertical segments, joining two vertically adjacent cells. Any four consecutive cells along the path contain digits with four different remainders when divided by 4. Every square lies on the path; every circle lies off the path. If a square contains digit N, then digit N occurs exactly N times on the path. If a circle contains digit N, then digit N occurs exactly N times in cells not on the path.
3334: Normal sudoku rules apply. Using red, green, and blue, colour in all circles such that: Orthogonally adjacent circles are different colours; and the digit inside a circle appears that many times in circles of that colour.
3335: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. The sum of the digits along a double arrow line connecting two circles is equal to the sum of the digits in the circles.
3336: Normal sudoku rules apply. If a black dot sits between two digits, then one is double the other. In row N or column N, a clue outside the grid indicates the sum of all the digits that appear in that row or column before reaching the digit N, reading from the end nearest the clue. (The digit N is not included in the sum.) (Rows are numbered from top to bottom; columns from left to right.)
3337: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow may repeat and sum to the digit in the attached circle.
3338: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a loop, one-cell wide, that moves orthogonally between cells. The loop cannot touch itself, even diagonally: ie If two loop cells are side-by-side, they must be directly connected by the loop; and, if a 2×2 area contains two diagonal loop cells, they must be connected by a third loop cell in that same 2x2. A green circle is on the loop, and its digit indicates the number of cells in its box that are on the loop. A red square is NOT on the loop, and its digit indicates the number of cells in its box that are NOT on the loop. For any two neighbouring cells along the loop, dividing one by the other gives an exact integer (one is a multiple of the other.)
3339: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 so that digits don't repeat in any row, column, or any of the five coloured 3x3 boxes. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a black dot must be in ratio 1:2 (ie one digit is double the other). Not all Xs or dots are necessarily given.
3340: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Each turquoise line is an Index Line, i.e. the digit in the Nth cell along such a line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. For example, if a diamond cell contains a 3, the third cell along that line must have a 1.
3341: Fill the grid so that every row, column, and box contains the digits 1-7, one / mirror and one \ mirror. Each clue shines a beam of light into the grid that travels straight horizontally or vertically and reflects off of mirrors. For example, a beam entering a / mirror from the left would leave going upwards. Clue values give the sum of digits along the beam until it leaves the grid. The ?s may be any digit except 0.
3342: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells separated by a single king's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
3343: Normal sudoku rules apply. Only cells joined by a black dot are in a 2/1 ratio. Digits in a cage sum to the total given. Identical digits cannot appear in cells a chess king's move apart.
3344: Normal sudoku rules apply. Starting from one end of a white line (which end is to be deduced by the solver), the third digit along the line is the sum of the previous two digits and then the following numbers are the sum of their previous two digits. Where the addition results in a number greater than nine, then only the second of the two digits is placed and this number is used for the ongoing additions (eg 52796516 etc). A black dot separates adjacent digits that are in the ratio of 2:1 and a white dot separates adjacent digits that are consecutive.
3345: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on the line have a difference of at least 5, and the digits on the line are the same in both directions. The digit in the grey cell must be larger than those in the cells orthogonally touching it.
3346: Normal sudoku rules apply. The red/yellow lines are a famous tune put into C major using notes of the scale from 1 to 5 (1=c, 2 =d etc). The yellow line is the first line of the tune and the red line is the second line of the tune. On a green line, adjacent digits have a difference of at least 5. A purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order.
3347: Normal sudoku rules apply. Lines are slow thermometer arrows where, in one direction, the digits increase or stay the same from one end to the other; and in the other, the first digit is the sum of the other digits on the line.
3348: Normal sudoku rules apply. On Poison Arrows the digits in the circles are the sum of the digits on their line (including the tip) divided by the digit on their tip.
3349: Normal sudoku rules apply. The small number appropriate to the corner of each cage is the sum of all the digits in that cage including those in the small number itself. All the small numbers are different. On a black dot, one digit is double the other.
3350: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide the blue line into segments. Each segment's total is found by summing the digits on that segment. The segment totals must increase by 1 from one end of the line to the other. Adjacent digits on the line must not be consecutive.
3351: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide the blue line into segments with the same sum. Adjacent digits along the line have a difference of at most 2.
3352: Normal sudoku rules apply. A pair of adjacent digits along a line sum to a square number.
3353: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide a purple line into segments with the same sum. Each segment is also a non-repeating consecutive set of digits in any order.
3354: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide the blue line into segments. The sum of each segment must increase from one end of the line to the other. Any 2 connected segments have no digits in common. On a black dot, one digit is double the other.
3355: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide the line into segments. The sum of each segment must increase from one end of the line to the other. Adjacent digits along each segment (not the whole line) differ by at least 5.
3357: Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column, and 3x3 box). The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments. The digits on each segment of the same line must sum to the same total. (Eg r2c6+r3c6=r4c7+r4c8+r4c9). The digits along each line must sum to a unique number, and the sums of these lines must form a set of consecutive numbers.
3358: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line in the grid represents the path of a different rider. Riders earn 1 point for every odd digit on their path. A digit in a cell with a rider indicates the amount of points earned by that rider. The Red rider (R4C5) doesn't share a cell with its line. Stage Results: The Yellow rider scored more than the Green rider, who scored more than the Red rider, who scored more than the Teal rider. Two cells connected by a Yellow line must have a difference of at least 4. Two cells connected by a Green line must have a difference of at least 5. Adjacent digits along the red line have a different odd/even parity. Any set of three sequential cells along a dashed teal modular line contains one digit from (1,4,7), (2,5,8), and (3,6,9).
3359: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide path through the centers of cells, starting at the rider (R1C9) and ending at the medal (R3C5). The path moves orthogonally between cells. It may not branch or visit any cell more than once. Every set of three consecutive digits along the path must contain a low (1,2,3), a medium (4,5,6), and a high digit (7,8,9). Each mountain cell lies on the path. The path must travel straight vertically through each mountain cell. If the digit in a mountain cell is N, then that mountain is part of a vertical straight section of length N. The sums of the digits above and below the mountain within that section must differ by N. Each flat road cell lies on the path. The path must travel straight horizontally through each flat road cell. If the digit in a flat road cell is N, then that road is part of a horizontal straight section of length N. The sums of the digits to the left and right of the road within that section must differ by N. Each chequered flag lies on the path. The path must turn at each flag, with one straight horizontal stage and one straight vertical stage meeting at the flag. If the digit in a flag cell is N, then both stages have length N, including the flag cell itself. The sums of the non-flag digits in the two stages must differ by N. Soigneur (standing man) cells are not on the path. A digit in a Soigneur cell indicates the number of path cells in the (up to) 8 surrounding cells.
3360: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must not repeat and sum to the number in the top left corner (if given). Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area can be entirely shaded or unshaded. All cages have 1 shaded cell and 1 unshaded cell. The largest digit in a cage is always shaded and the smallest digit is always unshaded. ALL GIVEN DIGITS ARE OF THE SAME SHADING. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.
3361: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a Green line must differ by at least 5. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and must sum to the number in the top left corner if given.
3362: Normal sudoku rules apply. If digits are separated by a white dot, they must be consecutive. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area can be entirely shaded or unshaded. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits strictly between the 1 and 9 in the respective row or column. The full sandwich must be shaded if a sandwich clue is given (i.e. in the case of a sandwich clue of 6 the string of digits 1429 MUST be shaded in that row).
3363: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits given inside a circle appear at least once in the surrounding four cells. Digits along arrows sum to the digit in the arrow's circle.
3364: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. Digits along an arrow must sum to the two-digit total given in the arrow's attached pill (read from left to right). Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area can be either entirely shaded or unshaded. Each arrow total is a two digit number to be read as (X,Y). The X value (tens digit) indicates how many SHADED cells can be seen from that cell in ONLY the HORIZONTAL direction including itself. The Y value (ones digit) indicates how many UNSHADED cells can be seen from the cell in ONLY the VETRICAL direction including itself. (The other shading blocks vision). Cells separated by a Kropki Dot MUST be of opposite shading.
3365: Normal sudoku rules apply. Most of the grid is obscured with fog. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. A digit on a lime green 'minimum line' must be equal to or greater than the number of cells that the line occupies. A digit on a blue 'maximum line' must be equal to or less than the number of cells that the line occupies. Lines do not branch, cross each other, or share cells.
3366: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a grey line have values between the two circled digits at the ends of that line. In addition, the digit in one circle is equal to the sum of the digits on the line AND the digit in the other circle.
3367: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each L-shaped blue line is divided by 3x3 box borders into segments with the same sum. Different lines may have different sums. The digit at the bend of each line equals the number of distinct digits appearing on that line.
3368: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum the digit in the attached circle. The sum of the digits on a line is equal to the sum of the digits in the circles at each end of that line.
3369: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colored lines are disconnected palindromes. Identically colored lines contain the same sequence of digits in the same order. They may be read in any direction.
3370: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into two orthogonally connected regions; one green and one orange. No 2x2 area may be fully within one region. In the green region, the value of a cell equals its digit, as normal. In the orange region, the value of a cell equals its row number plus its column number, regardless of what digit appears in the cell. Values along a thermo strictly increase from bulb to tip. If a black dot sits between two cells, the value of one is double the value of the other.
3371: Fill each cell with a digit from 1-9. Cells sharing an edge can't have the same digit. Each horizontal row and vertical column contains a non-repeating consecutive set of digits (like 23456) in any order. Digits cannot repeat within a region.
3372: Divide the grid into orthogonally connected regions, and place the digits 1-7 once each in every row, column, and region. A digit in a diamond counts how many cells of its own region it "sees" in the row and column combined, including itself. Region borders block vision. A clue outside row or column N gives the sum of all digits up to the cell that contains the digit N (N is not included in the sum). The digits in that sum must belong to the same region and "N" must belong to a different region.
3373: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a circle indicates how many times that digit must appear in circles. Each counting circle is the center of a 3x3 area which contains 9 unique digits. (The circle on the edge of the grid only reaches 6 cells.) Digits separated by an X sum to 10.
3374: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Correctly placed digits may remove fog from other cells. Any constraint type can not have a repeated digit. (E.g. if a 2 appears on a parity line, another 2 may not appear on any parity line.) In addition, digits across a constraint type must make up a consecutive set of digits. (E.g. if a 2 and 4 exist on dutch whisper line(s), there must also be a 3 somewhere on a dutch whisper line.) Constraint types: 1. Arrow - Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the connected circle. Each circle is associated with exactly one arrow; 2. Region Sum (RS) - The 3x3 box borders divide a blue line into segments; each segment along an individual line must have the same sum. Each line crosses at least 1 box border and does not branch; 3. Renban (R) - Purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order; 4. Dutch Whispers (DW) - Adjacent digits along an orange line have a difference of at least 4; 5. Entropic (E) - Any three adjacent digits along a peach line are from one each of low(1,2,3), medium(4,5,6), and high(7,8,9) digits. Entropic lines must be at least 3 cells long; 6. Kropki - Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive; 7. Parity (P) - Along a red line, adjacent digits must alternate between odd and even.
3375: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring digits on the orange line must differ in value by at least 4.
3376: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in its attached circle. Digits along a line sum to the same total as the sum of the digits in its attached circles. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. The cage shows its sum.
3377: Divide the grid into 10 regions, each with 10 orthogonally connected cells. Every cell in a region should contain the same digit. All of the digits 0-9 must appear in the grid. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. If a black dot sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a green dot sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5.
3378: Normal sudoku rules apply. On each line, the sum of either the odd digits or the even digits is exactly half or double the sum of the other parity. Additionally, all end cells of any line contain digits of the same parity (all odd or all even). Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Entering correct digits may lift fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is required.
3379: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2×2 region is entirely shaded or entirely unshaded. The shading must also be centrally symmetric: cells mapped to each other by a 180∘ rotation about the center of the grid have the same shading. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Each cage contains at least one shaded and one unshaded cell, and the sum of its unshaded digits equals the product of its shaded digits (a sum or product consisting of a single digit is simply that digit).
3380: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Draw a path through every cell in the grid, which only moves orthogonally and doesn't visit any cell more than once. The start and end of the path are to be determined. The value of a cell equals its own digit plus the sum of all the digits visited before it. A pink clue in a cell indicates its value. If a black dot sits between two cells, the VALUE of one is double the VALUE of the other. If a white dot sits between two cells, the VALUES of the two cells are consecutive.
3381: Normal sudoku rules apply. In a cage, digits cannot repeat and sum to the total shown. Two orthogonally adjacent digits sum to 10 if there is an X between them, and sum to a value other than 3, 10, 12, or 17 if there is no X between them.
3382: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a yellow dot are non-consecutive. Digits separated by a red dot must contain one even digit and one odd digit. Draw a single cable that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branches, crosses, or overlaps itself, and eventually closes into a loop. The cable must pass through every electricity sign and may not cross rivers (blue borders). 90-degree turns split the loop into segments (including endpoints). If a segment of length N exists, then the total number of segments of length N in the loop is M, where M is greater than 1 and M and N share the same parity. Additionally, if a segment has length N, then the digit N must appear in one of that segment’s endpoints. A digit in a purple sensor counts the number of loop cells in the 3×3 box centered on that sensor, up to a maximum of 9. Cells on the marked diagonals may not be part of any segment of length exactly 5.
3383: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells, which MAY touch itself orthogonally or diagonally, and must visit each box at least once. Two different cells on the loop are called partners if it takes the same amount of steps along the loop to reach each other in both directions. The difference in value between two partner cells is different for each pair of partner cells. Digits in circles must appear in the surrounding four cells at least once. The grey perimeter can be used for making notes.
3384: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column and 3x3 box). Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end.
3385: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Exactly one cell in each row, column, and box is a "doubler", and doubler cells contain a complete set of the digits 1-6. The value of a doubler cell is equal to its digit multiplied by two. Values along thermometers increase from the bulb. Values in cells with a shaded square are even.
3386: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into two galaxies of orthogonally connected cells. No 2x2 area may be completely within one galaxy. Both galaxies must be symmetrical through 180 degrees. A digit in a green circle indicates how many cells in its sudoku box are in its galaxy. A digit in a red square indicates how many cells in its sudoku box are NOT in its galaxy. One of the two galaxies is special. In that galaxy, for any two orthogonally adjacent cells, dividing one digit by the other always gives an exact integer (one is a multiple of the other.)
3387: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits a King's move (as in chess) apart must be different. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. On black dots one digit is double the other and on white dots digits are consecutive. Not all dots are necessarily given.
3388: Divide the grid into nine non-overlapping regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Some borders between the regions are already given. Fill the grid with digits 1–9 so that each row, column, and region contains each digit exactly once. Digits may not repeat within a cage, and no cage is entirely contained within a single region. Region borders divide each cage into pieces with equal sums. That is, in each region containing cells of a cage, those cells form a single orthogonally connected piece, and all pieces of that cage have the same sum (different cages may have different sums). Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all possible dots are necessarily given.
3389: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line differ by at least 5. The digit in a circle is the sum of the digits along the connected arrow.
3390: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat along the blue diagonal. Circle one cell in each row, column, and box. Digits may not repeat in circled cells. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the first X digits in the corresponding direction, where X is the digit placed in the circled cell in that row or column. A question mark may represent any digit from 0 to 9, but for double digit numbers, the first digit may not be 0.
3391: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along the green line differ by five or more. Cells joined by black dots are in the ratio of 1:2 or 1:3. All dots are given.
3392: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages may not repeat and sum to the small number printed in the corner. Digits along arrows sum to the digit in the attached circle. The two cells containing a blue diamond contain the same digit.
3393: Divide the grid into 10 regions, each with 10 orthogonally connected cells. Every cell in a region should contain the same digit. All of the digits 0-9 must appear in the grid. No two digits on a yellow line may be the same or consecutive. The two digits at either end of a lavender line sum to the digit on the central spot.
3394: Normal sudoku rules apply. Place nine circles in the grid: one in each row, column, and 3×3 box, with the digits in the circled cells forming a complete set of 1–9. Digits may not repeat within a cage. If an X is in a row with circled digit A and a column with circled digit B, the digits in the cage containing this X sum to A×B (A and B need not be distinct).
3395: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end.
3396: Place TWO digits from 1-8 in every cell so that each digit appears exactly once in every row, column, and 2x2 box. The smaller digit should go in the upper left, and the larger one in the lower right. A cell can take the value of either of its digits. A number on a diamond is a sum of the cells it separates. A number outside a row a column is a sum of that row or column.
3397: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Along orange lines, every set of three adjacent cells contains one low digit (1,2,3), one middle digit (4,5,6), and one high digit (7,8,9). Digits in cells with a shaded square are even.
3398: Normal sudoku rules apply. Nine unlikely friends must each find a path through their box, to reach something that will give them an energy boost. FEEDING MISSIONS: • BOX 1: The frog must reach the fly resting on a waterlily. • BOX 2: The mad scientist must reach his lettuce. • BOX 3: The digital snake must reach the cake. • BOX 4: The robot must reach the battery. • BOX 5: The dolphin must reach the fish. • BOX 6: The flamingo must reach the pancakes. • BOX 7: The cat must reach the milk. • BOX 8: The zebra must reach the broccoli. • BOX 9: The hippo must reach the doughnut. MOVEMENT: Characters each stay in their own box, but do not necessarily need to visit all 9 cells. They may not pass through any thick walls, visit any cell more than once, or cross their own paths. As well as moving orthogonally, they may also move diagonally if there is a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass through the end of a wall on the corner of a cell. MATCHING PATHS: Every character visits exactly the same sequence of digits, in the same order. ONE WAY DOORS: A purple arrow points towards the smaller of the two digits it sits between, and may only be passed through in the direction it's pointing. EXTRA ITEMS: If two digits are separated by a test tube (in box 2), a metal gear (in box 4), a black sea urchin (in box 5), or a cookie (in box 7), then one digit is double the other. Extra items may or may not be visited.
3399: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must sum to the small clue in the cage's top left corner. The clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits cannot repeat along the main diagonal marked with a blue line. The grey square contains an even digit. Grey lines are palindromes ie they read the same forwards and backwards. Digits separated by a white dot have a difference of one. If two digits are separated by a black dot then one is double the other.
3400: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a large diamond indicates the number of cells it can see in its row and column that are larger than itself, where digits smaller than itself block vision. A small diamond separates two digits whose difference is a multiple of three.
3401: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a pink (renban) line form a non-repeating consecutive set. Digits along an arrow tip sum to the digit in the arrow's bulb. All arrow tips are also renban lines (note this does NOT include the arrow's bulb).
3402: Normal sudoku rules apply. Beige lines are "hit point lines": Counting the diamond as position one, digits in their correct position must sum to the number in the diamond (eg a line who's diamond was the value 9 may be made up 93145 as 4&5 are in the 4th and 5th position and sum to 9 fulfilling the diamonds requirements). Digits may not repeat along a line (the digit in the diamond is considered on the line and may not appear elsewhere along its line). Digits in the diamonds also count how many different lines they appear on, including themselves (eg if a diamond contained the number 3 it would appear, in any position, on two more lines). Digits which don't appear in a diamond have no limitations as to how many lines they appear on.
3403: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move cannot contain the same digit. All lines sum to the same total. Any three adjacent digits along the teal "modular" line have different residues modulo 3 (i.e. one digit from {1,4,7}, one from {2,5,8}, and one from {3,6,9}). Box borders divide the blue "region sum" line into segments with the same sum. Along the pink "renban" line, digits form a consecutive sequence in any order. Along the orange "dutch whisper" line, adjacent digits differ by at least 4. Along the gold "nabner" line, digits do not repeat and no two digits appearing anywhere on the line can be consecutive. Any three adjacent digits along the peach "entropic" line contains one low digit (123), one middle digit (456), and one high digit (789). Along the green "german whisper" line, adjacent digits differ by at least 5. Digits along the red "parity" line must alternate between odd and even.
3404: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along each line sum to the same total as the digits in the two circles at its ends. Digits in cells with grey squares are even.
3405: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum. Digits along each cyan thermometer must increase from the bulb end.
3406: Normal sudoku rules apply. If two digits are joined by a black dot, one is double the other. If two digits are joined by a white dot, they are consecutive. If two digits are joined by an X, they sum to 10. Two lines of the same colour are twins, meaning their digits have the same sum. Adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5. Digits on a pink line form a non-repeating, conseuctive sequence which can be arranged in any order along the line. Box borders divide a blue line into segments, each of which have the same sum. Digits along a grey thermometer must increase as they get further away from the bulb. On a red line, digits must alternate between even and odd. No two digits anywhere on a yellow line may be consecutive.
3407: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a line can never be lower than the length of the line. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. Not all dots are given.
3408: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on an orange line must differ in value by at least 4.
3409: Normal sudoku rules apply. Double Arrows: The sum of the digits along each burgundy line is equal to the sum of the two digits in the connected circles. A digit in a double-arrow circle indicates how many circles in the puzzle contain that digit. Quadruple circles: the digit inside the small white circle appears in one of the four cells surrounding that circle. Digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10.
3410: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into four distinct regions. Each region consists of orthogonally connected cells and touches each of the other three regions orthogonally too (ie shares at least one edge). No 2×2 block may be entirely within one region. At least two regions are the same size. Draw two distinct orthogonally connected, non-branching paths, each joining a pair of hourglasses determined by the solver. The paths share exactly one cell, marked by the red pin, and otherwise do not overlap. Along one path, adjacent digits have opposite parity, along the other, adjacent digits are consecutive. A digit in an hourglass equals the number of times its path crosses the border of the region containing that hourglass. A digit N in a purple Sensor means the digit N appears exactly N times within that sensor’s region. Neither path may pass through a blue dot. Digits in cells joined by a green dot differ by at least 5. Digits in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive. If two digits are joined by a black dot one is TRIPLE the other. Digits in a cage sum to the value in its top-left corner and do not repeat within a cage. A digit in a cell with arrows equals the total number of cells containing any part of either path in all indicated directions, including the clue cell itself. Numbers outside the grid on a diagonal indicate the sum of the first X cells along that diagonal. The value of X is not 6 and must be determined by the solver. A number N outside a row/column means the first N cells from that side are in the same region, and the (N+1)th cell is in a different region. Note: You may finish one part before the others (digits, paths, and regions), but the puzzle is only solved once all three parts are completed.
3411: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single loop that moves orthogonally from cell to cell and never crosses or overlaps itself. A digit in a circle indicates how many of the up to 8 surrounding cells the loop passes through. The loop cannot pass through the circles. Adjacent digits along the loop differ by at least 5.
3412: Normal sudoku rules apply. For each blue line, the 3x3 box borders divide the line into segments of equal sum. The two lines may have different sums. If a digit N appears on either blue line, it appears exactly N times on the two blue lines combined.
3413: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a palindrome line read the same forwards and backwards. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Where two cells are separated by a black dot, the digit in one cell is double the digit in the other; all possible black dots are given.
3414: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is divided into four quadrants. Each quadrant obeys a constraint, and no constraint extends outside of its quadrant. In the NW quadrant (boxes 1, 2, 4, 5), cells separated by a single knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. In the NE quadrant (boxes 2, 3, 5, 6), where two cells are separated by a black dot, the digit in one cell is double the digit in the other; all possible black dots for that quadrant are given.
