Digits in shaded cells count as double their value for the purposes of sums. Digits in unshaded cells count their normal value. Digits cannot repeat in cages (though effective values may repeat, such as a doubled 1 and regular 2). Every cage contains at least one shaded cell and one unshaded cell. In each cage, the sum of values in shaded cells equals the sum of values in unshaded cells.
3485: Normal sudoku rules apply, and all clues are standard. Arrows: the sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in the connected circle, and these digits can repeat if allowed by other rules. Renban lines: purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Quadruple circles: a digit inside a white circle appears in one of the four cells surrounding that circle. Digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10.
3486: Normal sudoku rules apply. Two cells separated by a single king's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
3487: SQUISHDOKU: The grid is divided into nine 3x3 boxes, which overlap on dashed lines. Place a digit from 1-9 in each cell such that there are no repeats in any rows, columns or boxes. #FRIENDSHIPGOALS: Fletcher the Flat-Bellied Flamingo is feeling famished! He only eats food if it has been squished; so help to draw a path for him through the nice, flat pancakes to fatten him up, as he makes his way to bed for a post-pancake nap. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself or pass through any thick, brown crust walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Fletcher may move diagonally — if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so — but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall. TELEPORTS: Entering a red teleport will cause Fletcher to be instantly transported to the other teleport. From there he can continue his journey. The teleports contain the same digit. TRIALS AND TRAILS: In this test of friendship, every segment of Fletcher's path contained entirely within a 3x3 box is an Index Line. These segments may overlap, meaning some cells may be part of multiple Index Lines (For example, r3c1 would be part of a segment in box 1 and part of a segment in box 4). The digit in the Nth cell of an Index Line indicates the position of the digit N on that segment. Positions are counted starting from the first cell visited on the segment. Good luck!
3488: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Use the 7 types of tile shown at the top to tile the whole grid, so that a picture of a single blue loop is formed. The blue loop moves orthogonally between cells. A digit in a circle indicates how many times that cell's tile type appears in the grid. (Tiles may not be rotated.) If a yellow dot sits between two digits, they are non-consecutive digits. The loop may not pass through a yellow dot.
3489: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. 1. Move along the perimeter cells in a clockwise direction. From a cell on the perimeter, you move X steps clockwise where X is the digit in that cell. 2. No matter which perimeter cell you start from, you will return to it at some point following rule 1 for every cell you reach.
3490: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Purple lines contain sets of distinct consecutive digits in any order. On black dots one digit is double the other, on white dots digits are consecutive. An X indicates digits summing to 10.
3491: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
3492: Normal sudoku rules apply. On each line, there is exactly one cell whose value is greater than the sum of any other two cells on that line. Lines can't branch and any two different lines don't share cells with each other. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Entering a correct digit clears fog in its cell, and may or may not clear fog in other cells.
3493: Normal sudoku rules apply. A correct digit placed in a cell clears the fog around it. Sissa's Lines: Each line has a beginning and an end, but neither is marked. Every cell on a line has an associated value. Starting from the beginning of the line, each cell’s value is twice the value of the previous cell. The digit in each cell is the digital root of its value: keep adding the digits of the number until you get a single digit from 1 to 9. Example: A cell with value 32 contains 5 (3 + 2 = 5). The next cell has value 64 and therefore contains 1 (6 + 4 = 10 → 1 + 0 = 1). On each line, exactly one cell matches its value.
3494: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Any set of three adjacent cells along a teal "modular" line must have three different remainders when divided by 3 (ie one digit from the set (1,4,7), one digit from the set (2,5,8) and one digit from the set (3,6,9).
3495: Normal 6×6 sudoku rules apply. Diagonal and arrows: The digits on the marked diagonal are all different. For each row and column, let N be the digit in its cell on the marked diagonal. An outside arrow is present at an end of that row or column if and only if the sum of the first N digits seen from that end is divisible by N (i.e. all such arrows are shown).
3496: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a white dot must have consecutive digits; on a black dot, one digit is double the other. ALL POSSIBLE DOTS ARE GIVEN (a 1:2 combination may have either colour of dot). Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 cluster of cells is entirely shaded or unshaded. Orthogonally adjacent cells which separate shaded and unshaded regions must contain digits that differ by at least 3. Heavy black lines denote separation between shaded and unshaded regions. Cells separated by an X must have digits that sum to 10. For each X, both cells are either in the shaded or unshaded region. Not all X's are shown.
3497: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colour each cage using one of three colours, with the following restrictions: Orthogonally adjacent cages (i.e. cages sharing an edge) must be different colours; digits may not repeat within a cage; and all cages of the same colour must have the same sum.
3498: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9... there's more to it but we'll get there. #FRIENDSHIPGOALS If you give blackcatfitz a cookie... he's going to ask for some milk! Help him reach the milk by finding a path through the maze of sweet treats. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself or pass through any thick caramel walls. As well as moving orthogonally, blackcatfitz may move diagonally — if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so — but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall. SOMEDOKU Fill every row 'n' and column 'n' with exactly 'n' different digits, chosen from the digits 1-9, repeating as necessary. CHAOS CONSTRUCTION Divide the grid into nine (9) regions, each containing nine (9) orthogonally connected cells. Given caramel walls always separate two different regions; however, any isolated, rounded wall pillars may exist wholly within one region. COOKIES The digit in a cookie indicates how many different digits appear in its region. For example, a digit 6 in a cookie indicates that the region includes 6 distinct digits (and therefore 3 repeats). No two cookies contain the same digit. DARK CHOCOLATE CHIPS Cells sharing a dark chocolate chip must belong to the SAME region. Digits separated by a dark chocolate chip have a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other). WHITE CHOCOLATE CHIPS Cells sharing a white chocolate chip must belong to DIFFERENT regions. Digits separated by a white chocolate chip are consecutive. CRANBERRIES Note that blackcatfitz is allergic to cranberries — you must not include them on his path! If a cranberry sits between two digits one will be even and one will be odd. TRIALS AND TRAILS In this test of friendship, blackcatfitz must retrieve each of the nine cookies in numerical order (from 1-9) before returning to enjoy the milk. Good luck!
3499: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along every line (coloured green or mauve) the product of the 3 digits is 72. No three cells in a straight line (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally) can contain three consecutive digits in any order (Eg, so no straight horizontal/vertical/diagonal of three cells could contain a combination of 1, 2, and 3, regardless of how they are arranged).
3500: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single non-intersecting loop that moves orthogonally through the centers of some cells, that passes through every circle clue. The loop must turn on black circles and pass straight through the cells on either side. The loop must go straight through white circles and turn in at least one of the cells on either side. The loop acts as a Dutch Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 4). The digit in each given circle clue counts the total number of loop cells in all straight loop segments coming off of the cell (counting the cells where the loop turns, and counting the clued cell itself once).
3501: Normal sudoku rules apply. All orange blobs have the same sum. Digits joined by a black shape are in a 1:R ratio for some integer number R. The number R is the same if and only if it is the same shape. Digits joined by a white shape have a difference of D for some integer number D. The number D is the same if and only if it is the same shape.
3502: Normal sudoku rules apply. In graves (cages), digits must sum to the total of at least two of the day, month and year of the date on the grave. Digits cannot repeat within graves. Escape the graveyard by carefully plotting an orthogonally connected path between the green and red cells. The path may not cross the highest or lowest digits in a grave.
3503: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every row, column and 3x3 box contains one liar cell, whose real value is different from its digit. Every liar cell contains a different digit from 1-9. Every liar cell has a different value from 1-9. Two cells that are an equal distance from the central spot on a lavender line have values that sum to the value of that central spot. If an X sits between two cells, their values sum to 10. The arrows and circles on the right can be use to keep track.
3504: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in the connected circle. Purple lines contain a set of consecutive digits without repeats in any order. A digits in a shaded square is even.
3505: Divide the grid into nine regions of nine orthogonally connected cells, and fill every cell with a digit from 1-9 so there are no repeats in a row, column, or region. Every 5 in the grid must have a '1' directly above it or a '9' directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both. Along a (slow) thermometer, digits must not decrease moving along a line away from the bulb. Additionally, two cells connected orthogonally by a thermometer must be in the same region. Diagonal connections have no additional restriction.
3506: Fill the grid with digits 1–9 so that each row and each column contains every digit exactly once. Digits also may not repeat within regions. Construct regions made up of orthogonally connected cells such that every region contains exactly one circle. The number of cells in a region must match the number in the region's circle. Each region contains a consecutive set of digits, e.g: {2,3,4},{1},{4,5,6,7,8,9}. The digits do not have to start at 1 and may appear in any order within the region. If a black dot sits between two digits, then one is double the other. The two cells must be within the same region. Not all possible black dots are given. A white dot between two cells indicates the digits are consecutive. The two cells must be within the same region. Not all possible white dots are given. Clues outside the grid, indicated by arrows, show the sum of the digits along the diagonal path of the arrow.
3507: Fill the grid with digits 1–9, so that each digit appears exactly once in every row and column. All cells except those in cages must be grouped into regions consisting of orthogonally connected cells. Each region contains exactly one circle. The number inside the circle gives the number of cells in its region. No digit may repeat within any cage or any region. In addition, no two digits within the same cage or the same region may be consecutive. Allowed examples: {3,1,5}, {1}, {4,2,9,6}. Two cells joined by a white dot contain consecutive digits. If two cells are joined by a blue dot, they belong to different regions. Two cells joined by a V contain digits summing to 5. Not all possible dots or symbols are given. The arrow outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.
3508: Normal 8×8 sudoku rules apply. Each circled cell represents a chess piece on the corresponding square of a chessboard, with White moving up the board. Each piece type and colour is assigned a unique digit (eg all white pawns share one digit and all black pawns another), and not all piece types must appear. All white pieces are globally lower digits than all black pieces ((i.e. the highest white piece is lower than the lowest black piece), and within each colour the digit values follow standard chess hierarchy if they exist: Pawn is less than Knight is less than Bishop is less than Rook is less than Queen is less than King. The chess position is legal, no piece is currently attacking any piece of the opposite colour, regardless of it is defended, and White and Black have identical material (the same number of each piece type). No pawn promotions have occurred. It is White to move, and White has a checkmate in one. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
3509: Normal sudoku rules apply. All cages within the SAME 3×3 box sum to the same value. No two boxes share the same cage sums. A black dot between two cells indicates one digit is double the other.
3510: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a line must lie between the values in the circles at its ends. A digit shown in a circle indicates exactly how many circles in the entire puzzle contain that digit, including circles attached to lines. Cells joined by an inequality symbol must satisfy the indicated inequality, with the symbol pointing toward the smaller digit.
3511: Write the digits from 1 to 6 into the cells of the grid such that no digit repeats in a row, column, or region. The six regions, each consisting of six orthogonally connected cells, have to be determined. Some region boundaries are given and have to be respected. The cells on a purple line contain a set of distinct, (normally, not cyclically) consecutive digits, in any order. For digits 1–6, cyclic consecutive means the next digit in the cycle 1→2→3→4→5→6→1. If two orthogonally adjacent cells are separated by a region boundary, the bottom digit must be cyclic consecutive to the top digit, or the right digit must be cyclic consecutive to the left digit, respectively.
3512: Normal sudoku rules apply. No two orthogonally adjacent digits are consecutive. Black dots separate digits where one is double the other. A digit in a circle indicates how many circles contain that digit.
3513: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in the connected circle. Every set of three adjacent digits along a peach line contains one low digit (123), one middle digit (456), and one high digit (789).
3514: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every row, column and 3x3 box contains one liar cell, whose real value is different from its digit. Every liar cell contains a different digit from 1-9. Every liar cell has a different value from 1-9. One cell on each olive line contains the greatest value on that line, which is greater than the sum of any other pair of values on that line. If a black dot sits between two cells, the value of one is double the value of the other. If an X sits between two cells, their values sum to 10. NOTES: In each green arrow, enter the liar digit for its row, and in the circle to its right, write its real value.
3515: Normal sudoku rules apply. There are sixteen words in the grid, which can be grouped into four groups of four related words. Each cell that contains a word has the same digit as the other three words in its group. Filling in all four words of a group will clear fog to reveal the connection between them.
3517: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells are either land or water. Three sides of the grid are completely water; the fourth has some land. All land cells are orthogonally connected, as are all water cells, and no 2 x 2 area is either all land or all water. Digits within cages do not repeat. The number shown in the cage is the sum of the digits in its land cells minus the sum of digits in its water cells. Digits on a thermometer increase from the bulb end. When a thermometer's cells switch from land to water, or water to land, the value must increase by a minimum of 2.
3518: Normal sudoku rules apply. No two adjacent cells (orthogonally or diagonally) may contain the same digit. No two cells which are a camel's move away from each may contain the same digit. (A camel’s move is 3 cells orthogonally and one cell at right angles - so the digit in r1c4 may not be in r2c1, r4c3, r4c5 or r2c7.) Grey lines are palindromes: cells the same distance from each end contain the same digit.A white dot connects two consecutive digits. A black dot connects two digits in a 1:2 ratio. Not all possible dots are shown.
3519: Normal sudoku rules apply. If the digit N appears in a circle, then exactly N circles contain the digit N. Cages come in three sets: red, green and blue. All cages in the same coloured set have the same total, to be determined for each colour. These three totals are all different. Digits may not repeat within a set of cages of the same colour. For each set of cages, all possible two-cell combinations are used in the grid to reach that set's total. The digits not represented in the red cages, together with those not in the blue cages, and those not in the green cages, do not repeat. They are exactly the same set of digits as those to be found in the circle cells. A white dot between two cells indicates that their digits differ by 1.
3520: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade each cell in the grid using one of two colours, such that all cells with the same colour are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 square of cells is entirely one colour. Black dots between cells indicate that their digits are in a 1:2 ratio. The digits along a red arrow sum to the digit in its circle. The yin-yang colour boundary (when discovered) splits the line into segments, each of which is a separate Thermo line, all running in the same direction. Put another way, digits on this line increase continuously from the bulb, unless the line crosses a colour boundary, in which case the digit after the boundary may be lower than the one before it. All segments are either 3, 4 or 5 cells long.
3521: Divide the grid into 8 regions, each consisting of 8 orthogonally-connected cells. Regions may wrap around the grid's edges, both horizontally and vertically. Each row, column, and region contains the digits 1 to 8 exactly once. Some region boundaries are given and have to be respected. The digits along an arrow sum to the digit in its circle. The digits 1 to 3 are small and the digits 6 to 8 are large. Any two orthogonally adjacent cells separated by a region border must contain one small and one large digit. This includes cells in different regions at opposite edges of the grid, since the grid wraps.
3522: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. Each circle has exactly one arrow, and arrows only move orthogonally (ie north, south, east or west), and don't share cells. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit may or may not clear fog from part of the grid.
